nahhas-irab:75-75.t: (أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ): an imperfect verb with future meaning [Translator's note: the source says "فعل مستقبل", a future verb]. (أَنْ) is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb), i.e. "in that" (في أن). (يُؤْمِنُوا) is accusative by أن, and that is why the nūn has been dropped from it. (وَقَدْ كانَ فَرِيقٌ): al-Khalīl said: قد is for expectation. «فريق» is the noun of كان, and the khabar (predicate) is (يَسْمَعُونَ). It is also possible that the khabar is منهم, with «يسمعون» being a naʿt (adjective) of فريق. The plural of «فريق» for the lower numbers (three to ten) is أفرقة, and for the higher numbers أفرقاء. Sībawayh said: Know that some people of Rabīʿa say «منهم» [Translator's note: i.e. with kasra on the hāʾ, مِنْهِم], making it follow the kasra, since for them the vowelless letter [the nūn] was not a solid barrier.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: the original form of (لَقُوا) is لقيوا; we have mentioned this at the beginning of the sūra. The original form of (خَلا) is خلو: the wāw was changed into an alif because it is vowelled and preceded by a fatḥa. (لِيُحَاجُّوكُمْ) is accusative by the lām of kay (lām of purpose), or, if you like, by an implied (muḍmar) أن; the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn. Yūnus said: some Arabs vocalise the lām of kay with fatḥa. Al-Akhfash said: because fatḥa is the original vowel. Khalaf al-Aḥmar said: it is the dialect of Banū al-ʿAnbar.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t:
(وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ): nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (لا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتابَ) is in the position of the accusative. (إِلَّا أَمانِيَّ) is accusative because it is an exception that is not of the same kind as what precedes it (disjunctive exception); similar to it is ﴿ما لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا اتِّباعَ الظَّنِّ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 157]. Abū Jaʿfar [Translator's note: here the Medinan reader Abū Jaʿfar, not the author] read (إِلَّا أَمانِيَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ) [Translator's note: as printed the word carries a doubled yāʾ; the reading meant is evidently أَمَانِي with a light yāʾ, as the following explanation shows] and said: this is as one says مفاتح as the plural of مفتاح. Abū Jaʿfar said: dropping is more frequent with weak (muʿtall) words, as Dhū al-Rumma said: [al-Ṭawīl] 24-
وهل يرجع التّسليم أو يكشف العما ... ثلاث الأثافي والرّسوم البلاقع
(Can a greeting bring any reply, or can the three hearth-stones and the desolate traces dispel blindness?)
(وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ): mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: (فَوَيْلٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Akhfash said: it may also be accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "May Allah cause woe to cling to him" (ألزمه الله ويلا).

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: (وَقالُوا لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ): Sībawayh related from one of al-Khalīl's companions that the original of لن is «لا أن». Hishām related the same from al-Kisāʾī. Sībawayh held that this is a mistake and that لن governs like أن, adducing as evidence the Arabs' saying زيدا لن أضرب ("Zayd I will not strike"). (قُلْ أَتَّخَذْتُمْ) with assimilation (idghām). ʿĀṣim read (أَتَّخَذْتُمْ) without assimilation [Translator's note: i.e. pronouncing the dhāl clearly, أتخذْتم], because the second letter is treated as if separate, so pronouncing it distinctly (iẓhār) is good.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t:
(بَلى) has the same function as نعم, except that it only occurs after a negation. The Kufans held that it is «بل» with a yāʾ added to it: بل indicates rejection of the denial, and the yāʾ indicates affirmation of what comes after it. They said: if someone said "Did you not take a dinar?" and you answered نعم, the meaning would be "No, I did not take", because you would have confirmed the negation and what follows it; but if you say بلى, the meaning becomes "Yes, I did take." (مَنْ) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and it is conditional.
(فَأُولئِكَ) is a second mubtadaʾ. (أَصْحابُ النَّارِ) is the khabar of the second, and the second together with its khabar is the khabar of the first.

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: (لا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ): we have mentioned this in the book before this one. (وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً): a maṣdar (verbal noun). (وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً) is built on the pattern فُعْل. Al-Akhfash related "وقولوا للناس حسنى" on the pattern فُعْلى. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not permissible in Arabic; nothing of this kind is said except with the article, as in الفضلى, الكبرى and الحسنى. This is the view of Sībawayh. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read "وقولوا للناس حسنا" with two ḍammas [Translator's note: i.e. حُسُنًا], and this is like الحلم [Translator's note: الحُلُم]. The Kufans read حسنا [Translator's note: i.e. حَسَنًا], meaning "a good saying" (قولا حسنا). Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: حسن and حسن are like بخل and بخل [Translator's note: i.e. حُسْن/حَسَن like بُخْل/بَخَل]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: it is unsound in Arabic to say مررت بحسن ("I passed by a good one"), putting the adjective in place of the thing described, because it is not known what you meant. (ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): accusative as an exception; according to Sībawayh the excepted (mustathnā) is accusative because it resembles the object, while Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is truly an object, the meaning being "I excepted a few." (وَأَنْتُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ): mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: (وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَكُمْ): it is permissible to assimilate the qāf into the kāf because they are close to one another. (لا تَسْفِكُونَ) is like (لا تَعْبُدُونَ) [al-Baqara: 83]. Ṭalḥa read (تَسْفُكُونَ) with ḍamma on the fāʾ. (دِماءَكُمْ) is the plural of دم. The original form of دم is فَعْل — this is the clear view — and it has been said that its original form is دمي on the pattern «فَعَل», except that the mīm takes a vowel in the dual when it is restored to its original form, to indicate that it had been the letter carrying the case ending (ḥarf al-iʿrāb) when [the last radical] was dropped.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t:
(ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ): the mīm of «ثم» takes fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; it may not take ḍamma or kasra, as is allowed in «ردّ», because it is not inflected. (أَنْتُمْ) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; a pronoun does not show case endings. You give ḍamma to the tāʾ of أنتم because it had fatḥa when you address one male and kasra when you address one female, so when it became dual and plural only the ḍamma remained. (هؤُلاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): al-Qutabī [Ibn Qutayba] said: the implied form is "O these!" (يا هؤلاء). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is wrong according to Sībawayh's view; he does not allow هذا أقبل (meaning "O this one, come"). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «هؤلاء» means الذين (those who), and تقتلون is part of the ṣila (relative clause), i.e. "then you are those who kill." I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say:
I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: whoever said that «هذا» means «الذي» erred, even though this verse has been recited:
[al-Ṭawīl] 25-
عدس ما لعبّاد عليك إمارة ... نجوت وهذا تحملين طليق
(Go on, ʿAdas! ʿAbbād has no authority over you; you have escaped, and this one you carry is free.)
He said: for that would be the ruin of meanings. Abū al-Ḥasan said: this [هذا] is used in its proper sense, and «طليق» and «تحملين» are also khabars. Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied form may be — and Allah knows best — "I mean these" (أعني هؤلاء), with «تقتلون» the khabar of «أنتم» and «أنفسكم» its object. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh do not allow the object to be attached [as a pronoun] in such a case; they do not allow ضربتني ("I struck me") or ضربتك ("you struck you"). Sībawayh said: they dispensed with it by saying ضربت نفسي ("I struck myself") and ضربت نفسك ("you struck yourself"). Abū al-ʿAbbās said: this was not allowed lest the person addressed be agent and object at one and the same time. (تظّاهرون عليهم): this is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Mecca, assimilating the tāʾ into the ẓāʾ because of their closeness. The Kufans read (تَظاهَرُونَ), dropping the second tāʾ because the first indicates it. Qatāda read تظّهرون. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is far-fetched, and it is not like His saying ﴿يظّهّرون منكم من نسائهم﴾ [al-Mujādila: 2], because the meaning there is that he says to her "You are to me like my mother's back", so the action there is from one person, whereas in His saying تظّاهرون the action can only be from two or more. (وَإِنْ يَأْتُوكُمْ) is conditional, and that is why the nūn has been dropped from it; «تفادوهم» is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (أُسارى) [Translator's note: the context indicates the reading أَسْرى is meant here] on the pattern فَعْلى is the regular form, as you say قتيل/قتلى and جريح/جرحى. Whoever says (أُسارى) likened it to سكران/سكارى; each of the two is likened to the other. Sībawayh said: they said سكران/سكرى only because it is an affliction that befalls the mind. Abū Ḥātim said: أسارى is not permissible [Translator's note: the vocalisation intended is not marked in the source]. Abū Isḥāq said: as one says
سكارى; فَعالى is the original and فُعالى has entered upon it. It is related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: one says أسير/أسراء, like ظريف/ظرفاء. (أُسارى) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ إِخْراجُهُمْ): if you like, you may make the hāʾ vowelless because of the heaviness of the ḍamma, as Imruʾ al-Qays said:
[al-Madīd] 26-
فهو لا ينمي رميّته ... ماله؟ لا عدّ من نفره
(For he — his quarry does not get away wounded; what is wrong with him? May he not be counted among his kin!)
If you like, you may make the hāʾ vowelless because of the heaviness of the ḍamma, and likewise if you bring the fāʾ and the lām [before it]. «وهو» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; هو refers to the matter (pronoun of the matter), and the clause after it is the khabar. If you like, «هو» refers to the expulsion, and إخراجهم is a badal (substitute) from هو. Al-Farrāʾ held that «هو» is a ʿimād (support pronoun), and for the Basrans this is a mistake without meaning, because the ʿimād does not occur at the beginning of speech. (فَما جَزاءُ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ ذلِكَ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): mubtadaʾ and khabar. Al-Ḥasan read "ويوم القيامة تردّون إلى أشدّ العذاب" [Translator's note: i.e. with the second person تُرَدُّون].

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ): two objects. (وَقَفَّيْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ): Hārūn said: the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz is الرُّسُل with two ḍammas, whether in a genitive construct or not, and the dialect of Tamīm is the lightened form (الرُّسْل), whether in a construct or not. Abū ʿAmr took from both dialects together: he would lighten it when it was in construct with a two-letter [pronoun] and use the heavy form when it was in construct with a one-letter [pronoun] or not in construct at all. Ibn Muḥayṣin read وآايدناه [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably وآيَدْناه]. Mujāhid and Ibn Kathīr read (بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ) [Translator's note: their reading is القُدْس with a vowelless dāl; the printed vocalisation does not show this]. (أَفَكُلَّما): an adverbial (ẓarf). (بِما لا تَهْوى أَنْفُسُكُمُ): the hāʾ has been dropped because of the length of the noun [i.e. of the relative clause], i.e. تهواه. (فَفَرِيقاً) is accusative by كذبتم, (وَفَرِيقاً تَقْتُلُونَ).

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: (وَقالُوا قُلُوبُنا غُلْفٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar. It is derived from their saying أغلف, i.e. "there is a covering over our hearts." Similar to it is ﴿وَقالُوا قُلُوبُنا فِي أَكِنَّةٍ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 5], and likewise ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَسْمَعُوا لِهذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 26] and ﴿وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ﴾ [Nūḥ: 7]. It has been allowed that غلف is the plural of غلاف, with the ḍamma dropped because of its heaviness. As for غلف [Translator's note: i.e. غُلُف with two ḍammas], it is the plural of غلاف and nothing else, i.e. "our hearts are vessels for knowledge." It has also been said: i.e. "our hearts are not made clear by anything, like sheaths."

nahhas-irab:89-89.t:
(وَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ كِتابٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ): a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب. Outside the Qur'an it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is accusative in «Āl ʿImrān» [Translator's note: so in the source]. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: the apodosis of لمّا is omitted because the hearer knows it, as He said: ﴿فَإِذا جاءَ وَعْدُ الْآخِرَةِ لِيَسُوؤُا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 7], i.e. "when the promise of the last came, We left you and them to your sins and did not come between you and them." Similar to it is ﴿وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّقُوا ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَما خَلْفَكُمْ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 45], i.e. "when this was said to them, they turned away", indicated by "فإذا هم معرضون". Al-Farrāʾ said: (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ ما عَرَفُوا): it is as though the fāʾ is the apodosis of the first لمّا and of the second, and the first did not need an apodosis.
Sībawayh said: And He, Majestic and Mighty, said: [Translator's note: the entry breaks off here in the source.]

nahhas-irab:90-90.t:
(بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا): it is as though He said "Evil is the thing for which they sold themselves", then said «أن» by way of explanation, as if He were asked: "What is it?" — just as the Arabs say بئسما له, meaning "evil is the thing for him." Al-Kisāʾī said: ما and اشتروا form a single noun in the position of the nominative. Al-Akhfash said: it is like your saying بئس رجلا زيد ("an evil man is Zayd"); the implied form according to him is "evil as a thing is that for which they sold themselves." Similar to it is ﴿إِنْ تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 271], and similar to it is ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 58]. Al-Farrāʾ said: «ما» together with بئس may be like كلّما. Abū Jaʿfar said: the clearest of these views is that of al-Akhfash; parallel to it is what is related from the Arabs: بئسما تزويج ولا مهر ("an evil thing is marriage without a dowry") and دققته دقّا نعمّا ("I pounded it an excellent pounding"). Sībawayh's view is good: he makes «ما» alone a noun because of its vagueness, and the rule for بئس and نعم is that they do not govern a definite noun except one denoting the genus. As for al-Kisāʾī's view, it is rejected on this ground. Al-Farrāʾ's statement that «ما» with بئس is like كلّما is not permissible, because the verb would be left without an agent; «ما» is a restraining (kāffa) particle only with particles, as in إنّما and ربّما.
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: «أن يكفروا» — if you like, «أن» is in the position of the genitive, referred back to the hāʾ in به. Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. they sold themselves for disbelieving in what Allah sent down. Abū Jaʿfar said: one says بَئِس and نَعِم — this is the original — and one says بِئِس and نِعِم by vowel harmony, and one says بِئْس and نِعْم, transferring the vowel of the hamza to the bāʾ [Translator's note: the vowelling of these forms is not marked in the source and is supplied here according to the standard forms]. (بَغْياً): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and in reality it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ) is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "because Allah sends down His favour upon His Prophet."

nahhas-irab:215-215.t: يَسْئَلُونَكَ ماذا يُنْفِقُونَ: if you lighten the hamza, you cast its vowel onto the sīn, giving it a fatḥa, and drop the hamza, so you say: يسلونك. ماذا يُنْفِقُونَ: «ما» is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» is the khabar (predicate); it means الذي (which), and the yāʾ was dropped because of the length of the noun, i.e. "what is it that they spend (ينفقونه)?" [Translator's note: the source says "the yāʾ"; the element omitted in the implied form ينفقونه is the pronoun hāʾ.] Or, if you wish, «ما» is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) by ينفقون, and «ذا» together with «ما» is treated as a single word. قُلْ ما أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ: «ما» is in the position of accusative by أنفقتم, and likewise وما تنفقوا; it is a condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَلِلْوالِدَيْنِ, and likewise وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ.

nahhas-irab:216-216.t: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتالُ: (الْقِتالُ) is the noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَكُمْ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:217-217.t:
يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الْحَرامِ قِتالٍ فِيهِ: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is «عن قتال فيه», and the reading of ʿIkrima is «عن الشهر الحرام قتل فيه» without an alif, and likewise «قل قتل فيه كبير». Al-Aʿraj read «ويسئلونك» with a wāw.

عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الْحَرامِ قِتالٍ فِيهِ: Abū Jaʿfar said: the genitive, according to the Basrans, is as a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). Al-Kisāʾī said: it is genitive by repetition, i.e. "about fighting in it". Al-Farrāʾ said: it is genitive with «عن» intended. Abū ʿUbayda said: it is genitive by proximity (jiwār). Abū Jaʿfar said: it is not permissible to parse anything by proximity in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nor in any speech at all; proximity is only an error, and it occurs only in something anomalous, namely their saying: «هذا جحر ضبّ خرب» (this is the burrow of a lizard, ruined). The proof that it is an error is what the Arabs say in the dual: «هذان جحرا ضبّ خربان». This is only on a par with iqwāʾ (a vowel fault in rhyme), and nothing in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is to be construed on this; it is only in the most eloquent and soundest of usages. Nor is it permissible to imply «عن». The correct view on it is that it is a badal (substitute). Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 48-
فما كان قيس هلكه هلك واحد ... ولكنّه بنيان قوم تهدّما
(Qays's death was not the death of a single man; rather, it was the edifice of a people that collapsed.)

As for «قتال فيه» in the nominative, it is obscure in Arabic. Its meaning is: they ask you about the sacred month: is fighting in it permissible? For his saying «يسألونك» indicates the interrogative, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 49-
أصاح ترى برقا أريك وميضه ... كلمع اليدين في حبي مكلّل
(O companion, do you see lightning whose flash I show you, like the flicking of two hands in a crowned, piled-up cloud?)
The meaning is «أترى برقا» (do you see lightning?); he dropped the interrogative alif because the alif in «أصاح» stands in its place and indicates it, even though it is the vocative particle. And as the poet said: [al-Mutaqārib] 50-
تروح من الحيّ أم تبتكر
(Will you leave the tribe in the evening, or set out early in the morning?)
The meaning is «أتروح»; he dropped the alif because «أم» indicates it.

قُلْ قِتالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَصَدٌّ: mubtadaʾ. عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: genitive by عن. وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ: conjoined to صدّ. وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ: conjoined to سبيل الله. وَإِخْراجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ: conjoined to صدّ, and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is «أكرم عند الله» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Qur'anic text is «أَكْبَرُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ»]. وَالْفِتْنَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ: mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. greater in sin than fighting in the sacred month. It has been said that «المسجد الحرام» is conjoined to «الشهر», i.e. "and they ask you about the Mosque", and so He the Exalted said: "and expelling its people from it is greater in the sight of Allah". This has no valid aspect, because the people were in no doubt about the enormity of what the polytheists had done to the Muslims in expelling them from their homes in Mecca, such that they would need to ask about it, whether that was permitted to them. Moreover, it is a view that departs from the view of the scholars, because they agreed that it was revealed on the occasion of the killing of Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī.

nahhas-irab:218-218.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: (الَّذِينَ) is the noun of إنّ. وَالَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا: conjoined to it. أُولئِكَ يَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of إنّ.

nahhas-irab:219-219.t:
يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِما إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ: this is the reading of the people of the Two Sanctuaries and of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ; the Kufans read «كثير». Their agreement on حُوباً كَبِيراً [al-Nisāʾ: 2] also indicates that «كبيرا» is preferable; just as one says "a small sin" (إثم صغير), so one says "a great (كبير) one". If «كثير» were allowed, one would say "a little sin" (إثم قليل). The Muslims agreed on their expression «كبائر وصغائر» (major and minor sins).

وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ ماذا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلِ الْعَفْوَ: so read the people of the Two Sanctuaries and the people of Kufa; Abū ʿAmr, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «قل العفوُ» in the nominative. Abū Jaʿfar said: if you make «ذا» mean الذي (which), the preferred choice is the nominative and the accusative is permitted; if you make «ما» and «ذا» a single thing, the preferred choice is the accusative and the nominative is permitted. The grammarians cited: «ماذا تعلّمت أنحوا أم شعرا؟» (what did you learn, grammar or poetry?) in the accusative and the nominative, both being good and sound, except that the exegesis of the verse points to the accusative. Ibn ʿAbbās said: [it is] the surplus; and he said: العفو is what is left over beyond [the needs of] your family. So the meaning of this is: they spend the surplus. Al-Ḥasan said: the meaning is: say, spend the surplus. Abū Jaʿfar said: and we have explained [this]. لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ: in this world and the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:220-220.t: قُلْ إِصْلاحٌ لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَإِنْ تُخالِطُوهُمْ فَإِخْوانُكُمْ: a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the implied form is «فهم إخوانكم» (then they are your brothers). Outside the Qur'an «فإخوانكم» is permitted, the implied form being «فتخالطون إخوانكم» (then you mix with your brothers). [Translator's note: the source writes the word unvowelled; the permitted alternative intended is the accusative فإخوانَكم.]

nahhas-irab:221-221.t: وَلا تَنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكاتِ حَتَّى يُؤْمِنَّ: one says نكح ينكح when [a man] has intercourse; this is the original sense, then it came to be used for one who marries. It is also permitted to read «ولا تُنكحوا», i.e. do not give in marriage, with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and «ولا تنكحوا المشركين», i.e. do not give [women] in marriage to them. Everyone who disbelieves in Muhammad ﷺ is a polytheist (mushrik); the Qur'an indicates this, and we will mention it, if Allah wills, in its place. وَلَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise أُولئِكَ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ, and likewise وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُوا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ, and likewise «وَالْمَغْفِرَةُ بِإِذْنِهِ» in the reading of al-Ḥasan [Translator's note: the source prints «وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ» here; the nominative is implied by its being parsed as mubtadaʾ and khabar]; and in the reading of Abū al-ʿĀliya وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ, conjoined to الجنة.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «الم» … The view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh concerning «الم» and what resembles it is that it is not declined because it is in the status of the letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al-tahajjī); they are reproduced as quoted (maḥkiyya), and if they were declined the sense of quotation would be lost and part of a noun would have been declined. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is not declined only because you do not intend to predicate anything of it. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: I do not like al-Khalīl's view on it, because when you say «زاي» this is not the zāy that is in زيد, since you have added to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: this rebuttal does not follow, because you cannot pronounce a single letter without adding to it. Ibn Kaysān said:
«الم» is in the position of the accusative in the sense of "Recite «الم»" or "Upon you is «الم»"; its position may also be nominative in the sense of "This is «الم»", or "it", or "that".
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic:

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
«ذلِكَ»: there are six ways [of parsing] it. It may be in the sense of "this is that Book", so that it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied هذا. It may be in the sense of "«الم» is that", which is the view of al-Farrāʾ, i.e. "the letters of the alphabet are that Book", some of them sufficing for the rest. It may be nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject) with «الْكِتابُ» as its khabar; the Kufans say: we made this nominative by that and that by this. «الكتاب» may be the ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) that stands in place of the naʿt (adjective), with «هُدىً» as the khabar. Or «لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ» may be the khabar; the Kufans say: the resumptive hāʾ is the khabar. The sixth way is that the khabar is «لا ريب فيه», because the meaning of "no doubt" is "true"; on this, the sense is complete at «لا ريب». One says ذلك, and the dialect of Tamīm is ذاك. Neither ذلك nor هذا is declined, because they do not stay fixed to [one] named thing. The Basrans said: the lām in ذلك is for emphasis. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: the lām was brought in ذلك so that it would not be thought that ذا is in construct with the kāf. It is also said: the lām was brought as a substitute for the hamza, and that is why it has kasra. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: the lām was brought to indicate great distance. Abū Isḥāq said: it was given kasra to distinguish it from the lām of the genitive, and the kāf has no grammatical position. The noun, according to the Basrans, is «ذا», and according to al-Farrāʾ the dhāl.
Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said «لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ». «ريب» is accusative because «لا», according to the Basrans, resembles إنّ, so they made it govern the accusative; and «لا» governs only an indefinite noun because it is an answer to an indefinite that carries the meaning of «من»; it is built (mabnī) together with the indefinite noun and the two are made a single thing. Al-Kisāʾī said: the norm with an indefinite noun is that its predicate precedes it, so you say قام رجل; when the predicate came later in the tabriʾa [the lā of generic negation], they used the accusative but did not add tanwīn, because it is a deficient accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: the norm of «لا» is to come in the sense of غير; you say مررت بلا واحد ولا اثنين ("I passed by no-one and no two"). When you use it without the sense of «غير» and ليس, you make [the noun] accusative by it and do not add tanwīn, so that it will not be thought that you have put the adjective in place of the thing qualified. It is also said: it is accusative only because the meaning is "I find no doubt", and when the accusative-governing verb was omitted the tanwīn was omitted. «لا رَيْبٌ فِيهِ» is also permissible, making «لا» in the sense of ليس. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowelling «لا رَيْبَ» here; the nominative with tanwīn is what is meant.]
Sībawayh recited: [Majzūʾ al-Kāmil metre] 3-
من صدّ عن نيرانها ... فأنا ابن قيس لابراح
(Whoever turns away from its fires — I am the son of Qays: there is no leaving [the field].)
«فِيهِ هُدىً»: the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive through في. There are five ways with the hāʾ. The best is «فيهِ هدى»; next is «فِيهُ هُدىً» with ḍamma on the hāʾ and no wāw, which is the reading of al-Zuhrī and Sallām Abū al-Mundhir; next is «فيهي هدى» with the yāʾ pronounced, which is the reading of Ibn Kathīr; «فيهو هدى» with wāw is permissible; and «فِيهِّدىً» with assimilation is permissible. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «فِيهِ هُدىً» for the ḍamma and assimilated forms; the forms are as the words describe.] The original is «فيهو هدى»: the noun is the hāʾ, and the wāw was added according to al-Khalīl because the hāʾ is faint, so it was strengthened by a firm letter far from it [in articulation]. A yāʾ is substituted for it because a yāʾ precedes it, or it is dropped — because of the meeting of wāw and yāʾ according to Sībawayh, and because of the meeting of two quiescent letters according to Abū al-ʿAbbās — and the same with the yāʾ. It is assimilated because two hāʾs meet, but this is not good, because the guttural letters are not a basis for assimilation and two quiescent letters would meet. Sībawayh said:
The wāw was added just as the alif was added in the feminine. In «هدى» there are six ways: it may be in the position of the nominative as the khabar of ذلك; [nominative] by implying a mubtadaʾ; as a khabar after a khabar; and as nominative by being the mubtadaʾ — Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning would be "in it is guidance, and no doubt". These are four ways in the nominative. It may be nominative in a fifth way, namely in apposition to the position of «لا ريب فيه», i.e. "true, guidance". It may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ذلك — the Kufans call this qaṭʿ ("cutting off") — and it may be a ḥāl from الكتاب, and a ḥāl from the hāʾ. Al-Farrāʾ said: some of Banū Asad make الهدى feminine and say هذه هدى حسنة. It is not declined [visibly] because it is maqṣūr (ending in a short alif), and the alif cannot take a vowel.
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: «لِلْمُتَّقِينَ» is genitive through the lām, which is zāʾida (redundant). [Translator's note: so in the source.] The dialect of the people of the Hijaz is فلان مُوتَقٍ [i.e. with wāw]. This is the original. التَّقِيّة is originally الوَقِيّة, from وَقَيْتُ; tāʾ was substituted for the wāw because it is the closest of the augment letters to it. They have done this even where there is no tāʾ [following], as ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān told us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd from al-Māzinī, who said: I asked al-Aṣmaʿī about the poet's words: [al-Rajaz metre] 4-
فإن يكن أمسى البلى تيقوري
(If decay has now become my dignity …)
and I said to him: al-Khalīl said it is fayʿūl from الوقار ("dignity"), with tāʾ substituted for the wāw. He said: this is the view of the elders. The original of للمتّقين is with two light yāʾs [المتّقِيِين]; the kasra was dropped from the first yāʾ because of its heaviness, then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty:

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
«الَّذِينَ» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المتقين. It may also be accusative in the sense of "I mean", and nominative in two ways: as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being «أُولئِكَ عَلى هُدىً مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ», and by implying «هم».
«يُؤْمِنُونَ» is with hamza, because the original of آمن is أأمن; combining two hamzas was disliked, so an alif was substituted for the second. When you say يؤمنون, one of the two hamzas has disappeared, so you pronounce the hamza according to the original; if you lighten it, you say يُومنون without hamza. يؤمنون is like يكرمون, whose original is يُؤَكْرِمون, because the norm is that the imperfect exceeds the past by one letter; but the augment was dropped from it because the ḍamma indicates it, and if you brought it in its original form the hamzas would come together. The latent pronoun in يؤمنون refers back to الذين. Hudhayl say الّذون in the position of the nominative, and some of the Arabs say الذي for the plural, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 5-
أو إنّ الّذي حانت بفلج دماؤهم ... هم القوم كلّ القوم يا أمّ خالد
(Those whose blood was shed at Falj — they are the true men, all the men, O Umm Khālid.)
«بِالْغَيْبِ» is genitive through the bāʾ, which is zāʾida (redundant) [Translator's note: so in the source]; the bāʾ is connected to يؤمنون. «وَيُقِيمُونَ» is conjoined to يؤمنون; the original is يُقْوِمون — a kasra was shifted onto the qāf and [the wāw] turned into a yāʾ. «الصَّلاةَ» is accusative by يقيمون; its plural is صلوات, and [it is also said] صلاءة and صلاوة.
«وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ»: «ما» is in the position of the genitive through من; it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) and needs no resumptive pronoun. It may also be in the sense of الذي, with the resumptive pronoun omitted. The nūn and alif are nominative by the verb, and the hāʾ and mīm are accusative by it. من is connected to ينفقون, i.e. "and they spend out of what We have provided them".

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
«وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ» is conjoined to the first الذين. «بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ»: «ما» is genitive through the bāʾ, and the pronoun in أنزل refers back to «ما»; it is the noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. The kāf is genitive through إلى. The original is إلاك; yāʾ was substituted for the alif to distinguish between the alifs of fully declinable words and those of words that are not fully declinable and which must be in construct. Al-Kisāʾī allowed dropping the hamza and reading «وما أنزلّيك», and compared it with His saying «لكِنَّا هُوَ اللَّهُ رَبِّي» [al-Kahf: 38]. Ibn Kaysān said: it is not like it, because the nūn of لكن is quiescent while the lām of أنزل has a vowel.
«وَما أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ» is conjoined. «قَبْلِكَ» is genitive through من, and the kāf is genitive by قبل being put in construct with it. «وَبِالْآخِرَةِ» is genitive through the bāʾ, and the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يوقنون. «هُمْ» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يُوقِنُونَ» is an imperfect verb in the position of the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
«أُولئِكَ» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is «عَلى هُدىً». The people of Najd say أُلّاك, and some of them say ألا لك. «(هدى)» is genitive through على. «مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ» is genitive through من, and the hāʾ and mīm are genitive by the iḍāfa (genitive construct). It may be asked: how is it that the people of Kufa read «(عليهُم)» but did not read «من ربّهُم» nor «فيهُم»?
The answer is that in «عليهم» the yāʾ is changed from an alif, the original being علاهم. [The poet] said: [al-Rajaz metre] 6-
طارت علاهنّ فطر علاها
(She flew above them, so fly above her.)
So the hāʾ was left with its ḍamma; this is not the case in «فيهم» nor «من ربّهم».
«وَأُولئِكَ» is nominative as mubtadaʾ; «هُمُ» is a second mubtadaʾ; «الْمُفْلِحُونَ» is the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first. «هم» may also be an addition, which the Basrans call a fāṣila ("separator") and the Kufans call an ʿimād ("support"), with «الْمُفْلِحُونَ» the khabar of أولئك.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ»: «الَّذِينَ» is accusative through إنّ. إنّ governs because it resembles the verb in [taking] pronouns, two nouns come after it, and it carries the meaning of affirmation. «كَفَرُوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», and the latent pronoun refers back to الذين. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: «سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); «أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إنّ», i.e. they feigned stupidity until warning was of no avail with them. The implied sense is: "the warning and its omission are equal to them", i.e. "these two are equal to them"; the interrogative was brought because of the equalisation (taswiya). Ibn Kaysān said: سواء may be the khabar of إنّ, with what follows it standing in place of the fāʿil (agent); and the khabar of إنّ may be «لا يؤمنون», i.e. "those who disbelieve do not believe".
«أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ»: there are eight ways in it. The best according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is to lighten the second hamza and fully pronounce the first; this is the dialect of Quraysh, Saʿd ibn Bakr and Kināna, and it is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and al-Aʿmash: «أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ». Ibn Kaysān said: it is reported from Ibn Muḥayṣin that he read with the first hamza dropped: «سواء عليهم أنذرتهم»; he dropped it because of the meeting of the two hamzas, or, if you wish, you may say: because «أم» indicates the interrogative, as [the poet] said: [al-Mutaqārib metre] 7-
تروح من الحيّ أم تبتكر ... وماذا يضرّك لو تنتظر
(Will you leave the tribe in the evening, or set out at dawn? What harm would it do you if you waited?)
It is reported from Ibn Abī Isḥāq that he read «أَاأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ»: he pronounced both hamzas fully and inserted an alif between them so as not to combine them. Abū Ḥātim said: it is also permissible to insert an alif between them and lighten the second; Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ often do that. Ḥamza, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read with both hamzas fully pronounced: «أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ», and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. That is far-fetched according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; [Sībawayh] likens its heaviness to ضننوا. Sībawayh said: the hamza is far in its point of articulation; it is a stress (nabra) that comes out of the chest with effort, and it is the furthest of the letters in articulation, so it is heavy, because it is like retching.
These are five ways. The sixth was stated by al-Akhfash, who said: it is permissible to lighten the first of the two hamzas; but this is poor, because they lighten only after the heaviness has arisen and after the one [hamza] has been reached. Abū Ḥātim said: it is permissible to lighten both hamzas together. These are seven ways. The eighth is permissible outside the Qur'an, because it contradicts the written text (al-sawād). Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: hāʾ is substituted for the hamza, so you say «هانذرتهم», as one says إيّاك and هيّاك. Al-Akhfash said, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, «هأنتم»: it is only أأنتم.
The tāʾ in «أأنذرتهم» is in the position of the nominative; you gave it fatḥa to distinguish between the [masculine] addressee and the speaker [Translator's note: the source has «المخاطب والمخاطب», "the addressee and the addressee", evidently for المخاطِب/المتكلّم or the feminine addressee; translated by the evident sense]. The hāʾ and mīm are accusative because the verb falls upon them. [Translator's note: the source has «نصحب», a misprint for «نصب».] «أم لم تنذرهم» is jussive through لم; the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the ḍamma from the rāʾ; the hāʾ and mīm are also accusative. «لا يُؤْمِنُونَ» is an imperfect verb, and the لا has no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
«خَتَمَ اللَّهُ»: «خَتَمَ» is a past verb, and the name of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is nominative by the verb. «عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ» is genitive through على, and the hāʾ and mīm are genitive by the iḍāfa (genitive construct). «وَعَلى سَمْعِهِمْ» is the same. Why did He not say "and on their hearings (أسماعهم)", when He said «على قلوبهم»? There are three answers: one is that السمع is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and so was not put in the plural; it is also said that it is a singular standing for the plural; and it is said the implied sense is "and on the place of their hearing".
«وَعَلى أَبْصارِهِمْ غِشاوَةٌ»: [غشاوة] is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and according to the Kufans by the "ṣifa" [the preposition]. Al-Mufaḍḍal related from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdala «وَعَلى أَبْصارِهِمْ غِشاوَةً» in the accusative, implying "and He placed". Al-Ḥasan read «غُشاوة» with ḍamma on the ghayn [Translator's note: the source says «بضم العين», "ʿayn", evidently for the ghayn], and Abū Ḥaywa read «غَشاوة» with fatḥa. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowelling for these variants.] Abū Jaʿfar said: the best of them is «غِشاوَةٌ» with kasra on the ghayn; thus the Arabs use [this pattern] for everything that envelops a thing, like عِمامة and قِلادة. It is reported from al-Aʿmash: «غَشْوة», taking it back to the basic maṣdar. Ibn Kaysān said — and he is the grammarian; whenever we say "Ibn Kaysān said" it is he we mean —: غِشْوة and غُشْوة are permissible. If you make the plural of غشاوة, dropping the hāʾ, you say غشاء; and al-Farrāʾ reported غشاوى, like أداوى.
«وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ»: [عذاب] is nominative as mubtadaʾ; «عَظِيمٌ» is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
«وَمِنَ النَّاسِ» is genitive through من. The nūn was given fatḥa — whereas you say مِنِ الناس [Translator's note: the source prints «من الناس» without vowels; the contrast intended is with kasra] — because before the nūn in «من» there is a kasra, so they moved it with the lightest of vowels in most places, and went back to the original in nouns that have a connecting alif. In each of the two, what is permitted in the other is permitted. «الناس» is a noun that gathers إنسان and إنسانة; its original according to Sībawayh is أُناس. Al-Farrāʾ said: the original is الأُناس; the hamza was lightened, then the lām was assimilated into the nūn. Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialectal forms, neither of which has more right than the other; this is shown by the fact that the Arabs make the diminutive of ناس نُوَيْس, and if that [أناس] were the original they would say أُنَيْس.
«وَما هُمْ» is according to the meaning. «هم» is the noun (ism) of «ما» in the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and a mubtadaʾ (subject) in the dialect of Banū Tamīm. «بِمُؤْمِنِينَ» is genitive through the bāʾ, which is for emphasis (tawkīd) according to the Basrans, and according to the Kufans an answer to someone who says إنّ زيدا لمنطلق ("Zayd is indeed leaving").

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: «يُخادِعُونَ» is an imperfect verb, and likewise «وَما يَخْدَعُونَ»; they have no grammatical position. «إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «وَما يَشْعُرُونَ» is like the first.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: «فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ»: [مرض] is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). «فَزادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضاً»: two objects. Some of the people of the Hijaz pronounce «فزادهم» with imāla (inclining the vowel), to show that it is from زِدْتُ. «وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ»: the plural of «أليم» is إلام and أُلَماء, like كريم and كُرَماء; one also says آلام, like أشراف. «بِما كانُوا»: «ما» is genitive through the bāʾ. «يَكْذِبُونَ» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان.

nahhas-irab:222-223.t:
وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْمَحِيضِ: محيض is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like جاء مجيئا and قال مقيلا. قُلْ هُوَ أَذىً: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); أذى is from the verbs with final yāʾ. One says: أذيت به أذى, and أذاني, and هما آذياني. وَلا تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ حَتَّى يَطْهُرْنَ: the nūn was not dropped for the accusative because it is the sign of the feminine [plural], and we have mentioned this. فَإِذا تَطَهَّرْنَ فَأْتُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ: «حيث» in Arabic is for place, so some interpreted this according to what Arabic requires, that it is a specific place, namely the private part. Others said: that place has been made clear by His saying: فَأْتُوا حَرْثَكُمْ أَنَّى شِئْتُمْ, so "however you wish" is what He commanded. As for the saying of Mujāhid, "from where they were forbidden [to approach] during their menstruation", it indicates that he made the command and the prohibition one thing, and this is rejected. «أنّى» is an adverb (ẓarf), and its real sense is "from wherever you wish"; it has also been said: "however you wish". وَقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ: i.e. obedience, then the object was omitted. وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ مُلاقُوهُ: the nūn was dropped for the iḍāfa (genitive construct) because it has a future meaning.
Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say while delivering a sermon: «إنّكم ملاقو الله حفاة عراة مشاة غرلا» ("You will meet Allah barefoot, naked, on foot and uncircumcised"). Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ مُلاقُوهُ.

nahhas-irab:224-224.t: وَلا تَجْعَلُوا اللَّهَ عُرْضَةً لِأَيْمانِكُمْ: a prohibition. Ibn ʿAbbās said: [it is that] one swears not to keep ties with his relative. أَنْ تَبَرُّوا: in the position of accusative (manṣūb); or, if you wish, in the position of genitive (majrūr); or, if you wish, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ). The accusative is on three implied readings, among them: «في أن تبرّوا» (in that you be righteous), then «في» was omitted and the verb became transitive; among them: «كراهة أن تبرّوا» (out of dislike that you be righteous), then [كراهة] is omitted; and among them: «لئلا تبرّوا» (so that you not be righteous). The genitive is from one direction only, according to the view of al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī: it is «في أن تبرّوا», with «في» implied and causing the genitive. The nominative is as mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, the implied form being: «أن تبرّوا وتتقوا وتصلحوا بين الناس أولى» or «أمثل» (that you be righteous, fear [Allah] and make peace between people is more fitting / better), like طاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ [Muḥammad: 21].

nahhas-irab:225-225.t: لا يُؤاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمانِكُمْ: one says لغا يلغوا or يلغى, لغوا, and لغي يلغى لغى, when someone says what is not needed in speech, or what has no good in it, or that whose sin is not counted [Translator's note: the source reads «بما لا يلغى إثمه», literally "whose sin is not cancelled"; translated as written].

nahhas-irab:226-226.t: لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ: i.e. they swear; the maṣdar (verbal noun) is إيلاء, أليّة, ألوة and إلوة. تَرَبُّصُ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the ṣifa [Translator's note: i.e. by the preceding prepositional phrase لِلَّذِينَ, which the Kufans call ṣifa]. أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ: the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] was kept because it is a number for a masculine [noun], and we have mentioned its reason.

nahhas-irab:228-228.t:
وَالْمُطَلَّقاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ ثَلاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ: the hāʾ was kept here too because it is a number for a masculine [noun]; the singular is قرء. The implied form according to Sībawayh is «ثلاثة أقراء من قروء» (three aqrāʾ out of qurūʾ), because قروء is for a large number in his view. Some claimed that since «ثلاثة قروء» has the hāʾ, the hāʾ indicates that they are periods of purity and not menstruations; he said: had they been menstruations it would have been «ثلاث قروء» [Translator's note: the source prints «ثلاثة قروء» here; the argument requires the form without hāʾ, ثلاث]. This view is a gross error, because one thing may have two names, one masculine and one feminine, such as دار and منزل (house, dwelling), and this is clear and frequent. Allah the Exalted has said: وَلا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَنْ يَكْتُمْنَ ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ فِي أَرْحامِهِنَّ; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: it means menstruation, and this is among the soundest of views, and thus is the speech of the Arabs. The implied form is: "and divorced women shall wait by themselves three qurūʾ, and it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs of the qurūʾ", i.e. of menstruation. It is impossible that purity be meant here, because what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, creates in their wombs is only menstruation and the child, and the child has not been mentioned here, so it must be menstruation. Among the proofs that the qurʾ in the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, ثَلاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ is the menstruation is His saying, the Exalted: فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ [al-Ṭalāq: 1], while divorce is [pronounced] during purity. His saying, Majestic and Mighty, «لعدّتهنّ» cannot but mean before their waiting period, or after it, or with it; it is impossible that it be with it or after it. Since it must be before it, and the whole period of purity is a time for divorce, [the waiting period] must come after it, and after it there is nothing but menstruation. The implied form in Arabic is «ليعتددن» (so that they begin their waiting period).
وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). بعولة is the plural of بعل, and the hāʾ is for the feminine of the group.

nahhas-irab:229-229.t: الطَّلاقُ مَرَّتانِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the implied form is: the number of divorces with which taking back is possessed is two. فَإِمْساكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ: mubtadaʾ, with the khabar omitted, i.e. «فعليكم إمساك بمعروف» (then it is upon you to retain [them] honourably). Outside the Qur'an «فإمساكا» is permitted, as a maṣdar (verbal noun). وَلا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَأْخُذُوا مِمَّا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْئاً: «أن» is in the position of nominative by يحل. إِلَّا أَنْ يَخافا أَلَّا يُقِيما حُدُودَ اللَّهِ: Abū Jaʿfar Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and Ḥamza read «إلا أن يُخافا» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He said: because of His saying «فإن خفتم», He attributed the fear to others than them and did not say «فإن خافا»; and in this is an argument for whoever assigns khulʿ (divorce at the wife's request for compensation) to the ruler. Abū Jaʿfar said: I reject this choice of Abū ʿUbayd's, and I know of nothing in his choices more far-fetched than this word, because neither the grammar, nor the wording, nor the meaning requires what he chose. As for the grammar, he argues for it by the fact that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read «إلّا أن تخافوا ألا يقيما حدود الله»; in Arabic, when this is turned into the form whose agent is not named, one says «إلّا أن يُخاف أن لا يقيما حدود الله» [Translator's note: the source prints «أن لا يقيم», singular]. As for the wording: if it follows the wording of «يخافا», one must say «فإن خيف»; and if it follows the wording of «فإن خفتم», one must say «إلّا أن تخافوا». As for the meaning: it is far-fetched to say "it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you gave them unless others than you fear", and He the Exalted did not say "then there is no blame on you to take from her a ransom for him", so that khulʿ would belong to the ruler. It is soundly established from ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and Ibn ʿUmar that they permitted khulʿ without the ruler. Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad said: إِلَّا أَنْ يَخافا أَلَّا يُقِيما حُدُودَ اللَّهِ means what is required of them both in living together and companionship. As for «فإن خفتم» with «إلا أن يخافا» before it, this is an address of the Law, and it is among the subtle features of the speech of the Arabs, i.e. "if you are such-and-such, then if you fear". Its parallel is فَلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ أَنْ يَنْكِحْنَ أَزْواجَهُنَّ [al-Baqara: 232], because the guardian prevents someone else; and its parallel is وَالَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ [al-Mujādila: 3]. أَنْ يَخافا is in the position of accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first [i.e. a disjunctive exception]. «ألا يقيما» is in the position of accusative, i.e. «من أن لا يقيما», «بأن لا يقيما» and «على أن لا»; when the particle was omitted the verb became transitive. The saying of whoever said that «يخافا» means «يوقنا» (be certain) is not recognised; rather, recalcitrance (nushūz) occurs and then fear of [it going] further arises. أَلَّا يُقِيما حُدُودَ اللَّهِ: most scholars and people of reasoning hold that this applies to the woman specifically, because she is the one who does not uphold the limits of Allah in her recalcitrance. This is well known in the speech of the Arabs and clear to reason: if a man and a woman were together and the man prayed and the woman did not, you would say «ما صلّيا» (the two did not pray); this happens only in negation specifically. فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيما حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِما فِيمَا افْتَدَتْ بِهِ: it is said: the blame would only be on the husband, so how did He say "on them both"? The answer is that it might have been forbidden to them both that she ransom herself from him, so He permitted that to her and made known that there is no sin upon both of them together. Al-Farrāʾ said: it may be that «فلا جناح عليهما» is for the husband alone, like يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ [al-Raḥmān: 22]. وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ: in the position of jussive (majzūm) by the condition, which is why the alif was dropped from it; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ.

nahhas-irab:230-230.t: فَإِنْ طَلَّقَها: i.e. if he divorces her the third time. فَلا تَحِلُّ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدُ: i.e. after the third. حَتَّى تَنْكِحَ زَوْجاً غَيْرَهُ: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made clear that nikāḥ here is intercourse, and that is likewise its original sense in the language.

nahhas-irab:231-231.t: وَإِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ: «إذا» has the sense of a condition, which is why it needs an apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the apodosis is فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ. وَلا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِراراً: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of harming. لِتَعْتَدُوا: accusative with «أن» implied. وَلا تَتَّخِذُوا آياتِ اللَّهِ هُزُواً: two objects.

nahhas-irab:232-232.t: ذلِكَ يُوعَظُ بِهِ: He did not say «ذلكم» because it is construed on the meaning of the whole group; had it been «ذلكم» it would have been like ذلِكُمْ أَزْكى لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ.

nahhas-irab:91-91.t:
(وَراءَهُ): an adverbial (ẓarf). (وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (مُصَدِّقاً) is an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial) according to Sībawayh.
(لِما مَعَهُمْ): «ما» is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and معهم is its ṣila (relative clause); معهم is accusative by [the implied notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār), and whoever makes [its ʿayn] vowelless treats it as a particle. (قُلْ فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْبِياءَ اللَّهِ): the original is فلما, with «ما» in the position of the genitive by the lām; the alif has been dropped to distinguish the interrogative from the declarative. One should not pause on it, because if one pauses on it without a hāʾ it is a solecism (laḥn), and if one pauses on it with a hāʾ [i.e. لِمَهْ], something is added that belongs to the irregular readings.

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: (وَأُشْرِبُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْعِجْلَ): you give the mīm a ḍamma because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, since its original vowel is ḍamma; if you like, you may give it kasra according to the basic rule for the meeting of two vowelless letters. It is like ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82], and the meaning is: "the love of the calf was made to soak into their hearts."

nahhas-irab:94-94.t:
(قُلْ إِنْ كانَتْ لَكُمُ): conditional. (الدَّارُ) is the noun of كانت, and (الْآخِرَةُ) is its naʿt (adjective).
(خالِصَةً) is the khabar (predicate) of كانت; if you like, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and then (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) is in the position of the khabar. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read [Translator's note: the source does not state his reading here; something appears to be missing]. (فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ): the wāw takes kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned this at His saying ﴿اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلالَةَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 16].

nahhas-irab:95-95.t:
(وَلَنْ يَتَمَنَّوْهُ) is accusative by لن, and that is why the nūn has been dropped from it. (أَبَداً) is an adverbial of time, spanning from the length of life until death. (بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ): if you make «ما» mean الذي (that which), the implied form is قدّمته ("what they sent forward"); if you make it a maṣdar (verbal noun), you need no resumptive pronoun. (أَيْدِيهِمْ) is in the position of the nominative; the ḍamma has been dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness together with the kasra. Sībawayh allowed giving it ḍamma or kasra in poetry, and he recited, by Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt:
[al-Munsariḥ] 27-
لا بارك الله في الغوانيّ هل ... يصبحن إلّا لهنّ مطّلب
(May Allah not bless the fair women! Do they ever wake without someone seeking them?)
If it is in the position of the accusative, you give it a vowel, because the accusative is light; and it may be made vowelless in poetry. (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ): mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:96-96.t:
(وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ): two objects. (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا) is by omission, i.e. "and more eager than [those who associate]", so that a noun is conjoined to a noun. In Arabic it is permissible [to read] (مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ) in the sense of "among those who associate there are people one of whom would love", except that the meaning in the verse does not bear this, even though it is permissible in Arabic. [Translator's note: the source has "أدغمت" here, repeated in the next sentence.] The original of يودّ is يودد; it was assimilated so that two identical letters with vowels would not come together, and the vowel of the dāl was transferred to the wāw to indicate that it is [on the pattern] يَفْعَل. Al-Kisāʾī related:
وددت with fatḥa [Translator's note: i.e. وَدَدْتُ], so on this basis «يودّ» with kasra on the wāw is permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned (وَما هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ الْعَذابِ أَنْ يُعَمَّرَ) in the book before this one. (وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ), i.e. of what these people do, one of whom would love to be given a life of a thousand years. Whoever reads بما تعملون, the implied form for him is: "Say to them, O Muḥammad: Allah sees what you do."

nahhas-irab:97-97.t: (قُلْ مَنْ كانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ): the Arabs have five dialectal forms of it. The dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz: جبريل; the dialect of Tamīm and Qays: جبرئيل, as the Kufans read; the dialect of Banū Asad: «جبرين» with nūn. Al-Ḥasan and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr read (لِجِبْرِيلَ) with fatḥa on the jīm and without hamza [Translator's note: i.e. جَبْرِيل; the printed vocalisation shows kasra]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the pattern فَعْليل with fatḥa on the fāʾ is not known in the speech of the Arabs; what exists is فِعْليل, as in دهليز, قطمير and برطل [Translator's note: برطل does not fit this pattern; so in the source]. It is not to be denied that in foreign speech there should occur what has no parallel in the speech of the Arabs, nor that it should be much altered, as they said إبراهيم, إبراهم, ابراهم and ابراهام. The fifth form is جبرئل. Whoever interprets the ḥadīth [as saying] «جبر is "servant" and «ال» is "Allah"» would have to say: هذا جبرإل, رأيت جبرال and مررت بجبرإل; but this is not said, so the meaning of the ḥadīth must be that he is named by this. The plural in the four forms, as a broken plural, is جباريل.

nahhas-irab:98-98.t: In ميكائيل there are four dialectal forms. The dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz [Translator's note: the text here is disordered in the source; phrases appear out of place, and it is translated as it stands]: "a strong dislike; and when he saw it in the written text with a yāʾ and a lām after the kāf, he read it (وميكايل), and he held that the alif (ميكال), and Abū ʿAmr read it so; Nāfiʿ departed from it because he strongly disliked contradicting the script; it was dropped just as it is dropped from foreign names such as إبراهيم and إسماعيل." This is a clear proof. Abū ʿAmr's proof is that the letters of prolongation and softness are often changed into one another, as they wrote ابن أبي طالب with a wāw, replacing the yāʾ with a wāw, while only ابن أبي طالب is said [Translator's note: so in the source; the point is that it was written "أبو" but pronounced "أبي"]. One also says ميكائل, and one says ميكاأل, as one says إسرأل with a hamza with fatḥa. Both are foreign names, and that is why they are diptotes.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: (وَلَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ): «آيات» is in the position of the accusative. According to the Basrans the tāʾ takes kasra so that the accusative and genitive are the same in the feminine, since it is a sound plural, just as they are the same in the masculine. The Kufans' view is: because the tāʾ is not a radical. The original form of آية is آية [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended original form, e.g. أَيَيَة, is not shown], and no verb is pronounced from it so that two weaknesses do not come together. (وَما يَكْفُرُ بِها إِلَّا الْفاسِقُونَ): they are nominative by their verb. The implied form is "and no one disbelieves in them except the defiantly disobedient", because an affirmation [after إلّا] must be preceded by a negation.

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: (أَوَكُلَّما عاهَدُوا عَهْداً): al-Akhfash said: the wāw is redundant (zāʾida), and the interrogative alif has entered upon it. Al-Kisāʾī's view is that it is «أو» with its wāw given a vowel. (كُلَّما) is an adverbial (ẓarf). (عَهْداً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) is an imperfect verb [Translator's note: the source says "فعل مستقبل", a future verb] in the position of the khabar.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t:
(وَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ): nominative by its verb. (مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ) is a naʿt (adjective), and it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial). (نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ) is the apodosis of لمّا. (مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ) is the predicate of the verb whose agent is not named [Translator's note: so in the source, "خبر ما لم يسمّ فاعله"].
(كِتابَ اللَّهِ) is accusative by نبذ. (وَراءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ) is an adverbial (ẓarf). (كَأَنَّهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): an imperfect verb [Translator's note: "فعل مستقبل" in the source] in the position of the khabar of كأن.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: (وَاتَّبَعُوا ما تَتْلُوا الشَّياطِينُ): this is a difficult verse, and we have examined its meanings thoroughly in the book before this one. The position of «ما» is accusative by اتّبعوا, and تتلو belongs to the ṣila (relative clause); the hāʾ has been dropped from it because of the length of the noun, the original being تتلوه الشياطين. «وسليمان», may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is a diptote, because it is definite and ends in two augments, so it resembles سكران. (وَلكِنَّ الشَّياطِينَ) is accusative by لكنّ; if you lighten لكن, you put what follows it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ. (يُعَلِّمُونَ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be in the position of the nominative as a second khabar. (النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ): two objects. (بِبابِلَ) is a diptote because it is a foreign proper noun. (هارُوتَ وَمارُوتَ) are likewise. The plural is هواريت, like طواغيت, and one says هوارتة and هوار, موارتة and موار — take note; similar to it are جالوت and طالوت. (وَما يُعَلِّمانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ): من is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, the implied form being وما يعلمان أحدا. (حَتَّى يَقُولا) is accusative by حتّى, and that is why the nūn has been dropped from it; the dialect of Hudhayl and Thaqīf is عتّى. (فَلا تَكْفُرْ) is jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition. (فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ): the best thing said about it is that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). Al-Farrāʾ's view that it is conjoined to «يعلّمون» is a mistake, because if that were so it would have to be فيتعلمون منهم; His saying منهما prevents the implied form from being «ولكن الشياطين كفروا يعلّمون الناس السحر فيتعلّمون», except on the view of whoever said that the devils are Hārūt and Mārūt. Al-Farrāʾ has another view: he said it may be construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of (فلا تكفر) is "so do not learn sorcery", i.e. "yet they come and learn." It has also been said: the implied form is "the two teach people, and they learn." (مِنْهُما ما يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ): [ما] is in the position of the accusative by يفرّقون. (وَما هُمْ بِضارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ): «من» is redundant. Abū Isḥāq's statement that (إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) means "except with Allah's knowledge" is a mistake, because for knowledge one says إذن, as in "I was informed of it" (قد أذنت به إذنا) [Translator's note: i.e. the verb أَذِنَ بِ "to know of"]; rather, since He did not come between them and it and left them to do it, it was as if it were a permission, figuratively. (وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا): a lām of emphasis. (لَمَنِ اشْتَراهُ): a lām of oath, which is also for emphasis. The position of «من» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, because what precedes the lām does not govern what follows it, and من means الذي (he who). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is conditional. Abū Isḥāq said: this is not a place for a condition; من means الذي, as you say: لقد علمت لمن جاءك ما له عقل ("I knew that the one who came to you has no sense"). (ما لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلاقٍ): «من» is redundant, the implied form being ما له في الآخرة خلاق; من is not added in an affirmative statement.

nahhas-irab:103-103.t: (وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا): the position of أنّ is the nominative, i.e. "if their belief had occurred." (لو) is followed only by a verb, overt or implied, because it is like the conditional particles, since it must have an apodosis and must be followed by a verb [Translator's note: the source has "ولَوْلا يليها", evidently for "ولو لا يليها", "and لو is not followed by…"]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it does not function as a conditional [i.e. does not make the verb jussive] because the way of all the conditional particles is to turn the past into a future meaning, and since this is not so with «لو», it may not function as a conditional. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «لو» here has no apodosis in wording, only in meaning, the meaning being "they would have been rewarded."

nahhas-irab:104-104.t:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَقُولُوا راعِنا): an imperative, and that is why the yāʾ has been dropped from it. The best thing said about it is the view of Mujāhid. He said: "Do not say 'Listen to us and we will listen to you', but say 'Make us understand'"; (انْظُرْنا): "explain to us." It is a command that they address him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with reverence. This is good, i.e. do not say "Be on equal terms with us in speech", as He said: ﴿لا تَجْعَلُوا دُعاءَ الرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكُمْ كَدُعاءِ بَعْضِكُمْ بَعْضاً﴾ [al-Nūr: 63]. Al-Ḥasan read (راعنا) with tanwīn [Translator's note: i.e. رَاعِنًا], making it accusative as a maṣdar, or accusative by the verb "say", i.e. "do not say folly."
Abū Jaʿfar said: what juts out from a mountain is called رعن, and the mountain is أرعن; a أرعن army is one that is spread out; and a أرعن man is one whose arguments are scattered, whose mind is not collected.

nahhas-irab:105-105.t: «المشركين» is conjoined to أهل. In grammar «ولا المشركون» is also possible, by conjoining it to الذين. (أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ): «من» is redundant, the implied form being أن ينزّل عليكم خير, [خير being] the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

nahhas-irab:106-106.t: (ما نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ): a condition, and the apodosis is (نَأْتِ). His saying (أَوْ نُنْسِها) is conjoined to ننسخ, and the yāʾ has been dropped because of the jussive. Whoever reads أو ننسأها dropped the ḍamma from the hamza because of the jussive. (أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ): jussive by لم; the interrogative particle does not change the governing effect of the governor. أنّ takes fatḥa because it is in the position of a noun.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t: «ملك» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), (له) is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of أنّ. ملك is derived from ملكت العجين, i.e. "I kneaded the dough thoroughly." (وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا نَصِيرٍ): نصير may be nominative, conjoined to the position, because the meaning is وما لكم من دون الله وليّ ولا نصير.

nahhas-irab:108-108.t: (أَمْ تُرِيدُونَ), i.e. "or rather (أبل) [do you want]"; Sībawayh related إنّها لإبل أم شاء ("They are camels — or rather sheep"). (أَنْ تَسْئَلُوا رَسُولَكُمْ) is in the position of the accusative by تريدون. (كَما سُئِلَ مُوسى): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar, i.e. "an asking like Moses was asked". If you lighten the hamza and make it between hamza and yāʾ, you say سئل. Al-Ḥasan read سيل, and this is according to the dialect of those who say سلت أسال; it may also be by replacement of the hamza, except that replacing the hamza is far-fetched. (موسى) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the case ending is not apparent on it because it ends in a short alif (maqṣūr), and it has no tanwīn because it is a diptote due to its foreignness. (وَمَنْ يَتَبَدَّلِ الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيمانِ): jussive by the condition; the lām takes kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and kasra was chosen because it is the sister of the jussive; it has also been said: because ḍamma and fatḥa occur without tanwīn as case endings. The apodosis is (فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ).

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: (وَدَّ كَثِيرٌ): nominative by ودّ. (مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ): genitive by من. (لَوْ يَرُدُّونَكُمْ): an imperfect verb [Translator's note: "فعل مستقبل" in the source]. (كُفَّاراً) is the second object; if you like, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (حَسَداً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun); al-Farrāʾ said: it is like a tamyīz (specification). (فَاعْفُوا) is an imperative; the original is فاعفوا [Translator's note: i.e. فاعْفُوُوا], the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness, then the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
«وَإِذا» is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). «قِيلَ لَهُمْ» is a past verb; «قِيلَّهُمْ» with assimilation is also permissible. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «قِيلَ لَهُمْ» here; the assimilated form is meant.] Combining two quiescent letters is allowed because the yāʾ is a letter of prolongation and softness. The original is قُوِلَ: the vowel of the wāw was shifted onto the qāf, so what preceded the wāw had kasra and it was turned into a yāʾ. Al-Akhfash said: قُيل with ḍamma on the qāf and with yāʾ is permissible. The view of al-Kisāʾī is to give the qāf a trace (ishmām) of ḍamma, to show that it is of the verb whose agent is not named [i.e. passive]; this is the dialect of many of Qays. As for Hudhayl, Banū Dubayr of Banū Asad and Banū Faqʿas, they say قُولَ with a quiescent wāw. «لهم»: the hāʾ and mīm are genitive through the lām.
«لا تُفْسِدُوا» is jussive through لا; the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn. «فِي الْأَرْضِ» is genitive through في. If you lighten the hamza, you shift its vowel onto the lām and drop it, but you do not drop the connecting alif, because the vowel is incidental; so you say «الَرْض». Al-Kisāʾī reported «أللرض»: when he lightened the hamza and dropped it, he substituted a lām for it. Al-Farrāʾ said: when the hamza was lightened the lām took a vowel; he disliked its having a vowel, since its origin is quiescence, so he added another lām to it so that the quiescence would remain intact.
«قالُوا إِنَّما نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); «ما», according to Sībawayh, is a restraining particle (kāffa) that stops إنّ from governing. As for the ḍamma of «نحن», the grammarians have several views. Hishām said: the original is نَحْنُ … the vowel of the ḥāʾ was shifted onto the nūn and the ḥāʾ made quiescent. [Translator's note: the source prints «نحن» unvowelled; the original form Hishām intends (presumably نَحُنْ) cannot be recovered from the text.] Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: نحن is like قبلُ and بعدُ, because it relates to reporting about two or more. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: it is like حيثُ, needing two things after it. [Translator's note: the source has «حيت», evidently for «حيث».] Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj said: «نحن» is for a group, and one of the signs of a group is the wāw; the ḍamma is of the same kind as the wāw, so when they were compelled to give نحن a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, they gave it the vowel that belongs to a group. He said: for this reason they gave ḍamma to the wāw of the plural in His saying «أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلالَةَ بِالْهُدى» [al-Baqara: 16]. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: نحن is used for what is nominative, so they gave it the vowel that resembles the nominative.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: «أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ»: «إنّ» has kasra because it begins the sentence. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: giving it fatḥa is permissible, just as Sībawayh permitted حقًّا أنّك منطلق ("truly, that you are leaving"), with «ألا» in that sense. The hāʾ and mīm are the noun (ism) of «إنّ»; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «المفسدون» the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of «إنّ». «هم» may also be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ and mīm, and it may be a fāṣila ("separator"); the Kufans say ʿimād ("support").

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
«وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا»: [its alif is] a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ), because you say يُؤْمِن. «كَما آمَنَ النَّاسُ»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a belief like the belief of the people".
«قالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ كَما آمَنَ السُّفَهاءُ أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهاءُ»: there are four views on it [i.e. on the meeting of the two hamzas in «السفهاءُ ألا»]. The best is to lighten the second hamza, turning it into a pure wāw, and to pronounce the first fully, so you say «السّفهاءُ وَلا»; this is the reading of the people of Medina and the well-known reading of Abū ʿAmr. If you wish, you may lighten both, making the first between hamza and alif and the second a pure wāw; if you wish, you may lighten the first and pronounce the second fully; and if you wish, you may pronounce both fully.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
«وَإِذا لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا»: the original is لَقِيُوا; the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness, then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Muḥammad ibn al-Samayfaʿ al-Yamānī read «وإذا لاقوا الذين آمنوا», the original being لاقَيُوا. If it is asked: why is the wāw of «لاقوا» given ḍamma in connected speech while [its vowel] is dropped from «لقوا»? The answer is that before the wāw in لقوا there is a ḍamma that indicates it, so it was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, whereas in «لاقوا» it was given a vowel because a fatḥa precedes it. [Translator's note: the passage is translated as written; the reasoning concerns the wāw before the following sukūn in connected speech.]
«الَّذِينَ» is in the position of the accusative by the verb; «آمَنُوا» is part of the ṣila (relative clause). «قالُوا آمَنَّا» is the answer (jawāb) of إذا.
«وَإِذا خَلَوْا إِلى شَياطِينِهِمْ»: if you lighten the hamza, you shift its vowel onto the wāw and drop it, as the people of Medina read. «شياطينهم» is genitive through إلى; it is a broken plural, which is why no nūn is dropped from it in the construct. The hāʾ and mīm are genitive by the iḍāfa (genitive construct).
«قالُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ»: the original is إنّنا; [a nūn] was dropped from it because of the gathering of nūns. «معكم» is accusative through the [implied] istiqrār ("being settled"). Whoever makes the ʿayn quiescent [مَعْكم] treats «مع» as a particle.
«إِنَّما نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِؤُنَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). If you lighten the hamza, Sībawayh makes it between hamza and wāw; his argument is that its own vowel has more right to it. Al-Akhfash held that he makes it a pure yāʾ, saying:
مستهزِيُون. Al-Akhfash said: I do in this what I did in His saying «السفهاء ولا». Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is not as al-Akhfash said, because in His saying «السفهاء ألا», if you pronounced it "between-between" you would be inclining it towards the alif, and an alif can only be preceded by a fatḥa, so you were forced to turn it into a wāw; مستهزئون is not like that. Whoever substitutes [rather than lightens] the hamza says مستهزُون, and it is written this way in the codex (muṣḥaf).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: «اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ»: «يستهزئ» is an imperfect verb in the position of the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of the genitive through the bāʾ. «وَيَمُدُّهُمْ» is conjoined to يستهزئ, and the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of the accusative by the verb. «فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ» is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
«أُولئِكَ» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الَّذِينَ» the khabar (predicate). «اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلالَةَ بِالْهُدى» is in the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. On the ḍamma of the wāw there are four views. The view of Sībawayh: it was given ḍamma to distinguish it from the radical wāw, as in «وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى» [al-Jinn: 16]. Al-Farrāʾ said: there should have been a wāw with ḍamma before it, because it is the wāw of the plural; when the wāw before it was dropped and they needed to give it a vowel, they gave it the vowel of the one that was dropped. Ibn Kaysān said: ḍamma on the wāw is lighter than any other vowel because it is of its own kind. Abū Isḥāq said: it is the wāw of the plural, given ḍamma as was done with نحن.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «اشْتَرَوِا الضَّلالَةَ» with kasra on the wāw, following the original rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī related from Qaʿnab Abū al-Sammāl al-ʿAdawī that he read «اشْتَرَوَا الضَّلالَةَ» with fatḥa on the wāw, because of the lightness of the fatḥa and because what precedes it has fatḥa. Al-Kisāʾī allowed «اشْتَرَؤُا الضَّلالَةَ» with ḍamma on the wāw [changed to hamza], as one says «أُقِّتَتْ» [al-Mursalāt: 11] and أَدْؤُر. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «اشْتَرَوُا» for all three variants; the variants are as described. Al-Kisāʾī's form, by the comparison with أُقِّتَت and أدؤر, is evidently with the wāw turned into a hamza.] Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a mistake, because hamzating a wāw when it has ḍamma is permissible only when it has ḍamma for no [incidental] cause.
«فَما رَبِحَتْ تِجارَتُهُمْ»: [تجارتهم] is nominative by ربحت. «وَما كانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ» is accusative as the khabar of كان; al-Farrāʾ says:
[it is] a ḥāl (circumstantial) that cannot be dispensed with. Ibn Kaysān said: تجارة and تجاير, ضلالة and ضلايل are permissible [as plurals].

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
[«مَثَلُهُمْ»] is the mubtadaʾ (subject). [Translator's note: the source entry begins with «ابتداء» alone; the word under discussion, مثلهم, is supplied in brackets.] «كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي» is its khabar (predicate); the kāf is in the sense of مثل, and «الَّذِي» is genitive by the iḍāfa (genitive construct).
«اسْتَوْقَدَ ناراً» is its ṣila (relative clause). «فَلَمَّا أَضاءَتْ ما حَوْلَهُ»: «ما» is in the position of the accusative in the sense of الذي; likewise if it is indefinite, except that it must have a naʿt (adjective) if it is indefinite; and if it is redundant it has no position.
«حَوْلَهُ» is an adverbial of place (ẓarf makān), and the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive by its being put in construct with it. «ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ» and "He removed their light" (أذهب نورهم) have one meaning. «وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُماتٍ»: Abū al-Sammāl read «وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلْماتٍ» with the lām quiescent, dropping the ḍamma because of its heaviness; whoever keeps it does so to distinguish between the noun and the adjective. One also says:
«ظُلَمات» with fatḥa on the lām. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «ظُلُماتٍ» for the quiescent variant and leaves «ظلمات» unvowelled; the forms are as described.] The Basrans said: a fatḥa was substituted for the ḍamma because it is lighter. Al-Kisāʾī said: ظُلَمات is a plural of a plural, the plural of ظُلَم.
«لا يُبْصِرُونَ» is an imperfect verb in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: [«صُمٌّ» is nominative] by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are deaf"; «بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ» [likewise]. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ḥafṣa: «صمًّا بكمًا عميًا» [in the accusative], because the meaning is "and He left them not seeing, deaf, dumb, blind"; it may also be in the sense of "I mean".

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
[«أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ»]: the original [of صيّب], according to the Basrans, is صَيْوِب, then it was assimilated, like ميّت. According to the Kufans the original is صَوِيب, then it was assimilated; but if it were as they say, it could not be assimilated, just as طويل cannot be assimilated. The plural of صيّب is صيايب. The implied sense in Arabic is: "their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindled a fire, or as the likeness of a rainstorm".
«فِيهِ ظُلُماتٌ»: [ظلمات] is the mubtadaʾ (subject). «وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ» are conjoined to it. «يَجْعَلُونَ» is resumptive; or, if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «فيه». If it is asked: how can it be a ḥāl when nothing refers back to the hāʾ? The answer is that the implied sense is "in its thunderclaps", like «يُصْهَرُ بِهِ ما فِي بُطُونِهِمْ وَالْجُلُودُ» [al-Ḥajj: 20].
