«أَصابِعَهُمْ»: in the singular of الأصابع there are five dialectal forms: one says إِصْبَع with kasra on the hamza and fatḥa on the bāʾ; أَصْبِع with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on the bāʾ; and with fatḥa on both, kasra on both, and ḍamma on both. It is feminine, and so is الأذن. It is reported from al-Ḥasan that he read «من الصّواقع»; this is the dialect of Tamīm and some of Rabīʿa.
«حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ»: one also says حِذار. Sībawayh said: it is accusative because it is something for the sake of which [the action] is done, i.e. a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and in reality it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 8-
وأغفر عوراء الكريم ادّخاره ... وأعرض عن شتم اللّئيم تكرّما
(I forgive the noble man's lapse, to keep him in store, and I turn away from the base man's abuse out of magnanimity.)
«وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكافِرِينَ» is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
«يَكادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصارَهُمْ»: outside the Qur'an يكاد أن يفعل is permissible, as [the poet] said: [al-Rajaz metre] 9-
قد كاد من طول البلى أن يمصحا
(From long decay it had almost faded away.)
In «يخطف» there are seven ways. The eloquent reading is «يَخْطَفُ». ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read «يَكادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطِفُ أَبْصارَهُمْ» with kasra on the ṭāʾ; Saʿīd al-Akhfash said:
it is a dialectal form. Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī read «يَكادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخِطِّفُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the khāʾ and ṭāʾ, and it is reported from al-Ḥasan that he read with fatḥa on the khāʾ [يَخَطِّف].
Al-Farrāʾ said: some of the people of Medina read with the khāʾ quiescent and the ṭāʾ doubled [يَخْطِّف]. Al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: «يِخِطِّفُ» is permissible, with kasra on the yāʾ, the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «يَخْطَفُ» for these variants; the forms in brackets follow the descriptions.] These are six ways in agreement with the written text (al-sawād). The seventh was reported by ʿAbd al-Wārith, who said: I saw in the codex of Ubayy «يكاد البرق يتخطّف أبصارهم».
Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī held that for whoever reads «يَخِطِّف» with kasra on the khāʾ and ṭāʾ, the original according to him is «يختطف»; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ, two quiescent letters met, and the khāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of the two quiescent letters. Sībawayh said: whoever gives it fatḥa shifted the vowel of the tāʾ onto it. Al-Farrāʾ said: this is a mistake; whoever says it would have to say in يمدّ «يمدّ» — because the mīm was quiescent and the dāl after it was made quiescent — and in يعضّ «يعضّ». [Translator's note: the forms al-Farrāʾ intends (presumably يَمِدّ and يَعِضّ, with kasra) are unvowelled in the source.] Al-Farrāʾ said: the kasra is there only because the alif in «اختطف» has kasra. Abū Jaʿfar said: the followers of Sībawayh said: what al-Farrāʾ said does not follow, because if يَمِدّ and يَعِضّ were said they would be confused with yafʿil, whereas yaftaʿil can only be of one form. Al-Kisāʾī said: whoever says يِخِطِّف gives the yāʾ kasra because the alif in اختطف has kasra. As for what al-Farrāʾ reported from the people of Medina — the khāʾ quiescent with assimilation — it is not known and not permissible, because it combines two quiescent letters.
«كُلَّما»:
is accusative because it is an adverbial (ẓarf); and when كلّما is in the sense of إذا it is connected [to what follows]. Al-Farrāʾ said: one says أضاءك and ضاءك. «لذَّهب بسمعهم» with assimilation is permissible. «وَأَبْصارِهِمْ» is conjoined to it. «إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ» is the noun (ism) of إنّ and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:233-233.t:
وَالْوالِداتُ: mubtadaʾ (subject). يُرْضِعْنَ: in the position of the khabar (predicate); the verb of the infant is رضع يرضع, so he is راضع. حَوْلَيْنِ: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), and it is not permitted that the action be in only one of them. This is the view of Sībawayh.
Mujāhid, Ḥumayd ibn Qays and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «لمن أراد أن تَتمّ الرّضاعةُ», with fatḥa on the first tāʾ and the nominative on الرضاعة after it. Abū Jaʿfar said: لِمَنْ أَرادَ أَنْ يُتِمَّ الرَّضاعَةَ is [also] permitted with the yāʾ, because الرّضاعة and الرّضاع are the same. The Basrans recognise الرضاعة only with fatḥa on the rāʾ, and الرضاع only with kasra on the rāʾ, like القتال; the Kufans reported kasra on the rāʾ with the hāʾ and fatḥa without the hāʾ. Abū Rajāʾ, who was eloquent, read لِمَنْ أَرادَ أَنْ يُتِمَّ الرِّضاعَةَ [Translator's note: the source prints the vowelling الرَّضاعَةَ here; the point being made requires kasra, الرِّضاعة], and he read «لا تَكَلَّفُ نفسٌ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ. لا تُضَارَّ والِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِها: in the position of jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition; the rāʾ was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and kasra on it is permitted, and that is a reading. Abū ʿAmr read «لا تُضارُّ», making it a statement with the meaning of a prohibition; this is figurative, and the first is literal. Abān narrated from ʿĀṣim «لا تضارر والدة», and this is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: the implied form of «لا تضارّ والدة» may be «لا تضارَر», then it was assimilated. Abū Jaʿfar said: in «لا تضارّ والدة», [والدة] is the noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] if the implied form is «لا تضارَر», and if the implied form is «لا تضارِر» it is nominative by its verb [as fāʿil (agent)]. [Translator's note: the source writes both forms identically as «لا تضارر»; the distinction intended is the passive تضارَر versus the active تضارِر.] وَلا مَوْلُودٌ: conjoined to it with the wāw, and «لا» is for emphasis (tawkīd). وَعَلَى الْوارِثِ مِثْلُ ذلِكَ: nominative as mubtadaʾ or by the ṣifa [i.e. the prepositional phrase]. وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلادَكُمْ: the implied form in Arabic is «وإن أردتم أن تسترضعوا أجنبية لأولادكم» (if you wish to seek a [nursing] stranger for your children); the lām was omitted because it is a verb that takes two objects, one of them by means of a particle. Sībawayh recited: [al-Basīṭ] 51-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded; I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)

nahhas-irab:234-234.t:
وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْواجاً: it is asked: where is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»? There are several views on this. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: the implied form is «والذين يتوفّون منكم ويذرون أزواجا يتربّصن بأنفسهنّ بعدهم» or «بعد موتهم» (… [the wives] shall wait by themselves after them / after their death), then this was omitted, as a great deal is omitted. Al-Kisāʾī said: in the implied form it is «يتربّص أزواجهم» (their wives shall wait), just as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مَسْجِداً ضِراراً وَكُفْراً ... لا تَقُمْ فِيهِ أَبَداً [al-Tawba: 107, 108], i.e. do not stand in their mosque. Al-Farrāʾ said: when nouns are mentioned, then nouns annexed to them are mentioned that carry the meaning of the predicate, and the reliance in the predicate is on the second, the predication is made about the second and the first is left. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: this is an error; it is not permitted to begin with a noun and say nothing about it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: among the best of what has been said on it is the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad]. He said: the implied form is «والذين يتوفّون منكم ويذرون أزواجا أزواجهم يتربّصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشرا» (… their wives shall wait by themselves four months and ten), then [أزواجهم] was omitted, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 52-
وما الدّهر إلّا تارتان فمنهما ... أموت وأخرى أبتغي العيش أكدح
(Time is nothing but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a living, toiling.)
There is a fourth view on it, the implied form being «وأزواج الذين يتوفّون منكم» (and the wives of those of you who die). And we have mentioned وعشرا.

nahhas-irab:235-235.t: وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيما عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّساءِ: خطبة and خطب are the same; خُطبة [a speech] is what has a beginning and an end, and likewise whatever is on the pattern فُعلة, such as الأكلة and الضغطة. أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ: one says أكننت الشيء when you hid the thing within yourself, and كننته: I guarded it; from this is كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَكْنُونٌ [al-Ṣāffāt: 49]. These are the most eloquent of the usages. وَلكِنْ لا تُواعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا: i.e. «على سرّ» (in secret); the particle was omitted because it is among the verbs that take two objects, one of them by means of a particle. It may also be in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial). إِلَّا أَنْ تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفاً: an exception not of the same kind as the first. وَلا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكاحِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْكِتابُ أَجَلَهُ: i.e. «على عقدة النكاح», then «على» was omitted, as preceded. Sībawayh reported «ضرب فلان الظهر والبطن» (so-and-so was struck on the back and belly), i.e. with «على»; Sībawayh said: omission in these things is not analogically extended. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning may also be «ولا تعقدوا عقدة النكاح» (do not conclude the marriage tie), because the meaning of تعقدوا and تعزموا is the same; and one says تعزموا.

nahhas-irab:236-236.t: وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ: it is [also] read «قَدْرُه», and al-Farrāʾ permitted «قَدَرَه» [Translator's note: the source writes the forms without vowels; the vowelling given follows the discussion of the accusative below]. Abū Jaʿfar said: most of the lexicographers report that قَدْر and قَدَر have the same meaning. Some of them said: القَدْر with sukūn is capacity; one says "so-and-so spends according to his qadr", i.e. according to his capacity. And القَدَر with the vowel is mostly used for a thing when it is equal to another thing; one says "this is according to the qadar of this". As for the accusative, it is because the meaning of متّعوهنّ and أعطوهن (give them) is the same. مَتاعاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "his measure, in this state".

nahhas-irab:237-237.t: فَنِصْفُ ما فَرَضْتُمْ: i.e. «فعليكم» (then upon you is …); the accusative is permitted outside the Qur'an, i.e. «فأدّوا نصف ما فرضتم» (then pay half of what you appointed). One says نُصف and نِصف meaning نَصف [Translator's note: the source writes the three forms unvowelled]. إِلَّا أَنْ يَعْفُونَ: in the position of accusative by «أن», and the sign of the accusative is discarded in it because it is indeclinable (mabnī); we have mentioned its parallel, except that we will explain it further. Sībawayh's view is that it was made indeclinable only because of what they added to it, and because it resembles the past verb, and the past verb is indeclinable, so it was made indeclinable as the past is. Sībawayh illustrated this by the fact that [imperfect] verbs were made declinable because they resemble nouns, and a verb's resembling a verb is more fitting than a verb's resembling a noun; this is among the admired parts of Sībawayh's view. The Kufans said: its proper course would be to drop the nūn from it, but it is a sign, and if it were dropped the meaning would be lost. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this verb is defective from three directions, and when a thing is defective from three directions it is made indeclinable: that it is a verb, that it is for a plural, and that it is for a feminine. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq being asked about this, and he said: it is an error in the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās, because if we named a woman «فرعون» we would not make it indeclinable. أَوْ يَعْفُوَا الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكاحِ: conjoined. وَأَنْ تَعْفُوا أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوى: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the original form is «تعفووا» [Translator's note: the source writes «يعفوا»], the first wāw was made quiescent because of the heaviness of the vowel on it, then it was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. وَلا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ: Ṭāwūs said: [it is] doing kindness. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the ḍamma of this wāw in اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلالَةَ.

nahhas-irab:238-238.t:
حافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَواتِ وَالصَّلاةِ الْوُسْطى: we have mentioned it, and we will explain it further. Al-Ruʾāsī read «حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاةَ الوسطى» in the accusative, i.e. "and keep to the middle prayer". In the text of Ibn Masʿūd it is «وعلى الصلاة الوسطى», and it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās «والصلاة الوسطى صلاة العصر». This reading is by way of exegesis, because it is an addition to the Muṣḥaf. The hadith narrated about the reading and the writing, «حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى وصلاة العصر», does not require that the middle [prayer] be other than ʿAṣr, just as His saying, Mighty and Majestic: فِيهِما فاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ [al-Raḥmān: 68] [does not require] that the date palms and pomegranates be other than fruit, and as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 53-
النّازلون بكلّ معترك ... والطّيّبون معاقد الأزر
(Those who dismount at every battlefield, and those pure where their waist-wraps are tied.)
«الطّيّبون» here is not other than «النازلين». Sībawayh reported «مررت بزيد أخيك وصديقك» (I passed by Zayd, your brother and your friend), and the friend is the brother. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the argument of whoever said the middle prayer is ʿAṣr, because it is between two prayers of the daytime prayers and two prayers of the night prayers. Better than this argument is that it was called the middle because it lies between two prayers, one of them the first prescribed and the other the third of what was prescribed. The argument of whoever said it is Ṣubḥ (dawn) is that it is between two prayers of the daytime and two prayers of the night. The argument of whoever said it is Ẓuhr is that it is in the middle of the day. Some said: it is the later ʿIshāʾ; and some said: it is Maghrib, because it is between two prayers of the day and two prayers of the night. وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ: accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), and we have explained its meaning.

nahhas-irab:239-239.t:
فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ: a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is what we said: فَرِجالًا, accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "then pray on foot". The meaning is: if you fear [being unable] to stand before Allah devoutly, then pray walking or riding. Abū Jaʿfar said: one says راجل, رجلان and رجل with one meaning. In the plural there are several usages: one says رجّالة and رجال, like صاحب and صحاب, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 54-
وقال صح ابي: قد شأونك فاطلب
(And my companions said: they have outstripped you, so pursue.) [Translator's note: the source prints «صح ابي», evidently «صحابي» (my companions), the word being cited.]
رجال may also be the plural of رجل meaning راجل. In the plural one also says رجّال, like كاتب and كتّاب; and one says رجل, like تاجر and تجر; and one says راجل, رجلة and رجلة as a collective noun, and likewise رجال without doubling; and one says رجالي, رجالي and رجلي as plurals of رجلان. [Translator's note: the source gives these forms unvowelled and repeats some; translated as written.] فَإِذا أَمِنْتُمْ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ: i.e. then stand before Allah devoutly.

nahhas-irab:240-240.t: وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْواجاً وَصِيَّةً لِأَزْواجِهِمْ: «الذين» is in the position of nominative, if you wish as mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being «يوصون وصيّة» (they make a bequest), and the meaning «ليوصوا وصيّة» (let them make a bequest). Or, if you wish, «الذين» is nominative by an implied verb, i.e. «يوصّي الذين يتوفّون منكم وصيّة». There is a third aspect in the nominative, i.e. «وفيما فرض عليكم الذين يتوفّون منكم ويذرون أزواجا يوصون وصيّة لأزواجهم» (and among what has been prescribed for you: those of you who die and leave wives make a bequest for their wives). «الذين» is indeclinable in one state because it is only complete with a ṣila (relative clause), though one also says «الّذون» in the nominative position. Whoever read «وصيةٌ» in the nominative, its implied form is «والذين يتوفّون منكم عليهم وصيّة لأزواجهم» (upon them is a bequest for their wives). مَتاعاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to al-Akhfash; according to Abū al-ʿAbbās, i.e. «ذوي متاع» (possessors of provision). غَيْرَ إِخْراجٍ: there are three aspects in its accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. «من غير إخراج» (without expulsion). Al-Akhfash said: it is a maṣdar, i.e. «لا إخراجا», then «غير» was put in the place of «لا». It has been said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «غير ذوي إخراج», the meaning being: they make bequests for them, not expelling them. All this is abrogated by the quarter and the eighth [al-Nisāʾ: 12], by أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْراً [al-Baqara: 234], and by «لا وصيّة لوارث» (no bequest for an heir). فَإِنْ خَرَجْنَ: a condition, and the apodosis is فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فيما فعلن في أنفسهنّ من معروف.

nahhas-irab:241-241.t: وَلِلْمُطَلَّقاتِ مَتاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ حَقًّا: al-Akhfash said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. «أحقّ ذلك حقا» (I make that a binding right). Abū Jaʿfar said: عَلَى is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted verb, i.e. «يحق ذلك على المتّقين حقا» (that is binding upon the God-fearing as a right).

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: Al-Farrāʾ allowed (هُوداً) to mean يهودي (Jew), with the augment dropped from it, or to be the plural of هائد; the second view is the position of the Basrans. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: (إِلَّا مَنْ كانَ): He made كان singular according to the wording of «من», then said هودا in the plural because the meaning of من is plural. (تِلْكَ أَمانِيُّهُمْ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); تلك أمانيهم [Translator's note: i.e. with a light yāʾ, أمانِيهم] is also possible. (قُلْ هاتُوا): the original is هاتيوا; the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness, then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. For a single male one says هات يا هذا, like رام, and for a female هاتي, like رامي. (وإِنْ كُنْتُمْ) is conditional, i.e. «if you are truthful, then make clear what you have said with a proof».

nahhas-irab:112-112.t: (بَلى مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ) is according to the wording of من [i.e. singular]; then He said فلهم according to the meaning [i.e. plural].

nahhas-irab:114-114.t: Mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: the Qur'anic words, وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ, are not quoted in the source], i.e. "and who — which one — is more unjust." (مِمَّنْ مَنَعَ مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا اسْمُهُ): أن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from مساجد. The implied form may also be "from (من) His name being mentioned"; prepositions are dropped with أن because of the length of the speech, and it has been said: because the meaning is made clear in the verb after it. (وَسَعى) is conjoined to منع. (أُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause is the khabar. (خائِفِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا خِزْيٌ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ, or, if you like, in the sense of "[disgrace] is due", and so on.

nahhas-irab:115-115.t: (فَأَيْنَما تُوَلُّوا) is conditional, and that is why the nūn has been dropped. «أين» is the governing word and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida). Al-Ḥasan read (فَأَيْنَما تُوَلُّوا) with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the lām [Translator's note: i.e. تَوَلَّوْا], the original being تتولّون. (فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ): «ثمّ» is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and its meaning is distance, except that it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, not inflected, because it is vague; it is like هناك ("there") for distance, and if you want nearness you say هنا ("here").

nahhas-irab:116-116.t: (سُبْحانَهُ): a maṣdar (verbal noun). (بَلْ لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ): «ما» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or, if you like, by [the notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār). (كُلٌّ لَهُ قانِتُونَ): mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate); the implied form is كلّهم, then the hāʾ and the mīm were dropped.

nahhas-irab:117-117.t: (بَدِيعُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned the nominative of (فيكون).

nahhas-irab:118-118.t: (مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ): an object (mafʿūl); if you like, it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:119-119.t: (بَشِيراً): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَنَذِيراً) is conjoined to it. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: (وَلا تُسْئَلُ عَنْ أَصْحابِ الْجَحِيمِ) is also permissible with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the lām [Translator's note: so in the source; ḍamma on the lām is what the printed form already has], and it would then be in the position of a ḥāl, conjoined to «بشيرا ونذيرا».

nahhas-irab:120-120.t: (وَلَنْ تَرْضى عَنْكَ الْيَهُودُ وَلَا النَّصارى): the maṣdar is رضوان and رضوان, مرضاة, رضى and رضى [Translator's note: i.e. رِضْوان and رُضْوان, رِضًى and رُضًى]; it is one of the verbs with wāw [as last radical]. In the dual one says رضوان; al-Kisāʾī related رضيان, and he related رضاءا with the long alif (mamdūd), as though it were the maṣdar of راضى. (حَتَّى تَتَّبِعَ) is accusative by حتّى, and حتى stands in place of أن. (وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْواءَهُمْ): the plural of هوى, as you say جمل and أجمال.

nahhas-irab:121-121.t: (الَّذِينَ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ) is its ṣila (relative clause). (يَتْلُونَهُ) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; if you like, the khabar is (أُولئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ).

nahhas-irab:122-122.t: Al-Ḥasan read "نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم" with the yāʾ vowelless, then dropped in connected speech because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. (وَأَنِّي) is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «نعمتي».

nahhas-irab:124-124.t: ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Rajāʾ and al-Aʿmash read (قالَ لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ) [Translator's note: their reading is الظالمون in the nominative; the printed vocalisation shows the standard reading]. Al-Farrāʾ said: because whatever reaches you, you have reached it, as you say نلت خيرا ("I attained good") and نالني خير ("good reached me"). It is related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: the meaning requires the accusative of الظالمين. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said to Abraham, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿إِنِّي جاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِماماً﴾; He entrusted him with this, and Abraham asked, saying ﴿وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾, and He, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: "I will not make a wrongdoer an imam." It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: Abraham asked that an imam be made from his offspring, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that among his offspring there would be some who would disobey, so He said ﴿لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ﴾.

nahhas-irab:125-125.t:
(وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثابَةً): two objects. The original is مثوبة; the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the thāʾ, and the wāw changed into an alif, following ثاب يثوب. Al-Akhfash said: the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) in «مثابة» is for intensity, because of the great number of those who return to it. (وَأَمْناً) is conjoined to مثابة. (وَاتَّخِذُوا) [Translator's note: the reading discussed first is evidently وَاتَّخَذُوا, past tense; the printed vocalisation shows the imperative] is conjoined to جعلنا. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. "and remember when they took", conjoined to ﴿اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ﴾. Whoever reads (وَاتَّخِذُوا) cut it off from what precedes, made it an imperative, and conjoined a clause to a clause. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned that it has been said that the more likely view is that «مقام إبراهيم» is the one towards which the imams pray at present, and if so, then (وَاتَّخِذُوا) is preferable, because of the ḥadīth of Ḥumayd from Anas. Abū Jaʿfar said: that ḥadīth was transmitted from Anas only by Ḥumayd, only through one channel, so it is weak. It is not unlikely that «واتّخذوا» [i.e. the imperative] was by way of choice and then it was acted upon; moreover Ḥammād ibn Salama transmitted from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa from his father that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, for the early part of his caliphate, used to pray facing the House, and then ʿUmar prayed towards the Maqām. Abū Jaʿfar said: «مَقام» from قام يقوم can be a maṣdar (verbal noun) or a noun of place, and مُقام is from أقام; the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) may be added to both for intensity. (وَعَهِدْنا إِلى إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْماعِيلَ): in the position of the genitive; they are diptotes because they are foreign. A diptote in the position of the genitive is accusative [in form] because it resembles the verb, and the verb does not take the genitive — this is the view of the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ said: it ought to be in the genitive without tanwīn, except that they disliked its resembling the noun in construct in the dialect of those who say مررت بغلامِ يا هذا ("I passed by my servant, O you"). (أَنْ طَهِّرا بَيْتِيَ): أن may be in the position of the accusative, the implied form being بأن ("that"); it may also have no grammatical position, being explicative, since according to Sībawayh it then means أي ("that is"), while the Kufans say: it is in the sense of "saying".
(لِلطَّائِفِينَ): genitive by the lām. (وَالْعاكِفِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ): conjoined. (السُّجُودِ): a naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:126-126.t:
(وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ رَبِّ): a vocative in a genitive construct. (اجْعَلْ هذا) is a request whose wording is imperative, except that it is considered too grave to call it a command. (وَارْزُقْ أَهْلَهُ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ): an object. (مَنْ آمَنَ) is a badal (substitute) from أهل, and this is the substitution of the part for the whole. (قالَ وَمَنْ كَفَرَ): «من» is in the position of the accusative, the implied form being "and provide for whoever disbelieves", the omitted verb being indicated by فأمتّعه. من may also be conditional, in the position of the accusative with the verb implied after it. It may also be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being «فأمّتعه».
In the reading of Ubayy: "فنمتّعه قليلا ثمّ نضطره", and in the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb: "فأمتعه قليلا ثمّ اضطرّه" with kasra on the hamza [Translator's note: i.e. إِضطرُّه] and the verb in the nominative, according to the dialect of those who say أنت تضرب [Translator's note: i.e. تِضرب, with kasra on the prefix]. It is related from Ibn Muḥayṣin that he used to assimilate the ḍād into the ṭāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not permissible, because the ḍād has spreading (tafashshī), so it is not assimilated into anything; but the ṭāʾ may be assimilated into it, as they said اضّجع and «فمن اضّرّ». Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb ibn ʿAlī narrated to us: ʿImrān ibn Bakkār informed me:
Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Zubaydī narrated to us: Shuʿayb ibn Isḥāq narrated to us from Hārūn from Ḥanẓala from al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Rabīʿa, who said: (وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلًا ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُ) [Translator's note: his reading is evidently فأَمْتِعْهُ … ثم اضْطَرَّهُ as a request, as the following explanation shows; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is by way of asking and request. The original is اضطرره; then it was assimilated and given fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, because of the lightness of fatḥa; kasra is also permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading is irregular (shādhdh), and both the sequence of the speech and the exegesis point to something else. As for the sequence of the speech: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, related of Abraham, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said ﴿رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هذا بَلَداً آمِناً﴾, then brought his [further] words without separating them with "he said"; then He said [قال], so this was an answer from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and He did not say afterwards "Abraham said." As for the exegesis: it is soundly established from Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb — and this is the wording of Ibn ʿAbbās — that Abraham, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed specifically for those who believed, to the exclusion of other people, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that He provides for whoever disbelieves just as He provides for whoever believes, and that He gives him enjoyment for a little while and then forces him to the punishment of the Fire. Abū Jaʿfar said: and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿كُلًّا نُمِدُّ هؤُلاءِ وَهَؤُلاءِ مِنْ عَطاءِ رَبِّكَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 20], and He said ﴿وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ﴾ [Hūd: 48]. Abū Isḥāq said: Abraham, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, knew that among his offspring there would be disbelievers, so he singled out the believers, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, had said to him ﴿لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 124].

nahhas-irab:127-128.t:
(الْقَواعِدَ): the singular is قاعدة; and the singular in His saying ﴿الْقَواعِدُ مِنَ النِّساءِ﴾ [al-Nūr: 60] is قاعد. (وَإِسْماعِيلُ) is conjoined to إبراهيم. (رَبَّنا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا): al-Akhfash said: the one who said «ربّنا تقبل منّا» was Ishmael; others say: both of them said it. Al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ويقولان ربّنا تقبّل منّا". (وأرنا مناسكنا): وأرنا with a vowelless rāʾ is far-fetched, because the original is
أرينا [Translator's note: i.e. أَرْئِنا, with a hamza]; the yāʾ was dropped because it is an imperative, the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the rāʾ and the hamza was dropped, so if the kasra is also dropped that is excessive mutilation. This is not like فخذ [i.e. فخْذ for فخِذ], because the kasra in أرنا indicates the hamza, whereas the kasra in فخذ does not indicate anything; but it may be dropped, though unlikely, because it is felt heavy, just as the kasra in فخذ is felt heavy. Al-Akhfash said: the singular of المناسك is منسك, like مسجد, and one also says
منسك [Translator's note: i.e. مَنْسِك and مَنْسَك]. Abū Jaʿfar said: one says نسك ينسك, so on this basis one ought to say منسك [Translator's note: i.e. مَنْسُك], except that the pattern مَفْعُل does not exist in the speech of the Arabs.

nahhas-irab:129-129.t: (يَتْلُوا) is in the position of the accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of رسول, i.e. "a messenger reciting." Outside the Qur'an it may be jussive, as the apodosis of the request. (وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ) is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:130-130.t: (وَمَنْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is a complete noun in interrogation and in conditionals. (يَرْغَبُ) is an imperfect verb [Translator's note: "فعل مستقبل" in the source] in the position of the khabar (predicate); it is a rhetorical question of reproach that carries the meaning of negation, i.e. "no one turns away" (عَنْ مِلَّةِ إِبْراهِيمَ إِلَّا مَنْ سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ). Al-Farrāʾ's statement that (نَفْسَهُ) is like ضقت به ذرعا ("I was straitened by it in capacity") is impossible according to the Basrans, because he made a definite noun accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Sībawayh — he mentioned the ḥāl (circumstantial) and that it is like the tamyīz — said: this can only be indefinite; he means what is accusative as a ḥāl, just as that can only be indefinite, meaning the tamyīz. Abū Jaʿfar said: if you bring a definite noun, the meaning of tamyīz disappears, because you do not specify with it what belongs to its genus. Al-Farrāʾ said: similar to it is بطرت معيشتها; and according to him one may not say نفسه سفه زيد, nor معيشتها بطرت القرية [i.e. fronting it]. Al-Kisāʾī said — and it is one of al-Akhfash's two views —: the meaning is "except one who is foolish in himself", and both allow fronting. Al-Akhfash said: similar to it is ﴿عُقْدَةَ النِّكاحِ﴾, i.e. "upon the knot of marriage." Abū Jaʿfar said: we have examined this thoroughly in the book before this one. (وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): it may be asked: how is it permissible to put في الآخرة first when it belongs to the ṣila (relative clause)? The answer is that the implied form is not "and he is among those who are righteous in the Hereafter", which would make the ṣila precede. The grammarians have three views on it: one is that the meaning is "and he is righteous in the Hereafter", then [this] was omitted; it has been said that «في الآخرة» is attached to an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "his righteousness in the Hereafter"; and the third view is that الصالحين does not mean "those who became righteous" but is a noun standing by itself, as one says الرجل and الغلام. The original of (اصْطَفَيْناهُ) is اصتفيناه: the tāʾ was replaced by ṭāʾ because ṭāʾ is emphatic (muṭbaqa) like the ṣād and is from the point of articulation of the tāʾ. The ṣād may not be assimilated, because it is assimilated only into its two sisters, the zāy and the sīn, because of the whistling they have; but the tāʾ may be assimilated into it outside the Qur'an, so you say اصّفيناه before.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
«يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ» … «يا أَيُّهَا»: «يا» is the vocative particle, and أيّ is a single [non-construct] noun addressed in the vocative; it has ḍamma because it is in the place of a pronoun. It ought not to be declined, but they disliked leaving it without a vowel because it had been fully declinable, so they chose ḍamma for it, since fatḥa attaches to what is declined in the vocative and kasra attaches to what is put in construct [with the speaker's yāʾ]. Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī permitted «يا أيّها الناسَ» according to the position, as one says يا زيدُ الظريفَ. Al-Akhfash held that «الناس» is in the ṣila (relative clause) of أيّ, and «ها» is for drawing attention, except that it never separates from أيّ because it is a compensation for the construct. The dialect of some of Banū Mālik of Banū Asad is «يا أيُّهُ الرجل» with ḍamma on the hāʾ: since the hāʾ is inseparable, he gave it the vowel of أيّ.
«النَّاسُ» follows أيّ like a naʿt (adjective), being qualified as an adjective is; according to Abū al-ʿAbbās its accusative is not permissible because it cannot be dispensed with, so it is as if you said يا ناسُ.
«اعْبُدُوا»: [its alif is] a connecting alif, because it is from يَعْبُد; you gave it ḍamma — the original being kasra — so as not to combine a kasra and a ḍamma. Sībawayh said: there is no fiʿul pattern in the language. The nūn was dropped for the jussive according to the Kufans, and because [the imperative] does not resemble [nouns] according to the Basrans.
«رَبَّكُمُ» is accusative by اعبدوا. «الَّذِي» is its naʿt. «خَلَقَكُمْ» is in the ṣila, and the kāf and mīm are accusative by the verb. «وَالَّذِينَ» is conjoined to the kāf and mīm. «مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ» is in the ṣila. «لَعَلَّكُمْ»: the kāf and mīm are the noun (ism) of لعلّ. «تَتَّقُونَ» is an imperfect verb whose sign of the nominative is the nūn; it is in the position of the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
«الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فِراشاً» … «الَّذِي» is a naʿt (adjective) of ربّكم, or, if you wish, a naʿt of الذي خلقكم — and it is proper to speak of an adjective of an adjective because the adjective is the thing qualified in meaning. It may be accusative by تتقون; it may be in the sense of "I mean"; and it may be in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). «جعلّكم» with assimilation is permissible, because the two letters are identical and the vowels are many, but not assimilating is better because they belong to two words. «الْأَرْضَ فِراشاً» are the two objects of جعل.
«وَالسَّماءَ بِناءً» is conjoined. السماء may be a plural of سماوة and سماءة, or a feminine singular like عَناق; treating it as masculine is anomalous. Its plurals are سماوات, سماءات, أَسْمٍ and سمايا. السماء [also means] rain, and is masculine, as is [its sense of] "roof" in common usage; its plurals [in that sense] are أَسْمِية, سُمِيّ and سِمِيّ.
«وبناء» may be shortened [بِنًى], as the plural of بِنْية, and [the long form is] a maṣdar (verbal noun); one also says بُنًى as the plural of بُنْية. With the long (mamdūd) form, there are five dialectal ways of pausing. The best is «والسماء بناءْ» with a hamza between two alifs. It is permissible to lighten the hamza so that it becomes weak. It is permissible to drop it because of its closeness to a quiescent letter, being between two quiescent letters; if you drop it you drop the alif after it, and say «بنا», pronounced like the short form. Some of the Arabs add a prolongation after it in its form. Some of them substitute a yāʾ for the hamza and say بنيت بنايا; the Basrans say it is assimilated to خطايا, and al-Farrāʾ says the hamza was returned to its origin, since its origin is yāʾ. [Translator's note: the source says "five dialectal ways" but lists them in a compressed manner; translated as written.]
«وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً»: the original of ماء is مَوَه; the wāw was turned into an alif because it had a vowel and what preceded it had a vowel, so you said ماه; then two faint letters met, so a hamza was substituted for the hāʾ, because it is firmer and more like the alif, and you said ماء. The first alif is the ʿayn of the verb, after it comes the hamza that replaces the hāʾ, and after the hamza an alif that replaces the tanwīn. Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī said: according to the Basrans it may only be written with two alifs, or, if you wish, with three. When they make it plural or diminutive they return it to its origin and say مُوَيْه, أمواه and مياه, like أجمال and جمال.
«فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ»: plural of ثمرة. One says ثَمَر like شَجَر, ثُمُر like خُشُب, ثُمْر like بُدْن, and ثِمار like إكام. «رِزْقاً لَكُمْ» is the object. «فَلا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْداداً»: «تجعلوا» is jussive by the prohibition, which is why the nūn is dropped from it. «أندادا» is the first object, and «لله» is in the position of the second. «وَأَنْتُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ; «تَعْلَمُونَ» is an imperfect verb in the position of the khabar, and the clause is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
«وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ» is in the position of the jussive through the condition. «فِي رَيْبٍ» is genitive through في. «مِمَّا نَزَّلْنا»: «ما» is genitive through من, and the pronoun referring back to it is omitted because of the length of the noun [with its ṣila], i.e. "what We sent down (نزّلناه)". «عَلى عَبْدِنا» is genitive through على.
«فَأْتُوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), or, if you wish, you may call it the requital (mujāzāt). Ibn Kaysān said: فأتوا is [written] short because it is from the root of المجيء ("coming"). Al-Farrāʾ reported «فتوا» in his reading, so «فتوا» is permissible. «بِسُورَةٍ» is genitive through the bāʾ. «مِنْ مِثْلِهِ» is genitive through من. «وَادْعُوا شُهَداءَكُمْ» is accusative by the verb; it is the plural of شهيد. One says شاهد and شهيد, like قادر and قدير.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
«فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا»: it may be asked: how did «إن» enter upon «لم», when one governing word does not enter upon another?
The answer is that «إن» here does not govern in the wording, so it enters upon «لم» just as it enters upon the past verb; for it does not govern in لم just as it does not govern in the past. So the meaning of «إن لم تفعلوا» is "if you leave off doing".
Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: they made [the verb] jussive with لم only because it is a negation, so it resembled «لا» in your saying لا رجلَ في الدار; the vowel was dropped by it just as the tanwīn is dropped from nouns. Someone else said: it made [the verb] jussive because it resembled the conditional إن, since it turns the imperfect into the past just as «إن» does [the reverse]; and [the conditional] needs an answer, so it resembled the inception (ibtidāʾ), and the inception brings the nominative to nouns, which is most proper to nouns; likewise [the vowel] is dropped with «إن», because what is most proper to verbs is quiescence. [Translator's note: the argument is compressed in the source; translated as written.]
«وَلَنْ تَفْعَلُوا» is accusative (subjunctive) by لن; the sign of its accusative is the dropping of the nūn. The accusative and jussive are alike in verbs because both are secondary, and they are in the status of the accusative and genitive in nouns. It is reported from al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, that the original of «لن» is «لا أن». [Translator's note: the source prints «لا»; al-Khalīl's well-known view is لا أن, and the following words «وإن ردّ» appear to contain the displaced «أن».] Sībawayh refuted this, saying: if that were so, زيدًا لن أضربَ would not be permissible. Abū ʿUbayda said: some of the Arabs make [the verb] jussive with لن just as with لم.
«فَاتَّقُوا النَّارَ» is the apodosis of the condition, in the fāʾ and what follows it. The dialect of Tamīm and Asad is «فتَقُوا النّار», and Sībawayh reported تَقَى يَتْقِي. «النَّارَ» is its object; «الَّتِي» is its naʿt (adjective). «وَقُودُهَا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «النَّاسُ» is the khabar (predicate), and «وَالْحِجارَةُ» is conjoined to them. «أُعِدَّتْ» is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the sign of the feminine; it is quiescent according to the Basrans because it is a particle that came for a meaning; according to the Kufans, since you gave ḍamma to the tāʾ of the speaker, fatḥa to the tāʾ of the masculine addressee and kasra to the tāʾ of the feminine, and this tāʾ was left, the absence of a mark became its mark. [Translator's note: the source says «ضممت تاء المخاطب», "the tāʾ of the addressee", for what is evidently the speaker's tāʾ; translated by the evident sense.] The noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] is latent in أعدّت. «لِلْكافِرِينَ» is genitive through the lām, which is zāʾida (redundant). [Translator's note: so in the source.]
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «الَّتِي وُقُودُهَا» with ḍamma on the wāw. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: الوَقود with fatḥa on the wāw is the firewood, and الوُقود with ḍamma is the act [of burning]. Abū Jaʿfar said: on this basis it must be read only وَقودها with fatḥa on the wāw, because the meaning is "its firewood". However, al-Akhfash said — and it is reported — that some Arabs make الوَقود and الوُقود both mean the firewood and the maṣdar; he held that the former is more common, and said:
just as الوَضوء is the water and الوُضوء is the maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
«أَنَّ» is in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "that they have" (بأنّ لهم). Al-Kisāʾī and a group of the Basrans said:
«أنّ» is in the position of the genitive by an implied bāʾ. «جَنَّاتٍ» is in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of أنّ; the tāʾ has kasra according to the Basrans because it is a sound plural, so its genitive and accusative had to be the same, as was the case in the masculine. «تَجْرِي» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of الجنات, and it is nominative because it is an imperfect verb; the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness with it. «الْأَنْهارُ» is nominative by تجري. «كُلَّما» is an adverbial (ẓarf). «قالُوا هذَا»: [هذا] is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الَّذِي» its khabar (predicate); [Translator's note: the source prints «والَّذِينَ», evidently for «الَّذِي»;] it may also be [that the sense is] "this is the one which". «رُزِقْنا مِنْ قَبْلُ»: [قبل] is a ghāya (an end-word), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because something has been dropped from it; it is an adverbial that takes the accusative and genitive when intact, so when it was weakened by the omission it was given a vowel that did not otherwise attach to it. It is also said: it was given ḍamma because it is the furthest of the vowels. «وَأُتُوا بِهِ» is fuʿilū from أتيت. «مُتَشابِهاً» is as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «أَزْواجٌ» is nominative as mubtadaʾ.
«مُطَهَّرَةٌ» is a naʿt. The singular of الأزواج is زوج. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: the Arabs hardly ever say زوجة.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Farrāʾ reported that زوجة is said, and recited: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 10-
إنّ الذي يمشي يحرش زوجتي ... كماش إلى أسد الشّرى يستبيلها
(Whoever goes about stirring up my wife against me is like one who walks up to the lions of al-Sharā to provoke them.)
«وَهُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ and «خالِدُونَ» its khabar; the adverbial phrase is non-operative (mulghā). Outside the Qur'an, the accusative خالدين as a ḥāl would be permissible.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
«إِنَّ اللَّهَ» is the noun (ism) of «إنّ», and the clause is the khabar (predicate). The dialect of Tamīm and Bakr ibn Wāʾil is «لا يستحي» with a single yāʾ, and so read Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Shibl. There are two views on it. Al-Khalīl said:
the first yāʾ was made quiescent as [the middle letter] is made quiescent in «باع», and the second was made quiescent because it is the final radical. Sībawayh said — and [he said] "someone else said" —: since [the ḥāʾ] had kasra and they were two yāʾs, they dropped one and shifted its vowel onto the ḥāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the explanation of al-Khalīl's view is that the original is استحيا; he weakened it in two respects: he weakened the first yāʾ as one says استباع, and weakened the second as one says يرمي, then dropped the first so that two quiescent letters would not meet. This is very far-fetched, because they avoid weakening from two sides. The other view is that of Sībawayh. I heard Abū Isḥāq say: when Sībawayh says, after the view of al-Khalīl, "and someone else said", he means only himself; he does not name himself after al-Khalīl, out of reverence for him. The explanation of Sībawayh's view is that the original is استحيا; they used it so often that they dropped the first yāʾ and shifted its vowel onto the ḥāʾ, so it resembled iftaʿala, as in اقتضى, and they inflected it as that is inflected, saying استحى يستحي.
«أَنْ يَضْرِبَ» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "of striking" (من أن يضرب).
«مَثَلًا» is accusative by يضرب. «ما بَعُوضَةً»: there are three ways for its accusative. «ما» may be redundant and «بعوضة» a badal (substitute) from مثلا. «ما» may be in the position of the accusative as an indefinite noun, with «بعوضة» a naʿt (adjective) of ما — and it can properly be a naʿt because it means "small". The third way is the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, who said: the implied sense is "to strike a parable of what is between a gnat [and above it]"; «بين» was dropped and بعوضة was given its case, and the fāʾ is in the sense of «إلى», i.e. "up to what is above it". The meaning of "I struck him a parable" (ضربت له مثلا) is "I represented a likeness for him"; and "these structures are of one ḍarb", i.e. of one pattern. «فَما فَوْقَها» is conjoined to the first «ما». It is reported that Ruʾba was heard reading «إنّ الله لا يستحي أن يضرب مثلا مّا بعوضةٌ» in the nominative; this is the dialect of Tamīm. He made «ما» in the sense of الذي and made بعوضة nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject); the omission with «ما» is uglier than with الذي, because الذي has only one aspect and the noun [with it] is longer.
«فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا»: «الذين» is
nominative as mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is what follows the fāʾ. The fāʾ is indispensable in the answer of «أَمَّا» because it carries the meaning of condition, i.e. "whatever the case may be, the matter is thus". «فَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ»: «أنّ» is in the position of the accusative by يعلمون; the hāʾ is its noun and الحق its khabar. «مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ» is genitive through من.
«وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا»: the dialect of Tamīm and Banū ʿĀmir is «أيما»; they substitute a yāʾ for one of the two mīms out of dislike of doubling. On this basis the verse of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa is recited: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 11-
رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشّمس عارضت ... فيضحى وأيما بالعشيّ فيخصر
(She saw a man who, when the sun faces him, is scorched, and in the evening is chilled.)
«فَيَقُولُونَ ماذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِهذا مَثَلًا»: if you wish you may make «ما» and «ذا» a single thing in the position of the accusative by أراد — Ibn Kaysān said this is better — or, if you wish, make «ما» a complete noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, with «ذا» in the sense of الذي as the khabar; the implied sense would be "what is it that Allah intended by this as a parable?" Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab said: «مثلا» is accusative by qaṭʿ ("cutting off"). Ibn Kaysān said: it is accusative as a tamyīz (specification) that has occurred in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). «يُضِلُّ» is an imperfect verb.
«كَثِيراً» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «وَيَهْدِي»: the yāʾ in it is quiescent because combining it with a yāʾ and a kasra was felt heavy. «وَما يُضِلُّ بِهِ إِلَّا الْفاسِقِينَ» [is accusative] because the verb falls upon them; the implied sense is "He does not lead anyone astray by it except the transgressors". It is not permissible to make them accusative as the excepted (mustathnā), because exception occurs only after the sentence is complete.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
«الَّذِينَ» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of الفاسقين; or, if you wish, you may make it in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who". «يَنْقُضُونَ» is an imperfect verb, and the latent pronoun in it refers back to الذين. «عَهْدَ اللَّهِ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «مِنْ بَعْدِ مِيثاقِهِ»: you made بعد genitive through من, and ميثاقه [genitive] by بعد [being put in construct] with it; it means "His binding (إيثاقه)". Ibn Kaysān said: it is a noun that conveys the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as al-Quṭāmī said: [al-Wāfir metre] 12-
أكفرا بعد ردّ الموت عنّي ... وبعد عطائك المائة الرّتاعا
(Ingratitude, after you warded off death from me, and after your giving of the hundred grazing camels?)
«وَيَقْطَعُونَ» is conjoined to ينقضون. «ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ»: «ما» is in the position of the accusative by يقطعون. The maṣdar is قطيعة [for severing ties]; "I cut the rope" قطعًا; "I crossed the river" قُطوعًا; and "the birds migrated" (قطعت الطير) قِطاعًا and قَطاعًا, when they go out from one land to another; "the people were afflicted by قُطْعة" when their water ran low; and "a man has قُطْع", i.e. breathlessness. «وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ» is conjoined to يقطعون. «أُولئِكَ» is a mubtadaʾ.
«هُمُ» is a second mubtadaʾ; «الْخاسِرُونَ» is the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first. If you wish, «هم» may be redundant, with الخاسرون the khabar.

nahhas-irab:243-243.t:
أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ: this «ترى» is from seeing with the heart, i.e. "have you not become aware of this, and has knowledge of it not come to you?" The original has a hamza, which was dropped for lightness. حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ: the noun of إنّ and its khabar (predicate); the lām is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis.
The original of ذي is ذوى, so know this; the Qur'an has uttered it on the original form; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ذَواتا أَفْنانٍ [al-Raḥmān: 48]. The meaning of لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ here is that He revived these people after death and showed them the greatest sign.

nahhas-irab:244-244.t: وَقاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: a command, i.e. do not flee as those fled. وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ: the noun of «أنّ» and its khabar (predicate), i.e. He hears your words if you say what those said, and knows what you intend by them.

nahhas-irab:245-245.t: مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ: «من» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «ذا», and «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of ذا, or, if you wish, a badal (substitute). يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ: a noun standing for the maṣdar [Translator's note: so in the source; the remark evidently belongs to قَرْضاً, the noun used in place of the maṣdar إقراض]. The original sense of قرضت is "I cut"; from it the scissors are called المقراضان, and from it is تَقْرِضُهُمْ ذاتَ الشِّمالِ [al-Kahf: 17]. So the meaning of أقرضت الرجل is "I gave the man a piece of my wealth". «فيضاعفُه له»: conjoined to يقرض, or, if you wish, resumptive. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿraj read فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ in the accusative, and this is also narrated from ʿĀṣim; the accusative is as the answer to the interrogative. أَضْعافاً: with the meaning of the maṣdar. كَثِيرَةً: its naʿt. وَاللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْصُطُ: if you wish you may change the sīn into ṣād, because a ṭāʾ follows it.

nahhas-irab:246-246.t: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ: it has been said: الملأ are the nobles, because they are fully capable (مليئون) of what they undertake. إِذْ قالُوا لِنَبِيٍّ لَهُمُ ابْعَثْ لَنا مَلِكاً نُقاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request, and the request is in the form of a command. «نقاتلُ في سبيل الله» in the nominative is also permitted, meaning "we fight", i.e. "for we are among those who fight". Whoever read with the yāʾ, «يقاتلُ», the proper aspect for him is the nominative, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of ملك. قالَ هَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ: Abū Ḥātim said: there is no valid aspect for «عسِيتم», though al-Ḥasan, Nāfiʿ and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read it; had it been so, «فعسِي الله» would have been read. Abū Jaʿfar said: Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sikkīt and others reported that «عسِيت» is a dialect form, but a poor one. So when he says «عسى الله» and then says «فهل عسِيتم», he has used both dialects together, though he ought to read with the more eloquent of the two, which is fatḥa on the sīn. إِنْ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتالُ: a condition. أَلَّا تُقاتِلُوا: in the position of accusative (manṣūb). Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. "might you perhaps not fight?" [Translator's note: the source reads «هل عسيتم مقاتلة», "might you perhaps … fighting", without the negation.] قالُوا وَما لَنا أَلَّا نُقاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: al-Akhfash said: «أن» is redundant (zāʾida). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is construed on the meaning, i.e. "what has prevented us", as you say «ما لك ألّا تصلي» (what is with you that you do not pray?), i.e. what has prevented you. It has also been said: the meaning is "what is there for us in not fighting in the way of Allah?", and this is the best of them. «وأنزل» is in the position of accusative [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a corruption of «وأن», i.e. أنْ with its verb is in the position of accusative]. وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنا مِنْ دِيارِنا وَأَبْنائِنا: i.e. our offspring were taken captive. تَوَلَّوْا إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ: an exception.

nahhas-irab:247-247.t:
وَقالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طالُوتَ مَلِكاً: «طالوت» is an object; it is not fully declined because it is foreign, and likewise داوود and جالوت. Had you named a man طاووس or راقود you would decline it, even though both are foreign. The difference between this and the former is that you say الطاوس, admitting the alif and lām into it, so it becomes established in Arabic, and this does not happen with the other. «ملك السماوات» is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is «مَلِكاً», and the phrase «ملك السماوات» does not occur in it].
قالُوا أَنَّى: from which direction; it is in the position of accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). الْمُلْكُ عَلَيْنا: nominative, the noun of يكون. وَنَحْنُ أَحَقُّ بِالْمُلْكِ مِنْهُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). وَلَمْ يُؤْتَ: jussive (majzūm) by لم, which is why the alif was dropped from it. سَعَةً مِنَ الْمالِ: the predicate of [the verb] whose agent is not named [i.e. its second object].

nahhas-irab:248-248.t: إِنَّ آيَةَ مُلْكِهِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ التَّابُوتُ: the noun of «إنّ» and its khabar (predicate), i.e. the coming of the Ark. The sign in the Ark, according to what is narrated, is that a moaning used to be heard from it; when that was heard they marched towards them, and when the moaning died down they did not march and the Ark did not move. The dialect of the Anṣār is التابوه, with hāʾ, and it is narrated from Zayd ibn Thābit «التّبوت». فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ: nominative as mubtadaʾ or by the [implied] istiqrār (being located). The sakīna may be something in it, and likewise the remnant; and it may be that the Ark itself is a sakīna and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left. The original of آل is أهل.

nahhas-irab:249-249.t:
Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «إنّ الله مبتليكم بنهْر» with sukūn on the hāʾ. It is a dialect form, except that the Kufans say: any word whose second or third letter is one of the guttural letters, you may make it quiescent or give it a vowel, such as نهز, سمع and لحم; whereas the Basrans follow, in this, the usage heard from the Arabs and do not go beyond it. إِلَّا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةً: «من» is in the position of accusative by the exception. Abū ʿUbayd chose إِلَّا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةً with ḍamma on the ghayn; he said: because He did not say «غرف»; it is only the water itself.
Abū Jaʿfar said: fatḥa here is more fitting, because الغُرفة with ḍamma is the fill of a thing, applying to little and much, while الغَرفة with fatḥa is a single time, and the context of the speech indicates a small amount, so fatḥa is more appropriate. As for Abū ʿUbayd's saying that he chose it because He did not say «غرف», it is rejected, because غرف and اغترف have the same meaning.
فَشَرِبُوا مِنْهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ: an exception. فَلَمَّا جاوَزَهُ: the hāʾ refers to the river. «هو» is emphasis (tawkīd). «والذين» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the pronoun latent in جاوزه. It is ugly to conjoin to a nominative pronoun without emphasising it, because it has no [overt] sign, so it is as if you conjoined to part of the verb; when it is emphasised, the emphasis being the emphasised thing itself, it is as if you brought it as a detached [pronoun]. قالُوا لا طاقَةَ لَنَا الْيَوْمَ بِجالُوتَ: طاقة and طوق are two nouns meaning ability (الإطاقة). كَمْ مِنْ فِئَةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ: if you dropped «من», the preferred choice would be the genitive, because it is a declarative [كم].

nahhas-irab:251-251.t: وَعَلَّمَهُ مِمَّا يَشاءُ: it has been said: among that is the speech of birds and the making of coats of mail. «ولولا دفاع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض»: the name of Allah the Exalted is in the position of nominative by the verb, [the sense being] "were it not that He repels" (لولا أن يدفع), and (دفاع) is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh. «الناس» are objects. «بعضهم» is a badal (substitute) of الناس. «ببعض» is in the position of the second object according to Sībawayh, and in his view it is like your saying «ذهبت بزيد», where «بزيد» is in the position of an object. Abū ʿUbayd chose وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ and rejected «دفاع», saying: because no one contends with Allah the Exalted. Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading «دفاع» is good and sound, and there are two views on it. Abū Ḥātim said: دافع and دفع are the same; he holds that it is like طارقت النعل (I patched the sandal). Better than this, and it is the view of Sībawayh, because Sībawayh said: "on that basis is «دفعت الناس بعضهم ببعض»", then said: "and like that is «ولولا دفاع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض»". Abū Jaʿfar said: thus I read with Abū Isḥāq in Sībawayh's Book, namely that «دفاع» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of دفع, as you say «حسبت الشيء حسابا» and «لقيته لقاء». This is better, so that دفاع and دفع are both maṣdars of دفع.

nahhas-irab:252-252.t:
تِلْكَ: mubtadaʾ (subject). آياتُ اللَّهِ: its khabar (predicate); or, if you wish, it is a badal (substitute), and the khabar is نَتْلُوها عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ. وَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ: the khabar of «إنّ», i.e. "and you are indeed a messenger".
Here ends the second part of the book I'rab al-Qur'an. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and may Allah bless the Prophet Muhammad and his noble, righteous family, and grant them peace.

nahhas-irab:253-253.t:
تِلْكَ الرُّسُلُ فَضَّلْنا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ: «تلك» is for the feminine of the group, and it is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). «بالرسل» [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is «الرُّسُلُ»] is a naʿt (adjective), and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is the clause. According to the Kufans, «تلك» is nominative by the resumptive [pronoun], as you say «زيد كلّمت أباه» (Zayd, I spoke to his father). مِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَلَّمَ اللَّهُ: the hāʾ was dropped because of the length of the noun; the meaning is «من كلّمه الله» (whom Allah spoke to), and «من» is for Moses ﷺ; He said: وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسى تَكْلِيماً [al-Nisāʾ: 164]. وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجاتٍ: here, according to the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Shaʿbī and Mujāhid, it is Muhammad ﷺ: «بعثت إلى الأحمر والأسود وجعلت لي الأرض مسجدا وطهورا ونصرت بالرعب مسيرة شهر وأحلّت لي الغنائم وأعطيت الشفاعة» ("I was sent to the red and the black; the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification; I was aided by awe [cast into the enemy] a month's journey away; spoils were made lawful for me; and I was given intercession"). Among that are the Qur'an, the splitting of the moon, the tree's speaking to him, his feeding a great many people from a few dates, and the flowing of the milk of Umm Maʿbad's ewe after it had dried up. وَآتَيْنا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّناتِ: two objects. وَلكِنِ اخْتَلَفُوا: the nūn was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; outside the Qur'an it may be dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 55-
فلست بآتيه ولا أستطيعه ... ولاك اسقني إن كان ماؤك ذا فضل
(I will not come to it, nor am I able to; but give me to drink, if your water has a surplus.)
فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَفَرَ: «من» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ or by the ṣifa [i.e. the prepositional phrase].

nahhas-irab:132-132.t:
(وَوَصَّى) carries the meaning of intensity/frequency, and if that is so the reading with it becomes unlikely [Translator's note: so in the source]; better than this is that وصّى and أوصى have one meaning, like كرمنا and أكرمنا. (إِبْراهِيمُ) is nominative by its verb.
(وَيَعْقُوبُ) is conjoined to it. (يا بَنِيَّ) is a vocative in a genitive construct; this is the yāʾ of the first person, and here only fatḥa is permissible on it, because if it were vowelless two vowelless letters would meet; similar to it is ﴿بِمُصْرِخِيَّ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 22]. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): «إنّ» takes kasra because أوصى and قال are one [in meaning]; it has also been said: by an implied "saying". (فَلا تَمُوتُنَّ) is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition, emphasised with the heavy nūn; the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. (إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:133-133.t:
(أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَداءَ): the khabar (predicate) of كان; it is a diptote because it contains the alif of the feminine, which entered to mark the femininity of the group, just as the hāʾ enters. (إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ): a fronted object. Its fronting has a benefit according to Sībawayh's doctrine; he said: because they put first that whose explanation is more important to them and with whose explanation they are more concerned, even though both are important to them and concern them. (ما تَعْبُدُونَ): «ما» is in the position of the accusative by تعبدون. (قالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلهَكَ وَإِلهَ آبائِكَ إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ): in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute); they are diptotes because they are foreign. Al-Kisāʾī said: if you like, you may decline إسحاق as a triptote, deriving it from السحق, and decline يعقوب, deriving it from the bird [Translator's note: يعقوب, the male partridge]. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever reads "وإله أبيك" has two ways of taking it. One is that he made it singular because he disliked making Ishmael a father, since he was an uncle. Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not follow, because the Arabs call the uncle "father"; moreover it is far-fetched, because it implies "the god of Ishmael and the god of Isaac", so that he [Isaac], who is his nearest father, is removed from the sequence of Abraham, and the far-fetchedness of this is not hidden. There is another way according to Sībawayh's doctrine: أبيك is a plural. Sībawayh related أبون and أبين, as [the poet] said:
[al-Wāfir] 28-
فقلنا أسلموا إنّا أخوكم
(So we said: "Submit, for we are your brothers.")
Sībawayh and al-Khalīl say that the plural of إبراهيم and إسماعيل is براهيم and سماعيل, and this is the view of the Kufans; they also related براهمة and سماعلة, the hāʾ replacing the yāʾ, as one says زنادقة; and they related براهم and سماعل. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is a mistake, because the hamza is not in a place where it is an augment [Translator's note: so in the source]; rather I say أباره and أسامع, and أباريه and أساميع are also possible. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] allowed براه, as one says بريه in the diminutive. The plural of إسحاق is أساحيق; the Kufans related أساحقة and أساحق; likewise يعقوب: يعاقيب, يعاقبة and يعاقب. As for إسرائيل, we know of no one who allows dropping the hamza from its beginning; one only says أساريل, and the Kufans related أسارلة and أسارل. The rule in all of this is that it should be given a sound plural, so one says إبراهيمون, إسحاقون, إسماعيلون and يعقوبون, and with the sound plural there is no [internal] change. (إِلهاً واحِداً): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or, if you like, as a badal, because an indefinite noun may be substituted for a definite one and a definite for an indefinite.

nahhas-irab:134-134.t: (تِلْكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أُمَّةٌ): its khabar (predicate); (قَدْ خَلَتْ): a naʿt (adjective) of أمة, or, if you like, it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and أمة is a badal (substitute) from تلك. (لَها ما كَسَبَتْ): «ما» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, or by the adjectival phrase (al-ṣifa) according to the view of the Kufans. (وَلَكُمْ ما كَسَبْتُمْ) is the same.

nahhas-irab:135-135.t: (وَقالُوا كُونُوا هُوداً): the plural of هائد; it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "people of Judaism", as one says قوم عدل ورضى ("people of justice and approval"). (تَهْتَدُوا) is the apodosis of the imperative. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned «قل بل ملّة إبراهيم» in the book before this one. Abū Isḥāq said: (حَنِيفاً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: this is a mistake; one may not say جاءني غلام هند مسرعة ("Hind's servant came to me, she hurrying"); rather it is accusative by أعني ("I mean"). Someone else said: the meaning is "rather we follow Abraham in this state."

nahhas-irab:136-136.t: (وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنا) is in the position of the genitive, i.e. "and that which was sent down to us"; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun in أنزل.

nahhas-irab:137-137.t: (فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ): the kāf and the hāʾ-mīm are in the position of the accusative, two objects. Outside the Qur'an فسيكفيك إياهم is permissible. Likewise, when the verb passes to the first object it becomes strong, so it may come to the second as a detached pronoun.

nahhas-irab:138-138.t: (صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ): al-Akhfash said: i.e. Allah's religion; he said: it is a badal (substitute) from ملّة. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a good view, because the command and prohibition of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and His proofs mingle with the mind as dye mingles with a garment.

nahhas-irab:139-139.t: (قُلْ أَتُحَاجُّونَنا فِي اللَّهِ): the coming together of two vowelled letters of the same kind is permissible because the second is as if separate. Ibn Muḥayṣin read "قل أتحاجّونّا" with assimilation; this is permissible, except that it contradicts the written text (al-sawād), and it also combines two vowelless letters, which is permissible because the first is a letter of prolongation and softness. It may also be assimilated with a hint of the fatḥa [Translator's note: so in the source; the following example concerns a hint of ḍamma], as ﴿لا تَأْمَنَّا﴾ [Yūsuf: 11] was read with ishmām (lip-rounding) of the ḍamma. «أتحاجّونا» with the second nūn dropped is also permissible, as Nāfiʿ read ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 54].

nahhas-irab:140-140.t:
They said: al-Kisāʾī read (أَمْ تَقُولُونَ) with tāʾ. It is a good reading, because the speech is consistent, i.e. "Do you argue with us, or do you say…?" The reading with yāʾ is of two separate utterances, and «أم» then means «بل» ("rather"). Al-Akhfash said: as you say إنها لإبل أم شاء ("they are camels — or rather sheep"). «إنّ» takes kasra because the speech is reported. The Tribes (al-asbāṭ) among the children of Jacob are like the tribes (al-qabāʾil) among the children of Ishmael. (هُوداً) is the khabar (predicate) of كان, and the khabar of «إنّ» is the clause. Outside the Qur'an هود may be nominative as the khabar of «إنّ», with كان made inoperative.
Here ends the first part of the book «Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān». Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and may Allah bless the Prophet Muḥammad and his noble and righteous family and grant them peace.
Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl said about His saying, Mighty and Majestic:

nahhas-irab:142-142.t: (سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهاءُ مِنَ النَّاسِ): the plural of سفيه; for women [the plural is] سفايه [Translator's note: i.e. سفائه]. (ما وَلَّاهُمْ): «ما» is a complete noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ولّاهم is in the position of the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:143-143.t:
(جَعَلْناكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطاً): two objects. Al-Qutabī said: what is best is called وسط because excess and falling short are both blameworthy, and the best of affairs is their middle. Abū Isḥāq said: the Arabs liken a tribe to a valley and a plain, and the best of a valley is its middle; likewise the best of a tribe is its middle. It has also been said: the way of the eminent man and the chief is not to be at the edge but to be in the middle, and so the excellent is called وسط. (لِتَكُونُوا): the lām of kay (purpose), i.e. "in order that you be". (شُهَداءَ) is a khabar (predicate), and it may be conjoined. Al-Zuhrī read (إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ) [Translator's note: his reading is لِيُعْلَمَ, passive, as the following explanation shows; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading]; «من» is in the position of the nominative in this reading because it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The broken plural of قبلة is قبل, and the sound plural قبلات; the kasra may be replaced by a fatḥa, and the kasra may be dropped [Translator's note: i.e. قِبِلات, قِبَلات, قِبْلات]. (وَإِنْ كانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً): al-Farrāʾ holds that «إن» and the lām mean «ما» and «إلّا»; the Basrans say: it is the heavy «إنّ» lightened, so a verb may follow it, and the lām is obligatory with it so that it does not resemble the «إن» that means «ما». Al-Akhfash said: i.e. "and the qibla was indeed a great matter." (لَرَؤُفٌ) is on the pattern فَعُول, and the Kufans read (لَرَؤُفٌ) [Translator's note: their reading is لَرَؤُفٌ on the pattern فَعُل, without the wāw; the printed form shows the same vocalisation for both]. Al-Kisāʾī related that the dialect of Banū Asad is لرأف on the pattern فَعْل.

nahhas-irab:144-144.t: (شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ): an adverbial of place, as you say تلقاءه ("towards it") and جهته ("in its direction"). The adverbial is accusative because it is an extra element (faḍla), like the direct object, and also because the action occurs in it.

nahhas-irab:145-145.t: (وَلَئِنْ أَتَيْتَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ بِكُلِّ آيَةٍ ما تَبِعُوا قِبْلَتَكَ): because they disbelieved after the truth had become clear to them, so signs do not benefit them. Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: «إن» has been answered with the apodosis of «لو», because the meaning is "even if you brought those who were given the Book every sign, (ما تَبِعُوا قِبْلَتَكَ)"; likewise «لو» is answered with the apodosis of «إن»: you say لو أحسنت أحسن إليك ("if you had done good, I do good to you"). Similar to it is ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا لَظَلُّوا﴾ [al-Rūm: 51], i.e. "if We had sent a wind". Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is a mistake according to Sībawayh's doctrine, which is the truth, because the meaning of «إن» is different from the meaning of «لو». That is, with إن one thing becomes necessary because another becomes necessary — you say إن أكرمتني أكرمتك ("if you honour me, I will honour you") — while the meaning of «لو» is that one thing is precluded because another is precluded; so neither of them takes the place of the other. The meaning is "and if you bring those who were given the Book every sign, they will not follow your qibla." Sībawayh said: the meaning [in al-Rūm] is "and if We send a wind and they see it yellowed, they will surely continue (ليظلنّ)."

nahhas-irab:146-146.t: (الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَعْرِفُونَهُ) is in the position [Translator's note: the source breaks off here, evidently "in the position of the khabar"], i.e. they recognise the change [of qibla], or they recognise the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

nahhas-irab:147-147.t: (الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by an implied mubtadaʾ. It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read الحق in the accusative, i.e. "they know the truth." As for the one in «al-Anbiyāʾ», ﴿الْحَقَّ فَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 24], we know of no one who read it other than in the accusative. The difference between them is that the one in Sūrat al-Baqara begins a verse, while the one in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ does not.

nahhas-irab:148-148.t:
(لِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيها):
the hāʾ and alif are the first object, and the second object is omitted, i.e. "he turns towards it his face" or "himself"; the meaning is "he turns his face in its direction." The Arabs omit [the noun governed] by كلّ and بعض, saying كلّ منطلق, i.e. "every man [is departing]"; the implied form is "and for every nation and people of a religion." (اسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْراتِ):
an imperative, i.e. hasten to what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has commanded you, namely facing towards the Sacred House.

nahhas-irab:150-150.t: (وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ وَحَيْثُ ما كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ لِئَلاَّ يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيْكُمْ حُجَّةٌ إِلاَّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ فَلا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِي وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ) (150). (لِئَلَّا): if you like, you may lighten the hamza. (يَكُونَ) is accusative by أن; if you like, you may say تكون because of the femininity of الحجّة. This is attached to what preceded of the argument against them. (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ) is in the position of the accusative, an exception not of the same kind as what precedes (disjunctive exception), as the Arabs say: ما نفع إلّا ما ضرّ ("it did no good, only harm") and ما زاد إلّا ما نقص ("it did not increase, only decreased"). (وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكُمْ): al-Akhfash said: it is conjoined to لئلّا يكون, i.e. "and in order that I complete My favour upon you."

nahhas-irab:151-151.t:
(كَما أَرْسَلْنا فِيكُمْ): Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned its meaning. The kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "that you may be guided with a guidance like [Our] sending"; the implied form may be "and that I complete My favour upon you with a faith like [Our] sending"; the kāf may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "and that I complete My favour upon you in this state"; and the implied form may be "so remember Me with a remembrance like…". «ما» is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and أرسلنا is its ṣila (relative clause). (يَتْلُوا) is an imperfect verb [Translator's note: "فعل مستقبل" in the source]; its wāw originally has ḍamma, but the ḍamma is felt heavy and is also preceded by a ḍamma, so it was dropped. It is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of رسول.
(وَيُزَكِّيكُمْ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ) are conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:152-152.t: (فَاذْكُرُونِي): an imperative. (أَذْكُرْكُمْ) carries the meaning of a conditional apodosis, and that is why it is jussive. (وَلا تَكْفُرُونِ) is a prohibition, and that is why the nūn [of the indicative] has been dropped from it; the yāʾ has been dropped because it is the end of a verse, and keeping it is good outside the Qur'an.

nahhas-irab:153-153.t: I.e. from acts of disobedience [Translator's note: the Qur'anic words commented on, presumably وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ, are not quoted in the source]. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:154-154.t: (وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ يُقْتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْواتٌ): by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); and likewise (بَلْ أَحْياءٌ).

nahhas-irab:155-155.t: (وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ): this wāw has fatḥa according to Sībawayh because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. Others said: when it was joined to the nūn it became like خمسة عشر (fifteen) [i.e. indeclinable on fatḥa].

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: «كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ» … «كَيْفَ» is a noun in the position of the accusative; it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. Its norm would have been to be quiescent, because it has the sense of the interrogative and so resembled particles; fatḥa was chosen for it because of the yāʾ. «تَكْفُرُونَ» is an imperfect verb. «بِاللَّهِ» is genitive through the bāʾ. «وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْواتاً»: the implied sense is "while you had been (وقد كنتم) dead"; then قد was omitted. «أَمْواتاً» is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم. «فَأَحْياكُمْ»: the kāf and mīm are in the position of the accusative by the verb, and likewise «ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ». «ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ» is an imperfect verb.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: «هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «ما» is in the position of the accusative. «جَمِيعاً» is, according to Sībawayh, accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «ثُمَّ اسْتَوى»: the people of the Hijaz pronounce it with tafkhīm (full open vowel), and the people of Najd with imāla (inclining the vowel), to show that it is of the yāʾ-final verbs. «إِلَى السَّماءِ» is genitive through إلى. «فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ»: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd said: سبع is accusative as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ and nūn, i.e. "so He fashioned seven heavens". Abū Jaʿfar said: in my view it may be "so He fashioned of them", as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: «وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ» [al-Aʿrāf: 155], i.e. "of his people". «وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
«وَإِذْ قالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ»: Abū ʿUbayda said [that it is redundant; but] «إِذْ» is a noun, an adverbial of time, not one of the words that are added. [Translator's note: the source reads only «قال أبو عبيدة: إذ اسم …»; Abū ʿUbayda's well-known view is that إذ here is redundant, and the following words appear to be the rebuttal. The bracketed words are the translator's.] Abū Isḥāq said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the creation of mankind and others, so the implied sense is "He began their creation when your Lord said". «لِلْمَلائِكَةِ» is genitive through the lām, and the hāʾ is for the femininity of the group.
«إِنِّي جاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ»: the yāʾ is in the position of the accusative; جاعل is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. The original is إنّني; the nūn was dropped because two nūns met. «فِي الْأَرْضِ» is genitive through في. «خَلِيفَةً» is accusative by جاعل; dropping the tanwīn is not permissible because of the separation — if the object came right after it, dropping the tanwīn would be permissible. «خليفة» may be in the sense of an agent (fāʿil), i.e. one who succeeds those angels who were before him on earth, or those who were before him other than angels, as is reported; and «خليفة» may be in the sense of a patient (mafʿūl), i.e. one who is succeeded, as one says ذبيحة in the sense of مذبوحة.
«قالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ»: an imperfect verb.
