[Translator's note: the source has «فقل», a misprint for «فعل».] «فِيها مَنْ يُفْسِدُ»: [من] is in the position of the accusative by تجعل, and «فيها» stands in the place of the second object. «يفسد» is according to the wording [singular]; outside the Qur'an يفسدون would be permissible according to the meaning.
«وَيَسْفِكُ» is conjoined to it. It is reported from al-Aʿraj «وَيَسْفِكَ الدِّماءَ» in the accusative; he makes it the answer to the interrogative with the wāw. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «وَيَسْفِكُ» for the accusative variant.] The singular of الدماء is دم. No noun consists of two letters without something having been dropped from it; what is dropped from it is a yāʾ, and it has been pronounced in its original form. The poet said: [al-Wāfir metre] 13-
فلو أنّا على حجر ذبحنا ... جرى الدّميان بالخبر اليقين
(If we were both slaughtered on a stone, the two bloods would flow to give the certain news.)
«وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ»: assimilating the nūn into the nūn is not permissible, so that two quiescent letters do not meet.
«قالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ»: whoever gives the yāʾ a vowel, saying «إنّيَ اعلم ما», dislikes that a noun of a single letter should be quiescent; whoever makes it quiescent says: it is joined to what precedes it. «(أعلم)» is an imperfect verb; it may also be a noun in the sense of an active participle (fāʿil), as one says الله أكبر in the sense of كبير, and as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 14-
لعمرك ما أدري وإنّي لأوجل ... على أيّنا تغدو المنيّة أوّل
(By your life, I do not know — and I am indeed afraid — upon which of us death will come first.)
Assimilating the mīm into the mīm is permissible. «ما» is in the position of the accusative by أعلم if you make it a verb; if you make it a noun, «ما» may be in the position of the genitive by the construct, or in the position of the accusative with the tanwīn dropped because it is a diptote.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
«وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْماءَ كُلَّها»: «آدَمَ» and «الْأَسْماءَ» are the two objects of علّم. آدم is a diptote when definite by the consensus of the grammarians, because it is on the pattern afʿal and is definite; according to the Basrans nothing is barred from full declension except for two causes. If you make آدم indefinite, and it is not an adjective, al-Khalīl and Sībawayh do not decline it fully, but al-Akhfash Saʿīd declines it fully, because [he holds] it was barred from full declension only because it was an adjective on the pattern of the verb; so when it is not an adjective he declines it fully. Abū Isḥāq said: the correct view is that of Sībawayh; no distinction is made between the adjective and other words, because it is exactly the same. The plural of آدم when it is an adjective is أُدْم; if it is not an adjective its plural is آدمون and أوادم, and so with the whole class. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned «عرضهم» in the book before this one.
«فَقالَ أَنْبِئُونِي»: [its alif is] a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ), because it is from أنبأ يُنبئ. If you lighten the hamza you say أنبئوني "between-between"; if you substitute it you say أنبوني, like أعطوني. «بِأَسْماءِ هؤُلاءِ»: «بأسماء» is genitive through the bāʾ, and «هؤلاء» is in the position of the genitive by the construct, except that it is indeclinable (mabnī) on kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; it is indeclinable like هذا. There are several ways [of pronouncing] it when you lengthen it. If you wish, you may lighten the second hamza and fully pronounce the first.
This is the best way according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, and it is the reading of Nāfiʿ, so you say «هؤُلاءِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ» [with the second hamza lightened to a yāʾ-like sound]. Nothing else is permissible on the view of one who lightens the second; the proof of this is that they agree on reading His saying, Majestic and Mighty, «مِنَ النِّساءِ إِلَّا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ» [al-Nisāʾ: 22] in a single way from Nāfiʿ, and there is no difference between the two. If you wish, you may lighten the first and fully pronounce the second, saying «هؤُلاءِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ»; if you wish, you may fully pronounce both, saying «هؤلاء ان»; if you wish, you may lighten both; and if you wish, you may lighten [i.e. drop] the first, saying «هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين» — this is the view of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ on two hamzas when they agree [in vowel]. [Translator's note: the source does not vowel or otherwise mark these variants, so the printed forms look identical.] Tamīm and some of Asad and Qays shorten «هؤلا», so in their dialect it is «هاؤلا إن كنتم». Al-Aʿshā said: [al-Khafīf metre] 15-
هؤلا ثمّ هؤلا كلّا أعطيت ... نعالا محذوّة بمثال
(These, and then these — to all you gave sandals cut to a single pattern.)
Some of the Arabs say «هؤلا», dropping the alif and the hamza. [Translator's note: the intended form, unvowelled in the source, is presumably هُؤُلُ or similar.]
«إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ»:
«كنتم» is in the position of the jussive through the condition, and what precedes it is in the position of its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) according to Sībawayh; according to Abū al-ʿAbbās the apodosis is omitted, the meaning being "if you are truthful, then inform Me". Abū ʿUbayd said: some of the exegetes held that «إن» is in the sense of «إذ»; this is a mistake — it is the «أن» with fatḥa that is in the sense of «إذ»; this one is in the sense of condition.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t:
«قالُوا سُبْحانَكَ» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; it conveys the sense of "we glorify You with a glorification". Al-Kisāʾī said: it is accusative because it is not qualified; he said: it may also be accusative as a vocative in construct.
«لا عِلْمَ لَنا» is like «لا ريب فيه». «لا عِلْمٌ لَنا» is also permissible, making «لا» in the sense of ليس — the meaning is "there is not". [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «لا عِلْمَ» for the nominative variant.] «إِلَّا ما عَلَّمْتَنا»: «ما» is in the position of the nominative, as you say «لا إله إلّا الله»; the predicate of the tabriʾa [the lā of generic negation] is like the predicate of the mubtadaʾ (subject). The accusative is permissible when the sentence is complete, according to the basic rule of exception.
«إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ»: «أنت» is in the position of the accusative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf. If you wish it may be nominative as mubtadaʾ, with العليم its khabar (predicate) and the clause the khabar of إنّ; or, if you wish, it is a fāṣila ("separator") with no position — the Kufans say ʿimād ("support") — and the alif-lām [word, العليم] is in the position of the nominative. «الْحَكِيمُ» is a naʿt (adjective) of العليم.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
«قالَ يا آدَمُ»: a single [non-construct] noun in the vocative. «أَنْبِئْهُمْ»: the ḍamma was dropped from the hamza because it is an imperative. If you lighten the hamza you say أنبيهم, as you say ذيب and بير; if you substitute for it you say أنبهم, as Zuhayr said: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 16-
جريء متى يظلم يعاقب بظلمه ... سريعا وإن لا يبد بالظّلم يظلم
(Bold: whenever he is wronged he punishes the wrong swiftly, and if he is not wronged first, he does wrong.)
«بِأَسْمائِهِمْ» is genitive through the bāʾ. «فَلَمَّا أَنْبَأَهُمْ»: if you lighten [the hamza] you make it between hamza and alif, and if you substitute you say «أنباهم» with a pure alif. «قالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ»: the original is أَقْوُل; the vowel of the wāw was shifted onto the qāf, so the qāf took ḍamma, and the wāw was dropped because it and the lām were both quiescent; the lām was made quiescent for the jussive.
«إِنِّي»: the alif has kasra because what comes after القول ("saying") is an independent sentence. Sībawayh held that some of the Arabs treat القول like الظنّ ("thinking"), and this is the report of Abū al-Khaṭṭāb; on this basis [one would say] «أنّي أعلم». Al-Kisāʾī said: I have seen that when the yāʾ meets a hamza the Arabs like to use fatḥa, so they say «إنّيَ أعلم». «أعلم» is permissible [as a noun], because it is from علم. [Translator's note: the source reads «ويجوز اعلم لأنه من علم», which is ambiguous; it may refer to أعلم as an elative noun, as in verse 30.] «غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ» is accusative by أعلم, and likewise «ما تُبْدُونَ»; «وَما كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ» is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
«وَإِذْ قُلْنا لِلْمَلائِكَةِ» is genitive through the lām, which is zāʾida (redundant). [Translator's note: so in the source.] «اسْجُدُوا» is an imperative, which is why the nūn is dropped from it; you give the hamza ḍamma when you begin with it because it is from يسجُد. It is reported from Abū Jaʿfar [Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ] that he read «للملائكةُ اسجدوا» [with ḍamma on the tāʾ]; this is a solecism (laḥn) that is not permissible. The best that has been said about it is what is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, who said:
I reckon that Abū Jaʿfar used the genitive and then gave it a trace (ishmām) of ḍamma, to show that the beginning [of the next word] is with ḍamma, just as «وَغِيضَ الْماءُ» [Hūd: 44] is read with a pointing towards the ḍamma, to show that it is of the verb whose agent is not named. [Translator's note: the source prints «للملائكة» without the variant vowel.]
«لِآدَمَ» is in the position of the genitive through the lām, except that it is a diptote. «فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ» is accusative as the excepted (mustathnā); nothing else is permissible according to the Basrans because [the sentence] is affirmative; the Kufans permitted the nominative. «إبليس» is a foreign noun, which is why it has no tanwīn. Abū ʿUbayda held that it is Arabic, derived from أبلس ("he despaired"), except that it is a diptote because it has no counterpart.
«أَبى وَاسْتَكْبَرَ»: أبى يأبى إباءً. This is a rare word that came on the pattern faʿala yafʿalu without having one of the guttural letters. Abū Isḥāq said: I heard Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq say: my view on it is that the alif resembles the guttural letters. Abū Jaʿfar said: I do not know that Abū Isḥāq related any grammar from Ismāʿīl other than this word. «وَكانَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ» is genitive through من, and the nūn has fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
«وَقُلْنا يا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الْجَنَّةَ»: «أنت» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent pronoun. Outside the Qur'an it is permissible, though far-fetched, [to say] قم وزيد ("stand, you and Zayd"). «وَكُلا مِنْها»: the nūn was dropped because it is an imperative, and the hamza was dropped because of frequent use; dropping it is anomalous. Sībawayh said: some of the Arabs say أُوكُل, giving it in full. «رَغَداً» is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "an abundant eating". Ibn Kaysān said: it may also be a maṣdar in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).
«حَيْثُ شِئْتُما»: «حيث» is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it differs from its sisters among the adverbials in that it is not put in construct [with a single noun], so it resembled قبل and بعد when they stand alone, and was given ḍamma. Sībawayh reported that some Arabs give it fatḥa in every case. Al-Kisāʾī said: ḍamma is the dialect of Qays and Kināna, and fatḥa the dialect of Banū Tamīm. Al-Kisāʾī said: Banū Asad put it in the genitive in the position of the genitive and in the accusative in the position of the accusative. He said «سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ» [al-Aʿrāf: 182] [i.e. مِن حيثِ in their dialect], and it is given ḍamma and fatḥa. One also says حَوْث.
«وَلا تَقْرَبا» is a prohibition, which is why the nūn is dropped. «هذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ» is in the position of the accusative by تقربا. The hāʾ in هذه is a substitute for a yāʾ, the original being هذي. I know of no hāʾ of the feminine in Arabic preceded by kasra other than the hāʾ of هذه. Some of the Arabs say هاتا هند, and some say هاتي هند; Sībawayh reported هذهْ هند with the hāʾ quiescent. «الشَّجَرَةَ» is a naʿt of هذه. «فَتَكُونا» is the answer to the prohibition, accusative (subjunctive) by an implied «أن» according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; al-Jarmī held that the fāʾ is what governs the subjunctive. «فتكونا» may also be jussive, conjoined to تقربا.

nahhas-irab:254-254.t:
مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خُلَّةٌ وَلا شَفاعَةٌ: the clause is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of اليوم. If you wish you put [the nouns] in the nominative and say لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خُلَّةٌ وَلا شَفاعَةٌ, making «لا» mean «ليس», or as mubtadaʾ (subject); and if you wish you put them in the accusative by way of tabriʾa (the lā of generic negation). We have mentioned this before. وَالْكافِرُونَ: mubtadaʾ.
هُمُ: a second mubtadaʾ. الظَّالِمُونَ: the khabar (predicate) of the second. Or, if you wish, «هم» is redundant (zāʾida), for separation (faṣl), and الظالمون is the khabar of الكافرون.

nahhas-irab:255-256.t:
اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). [هو] is nominative, construed on the meaning, i.e. "there is no god but He" (ما إله إلّا هو); «لا إلهٌ إلّا هو» is also permitted [Translator's note: the source writes the form unvowelled]. Outside the Qur'an «لا إله إلّا إيّاه» is permitted, accusative as an exception.
Abū Dharr said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which of the Qur'an revealed to you is greatest, and he said: اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ. Ibn ʿAbbās said: the noblest verse in the Qur'an is the Verse of the Throne. الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ: a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; or, if you wish, a badal (substitute) of هو; or, if you wish, a khabar after a khabar; or, if you wish, with an implied mubtadaʾ. Outside the Qur'an the accusative of praise is permitted. We have mentioned the exegesis and the original form of it. لا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلا نَوْمٌ: the original is وسنة; the wāw was dropped as it was dropped from يسن. وَلا نَوْمٌ: the wāw is for conjunction and «لا» is for emphasis (tawkīd). لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ: in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ or by the ṣifa [i.e. the prepositional phrase]. مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ: «من» is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «ذا» is its khabar; and «الذين» [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is «الذي»] is a naʿt of ذا, or, if you wish, a badal. It is not permitted for «ذا» to be redundant as it is made redundant with «ما», because «ما» is vague (mubham), so «ذا» was added to it on account of its resemblance to it. One says كُرسيّ and كِرسيّ. «لا إكراهُ في الدين» is permitted [Translator's note: the source writes the form unvowelled]. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «قد تبيّن الرَّشَد من الغيّ» [Translator's note: the source prints the vowelling الرَّشَدُ for both], and the same is narrated from al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī.
One says رشَد يرشُد رُشدا and رشِد يرشَد رَشَدا when one attains what one loves, and غوى is its opposite, as the poet said:
[al-Ṭawīl] 56-
ومن يغو لا يعدم على الغيّ لائما
(And whoever goes astray will not lack someone to blame him for his straying.)
فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالطَّاغُوتِ: jussive (majzūm) by the condition. الطاغوت is feminine, and we have mentioned its meaning and what has been said about it. وَيُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ: conjoined. فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقى: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The plural of الوثقى is الوثق, like الفضلى and الفضل.

nahhas-irab:257-257.t: وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: mubtadaʾ (subject). أَوْلِياؤُهُمُ: a second mubtadaʾ, and بِالطَّاغُوتِ [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «أَوْلِياؤُهُمُ الطَّاغُوتُ»] is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of the first.

nahhas-irab:258-258.t:
أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْراهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ أَنْ آتاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ إِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ رَبِّيَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ قالَ أَنَا أُحْيِي وَأُمِيتُ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي بِالشَّمْسِ مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِها مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ (258)
أَلَمْ تَرَ: the yāʾ was dropped for the jussive, and we have mentioned the ṣila (relative clause). أَنْ آتاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ: in the position of accusative (manṣūb), i.e. «لأن» (because). قالَ أَنَا أُحْيِي وَأُمِيتُ: the noun is «أن»; when you say «أنا» or «أنه», the alif and the hāʾ are to show the vowel. One does not say «أنا فعلت» with the alif pronounced, except anomalously in poetry; yet Nāfiʿ pronounced the alif and read قالَ أَنَا أُحْيِي وَأُمِيتُ, and there is no valid aspect for it. فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ: «الذي» is in the position of nominative, the noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. One says بُهِت الرجل, بَهِت and بَهُت when he is cut short and falls silent, bewildered. [Translator's note: the source writes the three forms unvowelled.]

nahhas-irab:259-259.t:
أَوْ كَالَّذِي مَرَّ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ: it has been said: [it is called] قرية because people gather in it, from their saying قريت الماء, i.e. I collected it. وَهِيَ خاوِيَةٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). فَأَماتَهُ اللَّهُ مِائَةَ عامٍ: an adverb (ẓarf). قالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتَ: the people of Kufa read «قال كم لبتّ», assimilating the thāʾ into the tāʾ because of its closeness to it; pronouncing it distinctly is better. [Translator's note: the source prints the Kufan reading with the same spelling as the standard text.]
فَانْظُرْ إِلى طَعامِكَ وَشَرابِكَ لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ: the soundest of what has been said about it is that its meaning is "the years have not changed it". Whoever reads لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ وَانْظُرْ with the hāʾ pronounced in continuous recitation says: the original of سنة is سنهة, and he says سنيهة in the diminutive, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 57-
ليست بسنهاء ولا رجبيّة
(She is neither one barren from the years of drought, nor one propped up [for her heavy load].)
So he dropped the ḍamma for the jussive. Whoever reads «لم يتسنّ وانظر» says: in the diminutive it is سنيّة, and he dropped the alif for the jussive, and he pauses on the hāʾ, saying «لم يتسنّه», the hāʾ being to show the vowel. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «لم يسّنّ», assimilating the tāʾ into the sīn. وَانْظُرْ إِلَى الْعِظامِ كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُها: it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan «كيف نَنشُرها» [Translator's note: the source prints the same spelling as the standard text; the variant discussed is with rāʾ], and the meaning is the same, as one says رجع and رجعته, except that the meaning known in the language is أنشر الله الموتى فنشروا (Allah revived the dead, so they came back to life). It has also been said: ننشرها is like نشرت الثوب (I spread out the garment), as al-Aʿshā said: [al-Sarīʿ] 58-
حتّى يقول النّاس ممّا رأوا ... يا عجبا للميّت النّاشر
(So that people say, from what they have seen: how wondrous is the dead man who comes back to life!)

nahhas-irab:260-260.t: وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ رَبِّ: outside the Qur'an «ربّي», keeping the yāʾ, is permitted. Whoever drops it says: the vocative is a place of omission; and whoever keeps it says: it is a noun. When it is dropped, the preferred choice is that I pause without ishmām (lip-rounding), saying «ربّ», so this resembles the single [proper noun]. أَرِنِي: we have mentioned it. كَيْفَ: in the position of accusative (manṣūb), i.e. in what state do You revive the dead? وَلكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي: i.e. I asked You so that my heart may be at rest. ثُمَّ اجْعَلْ عَلى كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِنْهُنَّ جُزْءاً: Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "then put on every mountain a part of each one". Abū Jaʿfar and ʿĀṣim read (جزءا) on the pattern فُعُل. يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْياً: accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:261-261.t: فِي كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī said: some read «في كل سنبلة مائةَ حبة» [Translator's note: the source prints the same vowelling as the standard text; the variant is the accusative], on [the implied verb] «أنبتت مائة حبة» (it produced a hundred grains). Likewise some read «وللذين كفروا بربهم عذابَ جهنم» [al-Mulk: 6] on وَأَعْتَدْنا لَهُمْ عَذابَ السَّعِيرِ [al-Mulk: 5], [i.e.] "and We have prepared for those who disbelieve the punishment of Hell".

nahhas-irab:263-263.t: قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e. "kind speech is better and more fitting". It may also be that قول معروف is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "what you were commanded is kind speech". وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُها أَذىً: this is a difficulty which the parsing clarifies. «بالمغفرة» [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is «وَمَغْفِرَةٌ»] is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ. The meaning, and Allah knows best, is: and an act leading to forgiveness is better than a charity followed by injury; its implied form in Arabic is «وفعل مغفرة». It may also be like your saying: "Allah's favour to you is more than the charity you make a reproach of", i.e. Allah's forgiveness is better than this charity of yours which you make a reproach of.

nahhas-irab:264-264.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُبْطِلُوا صَدَقاتِكُمْ بِالْمَنِّ وَالْأَذى: the Arabs call what is given with reproach "a black hand", what is given without being asked "a white hand", and what is given upon being asked and without reproach "a green hand". كَالَّذِي يُنْفِقُ مالَهُ رِئاءَ النَّاسِ: the kāf is in the position of accusative (manṣūb), i.e. "a nullifying like that of one who spends his wealth to be seen by people", so it is a naʿt (adjective) of the omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial). فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرابٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhrī read «كمثل صفَوان» with a vowel on the fāʾ, and Quṭrub reported «مثل صفوان» [Translator's note: the source writes the forms unvowelled]. Al-Akhfash said: صفوان is a collective of صفوانة. He said: some said صفوان is a singular, like حجر (stone). Al-Kisāʾī said: صفوان is a singular, and its plural is صفوان, صُفيّ and صِفيّ. Abū Jaʿfar said: صفْوان and صفَوان may be either plural or singular, but the more fitting is that it be singular, because of His saying «عليه تراب فأصابه وابل», even though it is permitted to treat a plural as masculine; a thing is not taken out of its category except by a decisive proof. As for what al-Kisāʾī reported regarding the plural, it is not sound on true examination; rather صفوان is the plural of صفا, and صفا means صفوان. Its parallel is ورل and ورلان, أخ and إخوان, and كرى and كروان, as the poet said: [al-Wāfir] 59-
لنا يوم وللكروان يوم ... تطير البائسات وما نطير
(We have a day and the curlews have a day: the wretched birds fly, and we do not fly.)
The weak [view] in Arabic says: كروان is the plural of كروان, and صفيّ is the plural of صفا, like عصا and عصيّ. Al-Kisāʾī said: they are the smooth stones on which nothing grows. فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْداً: al-Kisāʾī said: one says صلِد يصلَد صلَدا with a vowel on the lām, and it is صلْد with sukūn; it is anything on which nothing grows. From it is جبين أصلد (a bald, smooth forehead). Al-Aṣmaʿī recited: [al-Rajaz] 60-
براق أصلاد الجبين الأجله
(Shining, with a smooth-browed, bald forehead.)

nahhas-irab:265-265.t: وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمُ ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِ اللَّهِ: [ابتغاء] is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). وَتَثْبِيتاً مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ: conjoined to it. كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ: Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī read (بِربوة) with kasra on the rāʾ, and al-Ḥasan, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī read بِرَبْوَةٍ with fatḥa on the rāʾ. Al-Akhfash said: one also says «برَباوة» and «برِباوة», all of it from الرابية (hillock), and its verb is ربا يربو. فَإِنْ لَمْ يُصِبْها وابِلٌ فَطَلٌّ: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. "then what strikes it is a drizzle". Abū Jaʿfar said: the lexicographers reported: وبلت and أوبلت, طلّت and أطلّت.

nahhas-irab:156-156.t: (الَّذِينَ إِذا أَصابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ): a naʿt (adjective) of الصابرين. (قالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ): al-Kisāʾī said: if you like, you may give the alif kasra, because of its [frequent] use and great frequency. Al-Farrāʾ said: the nūn in «إنا لله» takes kasra only because of their frequent use of it. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for al-Farrāʾ's view, it is an ugly mistake, because the nūn does not take kasra, and what precedes an alif is never vowelled with kasra or ḍamma. As for al-Kisāʾī's view, it is permissible if he means that the alif is inclined (mumāla) towards kasra; but that it should actually take kasra is impossible, because an alif never takes a vowel at all. The alif in «إنا لله» was inclined (imāla) only because of the kasra of the lām in لله; if you said إنّا لزيد شاكرون ("we are grateful to Zayd"), inclining the alif would not be permissible, because it is in another word; it was permissible in إنا لله because, since it is so frequent, the two things became like one thing. If you like, you may pronounce it full (tafkhīm). The original is إنّنا; one of the two nūns was dropped for lightness. Likewise (وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ راجِعُونَ).

nahhas-irab:157-157.t: (أُولئِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَواتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ). (وَرَحْمَةٌ) is conjoined to صلوات. (وَأُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ, (هُمُ) a second mubtadaʾ, (الْمُهْتَدُونَ) the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first. If you like, «هم» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis and «المهتدون» is the khabar.

nahhas-irab:158-158.t:
(إِنَّ الصَّفا): the noun of «إنّ»; its alif is changed from a wāw. (وَالْمَرْوَةَ) is conjoined to الصفا.
(مِنْ شَعائِرِ اللَّهِ) is the khabar (predicate). [شعائر] is derived from شعرت به ("I perceived it"); it has a hamza because it is on the pattern فعائل, the yāʾ having no original vowel, so it was replaced by a hamza. (فَمَنْ) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), (حَجَّ) is in the position of the jussive by the condition, and its apodosis and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is (فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِما). The original is يتطوّف; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ. It is related [as being read] (أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِما) in the intensive form [Translator's note: the printed form shows the same vocalisation as the standard reading]. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: أن يطّاف, the original likewise being يتطاف, with the tāʾ assimilated into the ṭāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: we know of no one who read «أن يطوف بهما». (وَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ خَيْراً فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ): a past verb in the position of the jussive by the condition. This is the reading of the people of Medina and of Abū ʿAmr, and it is good because it has no weakness. The reading of the people of Kufa, except ʿĀṣim: (وَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ خَيْراً) [Translator's note: their reading is يَطَّوَّعْ, as the following explanation shows; the printed form is the standard reading], the original being يتطوع with the tāʾ assimilated into the ṭāʾ. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ): the noun of إنّ. (شاكِرٌ) is its khabar; (عَلِيمٌ) is a naʿt (adjective) of شاكر, or, if you like, a second khabar.

nahhas-irab:159-159.t:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ): the noun of «إنّ». Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read (مِنْ بَعْدِ ما بَيَّنَّاهُ لِلنَّاسِ) [Translator's note: his reading is بَيَّنَهُ, as the following explanation shows] in the sense of "Allah made it clear." (أُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّهُ) is in the position of the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إنّ». لعنه means "He drove him away", i.e. removed him far from His mercy, as al-Shammākh said: [al-Wāfir] 29-
ذعرت به القطا ونفيت عنه ... مقام الذّئب كالرّجل اللّعين
(I startled the sandgrouse there and drove from it the wolf's standing-place, like the outcast man.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: we have explained the meaning of «وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّاعِنُونَ», because someone might say: the people of their own religion do not curse them. One of the best things said about it is that the people of their religion do in reality curse them, because they curse the wrongdoers, and these are among the wrongdoers.

nahhas-irab:160-160.t: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا): accusative as an exception.

nahhas-irab:161-161.t:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the noun of «إنّ»; (أُولئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ) is the khabar (predicate). Al-Ḥasan read "أولئك عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعون" [i.e. in the nominative], and this is conjoined to the position, as you say:
عجبت من قيام زيد وعمرو ("I wondered at the standing of Zayd and ʿAmr", with عمرو nominative), because the position of «زيد» is the nominative, the meaning being "that Zayd stood"; and the meaning is: "upon those is that Allah, the angels and all people curse them."

nahhas-irab:164-164.t: (إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِما يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ وَما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِنْ ماءٍ فَأَحْيا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها وَبَثَّ فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّياحِ وَالسَّحابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ) (164). (لَآياتٍ) is in the position of the accusative as the noun of إنّ.

nahhas-irab:165-165.t:
(مِنَ) [Translator's note: i.e. مَنْ] is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَتَّخِذُ) is according to the wording [i.e. singular]; outside the Qur'an يتخذون is permissible. (يُحِبُّونَهُمْ) is according to the meaning [i.e. plural]; outside the Qur'an يحبّهم is permissible. It is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يتّخذ; if you like, it is a naʿt (adjective) of أنداد; and if you like, it is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of من, taking من as indefinite, as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 30-
فكفى بنا فضلا على من غيرنا ... حبّ النّبيّ محمّد إيّانا
(It suffices us as a distinction over anyone other than us that the Prophet Muḥammad loves us.)
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ): mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate). (كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ) is by way of clarification. (وَلَوْ يَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا) with yāʾ is the reading of the people of Mecca, the people of Kufa and Abū ʿAmr, and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd; the people of Medina and the people of Syria read "ولو ترى الذين" with tāʾ. There is a difficulty and an omission in the verse. Abū ʿUbayd held that he chose the reading with yāʾ because it is related in the exegesis that the meaning is: "if those who did wrong could see in this world the punishment of the Hereafter, they would know that power belongs to Allah." Abū Jaʿfar said: it is related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said:
this exegesis that Abū ʿUbayd brought is far-fetched, and his wording of it is not good, because he supposes «ولو يرى الذين ظلموا العذاب», as though he made it something doubtful, whereas Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made it certain. Rather the implied form — and it is the view of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash Saʿīd — is: "if those who did wrong could see that power belongs to Allah", يرى meaning "know", i.e. "if they knew the reality of Allah's power"; so يرى operates on «أن», and the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, i.e. "they would have seen clearly the harm of their taking gods", as He said ﴿وَلَوْ تَرى إِذْ وُقِفُوا عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 27] and ﴿وَلَوْ تَرى إِذْ وُقِفُوا عَلى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 30], and no apodosis came for لو. Al-Zuhrī and Qatāda said:
leaving it implied is more forceful as a threat. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever reads "ولو ترى" with tāʾ takes «الذين» as the object [Translator's note: the source has "مفعولين", "two objects"], and also omits the apodosis of «لو»; «أن» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "because power belongs to Allah." Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 31-
وأغفر عوراء الكريم ادّخاره ... وأعرض عن شتم اللّئيم تكرّما
(I forgive the noble man's ugly word, to keep him in store, and I turn away from the base man's insult out of nobility.)
i.e. "to keep him in store". Al-Farrāʾ allowed «أنّ» to be in the position of the accusative by an implied "seeing". Whoever gave it kasra and read "إنّ القوة لله وإنّ الله" made it a new beginning (istiʾnāf). (جَمِيعاً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذابِ) is conjoined to the first أنّ.

nahhas-irab:166-166.t: (إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا): the hamza in اتبعوا takes ḍamma in harmony with the tāʾ, and the second tāʾ takes ḍamma to show that it is a verb whose agent is not named (passive). If it is said: the rule for a passive verb is that its first letter takes ḍamma as the sign, so how is it that the third letter here takes ḍamma as the sign? The answer is that the rule for the passive verb is that the first of its vowelled letters takes ḍamma; since the first tāʾ is vowelless, the hamza was brought in for it, and the second [tāʾ] was vowelled because it is the first of the vowelled letters. (وَرَأَوُا الْعَذابَ): the wāw takes ḍamma because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.

nahhas-irab:167-167.t: (لَوْ أَنَّ لَنا كَرَّةً): «أن» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "if that were to happen." (فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ) is the answer to the wish. (كَما): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "[that we may] disown [them] as…", and it may also be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (كَذلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "the matter is thus"; it may also be in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a showing like that". (يُرِيهِمُ اللَّهُ أَعْمالَهُمْ): two objects. (حَسَراتٍ عَلَيْهِمْ): accusative as a ḥāl.

nahhas-irab:168-168.t: (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُوا مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلالًا طَيِّباً): a naʿt (adjective) of an object, i.e. "something lawful" or "a lawful eating." Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned (خطوات الشيطان).

nahhas-irab:169-169.t: (وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to His saying (بِالسُّوءِ وَالْفَحْشاءِ).

nahhas-irab:170-170.t: (وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا): the wāw takes fatḥa because it is a conjunctive wāw.

nahhas-irab:171-171.t: (وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have examined its meaning thoroughly. (بِما لا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعاءً): accusative by يسمع. (وَنِداءً) is conjoined to it. (صُمٌّ): i.e. "they are deaf."

nahhas-irab:173-173.t: (إِنَّما حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ): accusative by حرّم, and «ما» is restraining (kāffa). You may also make it mean الذي (that which) and put الميتة, الدم and لحم الخنزير in the nominative. (فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ): the nūn takes ḍamma because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, making the ḍamma follow the ḍamma; kasra is also permissible according to the basic rule for the meeting of two vowelless letters. Abū Jaʿfar [the Medinan reader] read (فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ) with kasra on the ṭāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. اضْطِرَّ; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading], because the original is اضطرر, and when it was assimilated the vowel of the rāʾ was cast onto the ṭāʾ. (فمن اضّرّ) is also permissible: since the ḍād may not be assimilated into the ṭāʾ, the ṭāʾ was assimilated into the ḍād. It is also permissible to change the ḍād into ṭāʾ without assimilation and then assimilate the ṭāʾ into the ṭāʾ, so you say فمن اطّر — this is outside the Qur'an. (غَيْرَ باغٍ): «غير» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The original is باغي; the vowel on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless, and the tanwīn is vowelless, so the yāʾ was dropped because of its vowellessness and that of the tanwīn. It was the more fitting to be dropped because the tanwīn is a sign [of inflection], and before the yāʾ there is something that indicates it [the kasra]. Likewise (وَلا عادٍ).

nahhas-irab:174-174.t: (الَّذِينَ): the noun of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is (أُولئِكَ ما يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ إِلَّا النَّارَ).

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
«فَأَزَلَّهُمَا» is from أزللته فزلّ ("I made him slip and he slipped"), and «فأزالهما» is from أزلته فزال ("I removed him and he went"). [Translator's note: the source prints «فأزالها», evidently for «فأزالهما», the reading of Ḥamza.] «الشَّيْطانُ» is nominative by its verb. «وَقُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا»: the alif of اهبطوا was dropped because it is a connecting alif, and the alif of قلنا was dropped in pronunciation because it and the hāʾ after it are both quiescent. «بَعْضُكُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «عَدُوٌّ» its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied sense being "and this is your state". The wāw [of the ḥāl] was omitted because there is a resumptive pronoun in the sentence, as one says رأيتك السماءُ تمطر عليك ("I saw you, the sky raining on you"). It may be asked: how did He say «عدوّ» and not أعداء? There are two answers to this. One is that بعض and كلّ may be predicated with a singular, and this is in the Qur'an: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said «وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ» [Maryam: 95], and said «وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ داخِرِينَ» [al-Naml: 87]. The other answer is that عدوّ is used in the singular in the place of the plural; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said «وَهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ بِئْسَ لِلظَّالِمِينَ» [al-Kahf: 50], meaning أعداء. «وَلَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ»: [مستقرّ] is nominative as mubtadaʾ.
«وَمَتاعٌ» is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
«فَتَلَقَّى آدَمُ»: [آدم] is nominative by its verb. «كَلِماتٍ» is accusative by the verb. Al-Aʿmash read «فَتَلَقَّى آدَمُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ» with assimilation [آدمّ مّن]. «إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ»: «هو» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), «التواب» its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of إنّ. «هو» may also be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ, and it may be a fāṣila ("separator"). Abū Ḥātim reported that Abū ʿAmr, ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read «إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ» with assimilation [إنّهُّو], and that this is not permissible because between the two hāʾs there is a wāw in pronunciation, though not in writing. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh permitted dropping this wāw, and recited: [al-Wāfir metre] 17-
له زجل كأنّه صوت حاد ... إذا طلب الوسيقة أو زمير
(He has a clamour as though it were the voice of a camel-driver seeking the driven herd, or a piping.)
On this basis the assimilation is permissible.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
«قُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا مِنْها جَمِيعاً»: [جميعا] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ held that it may be said: this was addressed only to Adam ﷺ and Iblīs himself, meaning [also] his offspring, so it is as though He addressed them [all], as He said «قالَتا أَتَيْنا طائِعِينَ» [Fuṣṣilat: 11], i.e. "we came with what is in us". Someone other than al-Farrāʾ said: it may be an address to Adam, peace be upon him, Eve and the serpent; it may be to Adam and Eve, because two are a group; and it may be that Iblīs was joined with them in the address.
«فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ»: «ما» is redundant — the Kufans say ṣila ("connective"), and the Basrans say it carries the meaning of emphasis. «يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ» is in the position of the jussive through the condition, and the nūn is emphatic; when «ما» is added it is likened to the lām of the oath, so it is good to bring the nūn. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is the fāʾ in His saying «فَمَنْ تَبِعَ هُدايَ». «من» is in the position of the nominative and «تبع» in the position of the jussive through the condition; «فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ» is its apodosis. Al-Kisāʾī said: «فلا خوف عليهم» is the apodosis of both conditions together.
ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, ʿĪsā and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «فمن تبع هُدَيَّ». Abū Zayd said: this is the dialect of Hudhayl; they say هُدَيَّ and عَصَيَّ. The grammarians recited: [al-Kāmil metre] 18-
سبقوا هويّ وأعنقوا لهواهم ... فتخرّموا ولكلّ جنب مصرع
(They preceded my desire and hastened to their own desire, and were carried off — every side has its place of falling.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: the reason for this, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh — and this is the meaning of what they said — is that the norm with the yāʾ of the possessive is that what precedes it has kasra; since the alif could not take a vowel, a yāʾ was put before it as a compensation for the change.
Al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «فَلا خَوْفَ عَلَيْهِمْ» [with fatḥa, without tanwīn]. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «فَلا خَوْفٌ»; the variant is evident from the following discussion.] The preferred choice among the grammarians is the nominative with tanwīn, because the second [clause, ولا هم يحزنون] is definite and can only be nominative, so they chose the nominative in the first as well, so that the speech would be of one pattern.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
«وَالَّذِينَ» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). «كَفَرُوا» is part of its ṣila (relative clause). «وَكَذَّبُوا» is conjoined to كفروا.
«بِآياتِنا» is genitive through the bāʾ. «أُولئِكَ» is a mubtadaʾ and «أَصْحابُ النَّارِ» its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of الذين.
«وَهُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
«يا بَنِي» is a vocative in construct; the sign of the accusative in it is the yāʾ, and the nūn was dropped from it for the construct. The singular is ابن; its original is بَنَيٌ, and it is also said بَنَوٌ; if nothing had been dropped from it, one would say بَنًا, as one says عصا. Whoever says what was dropped from it is a wāw argues from their saying البُنُوّة; but this is no proof, because they have [also] said الفتوّة. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: in my view what was dropped from it is a yāʾ, as though it were from بنيت ("I built").
«إِسْرائِيلَ» is in the position of the genitive, except that it is a diptote because it is foreign. One also says إسرائل without yāʾ and with a hamza with kasra, and إسراأَل with a hamza with fatḥa; and Tamīm say إسرائين with nūn.
«اذْكُرُوا»: the nūn was dropped from it because it is an imperative; the alif was dropped because it is a connecting alif, and you give it ḍamma when beginning because it is from يذكُر. «نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي»: giving the yāʾ a vowel is more common in the speech of the Arabs when an alif-lām meets it; if you make it quiescent you drop it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «التي» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of نعمتي.
«أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ» is part of its ṣila (relative clause). «وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي» is an imperative. «أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ» is the answer to the imperative, jussive because it carries the meaning of requital (mujāzāt). Al-Zuhrī read «أُوَفِّ بِعَهْدِكُمْ» for intensiveness. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «أُوفِ» for al-Zuhrī's variant.] One also says وفى بالعهد. «وَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ»: the verb falls upon the nūn and yāʾ, and the yāʾ was dropped because it is the end of a verse. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «فارهبوني» with the yāʾ, and likewise فاتّقوني. «وإيّاي» is accusative by an implied verb; and this is the preferred choice with command, prohibition, negation and interrogation.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
«وَآمِنُوا» is conjoined. «بِما» is genitive through the bāʾ. «أَنْزَلْتُ» is its ṣila (relative clause), and the resumptive pronoun is omitted because of the length of the noun, i.e. "in what I sent down (أنزلته)". «مُصَدِّقاً» is as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «لِما» is genitive through the lām. «مَعَكُمْ» is the ṣila of ما.
«وَلا تَكُونُوا» is jussive through لا, which is why the nūn is dropped from it. «أَوَّلَ» is the khabar (predicate) of تكونوا; it has no tanwīn because it is in construct. If it were not in construct, tanwīn would be permissible, taking it as a noun that is not an adjective; ḍamma without tanwīn would be permissible, taking it as a ghāya (end-word); and leaving off the tanwīn would be permissible, taking it as an adjective. He said «كافِرٍ» and not كافرين; there are two views on this:
al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ held that it is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "the first who disbelieves in it"; and Sībawayh reported:
هو أظرف الفتيان وأجمله ("he is the most charming of the youths and the most handsome of him"), because he would be saying, as it were, "he is the most charming youth and the most handsome of him". [Translator's note: the source reads «لأنه قد كان يقول كأنه يقول», with an apparently duplicated phrase; translated by sense.] The other view is that the implied sense is "and do not be the first party (فريق) disbelieving in it". Imāla in كافر is the dialect of Tamīm, and it is good, because it is genitive, the rāʾ counts as two letters, and there is no preventing letter in it. The preventing letters are khāʾ, ghayn, qāf, ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ and ẓāʾ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: in «أوّل» there is some subtle Arabic, which we shall explain, if Allah wills. «أول», according to Sībawayh, is one of the words from which no verb is pronounced; it is on the pattern afʿal, its ʿayn and fāʾ being wāw. According to him no verb is pronounced from it only so that it would not be weakened from two sides; this is the view of the Basrans. The Kufans said: it is from وأل; and it may be from أأل. If it is from وأل, the original is أَوْأَل, then the hamza was lightened and you said أوّل, as you lighten the hamza of خطيئة and say خطيّة. If it is from أأل, the original is أأْوَل, then a wāw was substituted for the alif because it is a diptote. [Translator's note: the last reasoning is translated as written; its connection to the diptote status is not explained in the source.]

nahhas-irab:42-42.t:
«وَلا تَلْبِسُوا» is a prohibition, which is why the nūn is dropped from it. «الْحَقَّ» is the object. «بِالْباطِلِ» is genitive through the bāʾ. «وَتَكْتُمُوا» is conjoined to «تَشْتَرُوا» [Translator's note: so in the source; in this verse وتكتموا is conjoined to تلبسوا, while تشتروا belongs to the previous verse], or, if you wish, it is an answer to the prohibition, in the position of the accusative by an implied أن according to the Basrans, the implied sense being "let there not be from you buying and concealing". The Kufans say: it is accusative by ṣarf ("diversion"). Its explanation is that it is diverted from the particle that governed what precedes it, and it is not made a new start so as to be nominative, so nothing remains but the accusative; the wāw and the fāʾ were likened to كي and governed the accusative, as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil metre] 19-
لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله ... عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم
(Do not forbid a habit while you do the like of it — great shame is on you if you do.)
«وَأَنْتُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «تَعْلَمُونَ» is an imperfect verb in the position of the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: «وَأَقِيمُوا» is an imperative, and likewise «وَآتُوا» and «وَارْكَعُوا».

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: «أَتَأْمُرُونَ» is an imperfect verb. «وَتَنْسَوْنَ» is conjoined to it. «أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ» is the same.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
«وَاسْتَعِينُوا» is an imperative. «بِالصَّبْرِ» is genitive through the bāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned several views on it in the book before this, and the soundest is that it is patience in refraining from sins, and that «وَالصَّلاةِ» is like His saying «وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكالَ» [al-Baqara: 98] [i.e. a particular mentioned after the general]. One says "so-and-so is صابر", i.e. [refraining] from sins; and whoever is patient in refraining from sins has been patient in obedience. He, Majestic and Mighty, said: «إِنَّما يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ» [al-Zumar: 10]. One who is patient in a calamity is not called صابر [absolutely]; one says only "patient in such-and-such"; when you say صابر without qualification, it is as we have mentioned.
«وَإِنَّها لَكَبِيرَةٌ» is the noun (ism) of «إنّ» and its khabar (predicate). Outside the Qur'an وإنه would be permissible, and وإنهما would be permissible.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: «الَّذِينَ» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الخاشعين. «يَظُنُّونَ» is an imperfect verb; «أنّ» has fatḥa because of الظنّ; its noun is the hāʾ and mīm, and the khabar (predicate) is «مُلاقُوا». The original is ملاقون, because it is in the sense of "you will meet"; the nūn was dropped for lightness. «وَأَنَّهُمْ» is conjoined to the first; «وإنّهم» is also permissible, cutting it off from what precedes.

nahhas-irab:266-266.t: أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ تَكُونَ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنابٍ: it is asked: «تكون» is a future verb, so how is a past verb conjoined to it, namely وَأَصابَهُ الْكِبَرُ? There are two answers. One is that the implied form is «وقد أصابه الكبر» (and old age has already struck him). The other answer is that it is construed on the meaning, because the meaning is "would any of you like it if he had a garden", so on this basis [comes] وأصابه الكبر. وَلَهُ ذُرِّيَّةٌ ضُعَفاءُ: and He said in another place ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعافاً [al-Nisāʾ: 9], as you say ظريف, ظرفاء and ظراف.

nahhas-irab:267-267.t: وَلا تَيَمَّمُوا الْخَبِيثَ: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «ولا تأمّموا», and the two are dialect forms. Ibn Kathīr read «ولا تّيمّموا» [with the tāʾ doubled]; the original is تتيمّموا, and he assimilated the tāʾ into the tāʾ. Whoever read تَيَمَّمُوا dropped [one tāʾ]. Muslim ibn Jundub read «ولا تُيَمِّموا». [Translator's note: the source prints all these readings with the same vowelling as the standard text; the forms in square brackets or as given follow the explanations.] وَلَسْتُمْ بِآخِذِيهِ إِلَّا أَنْ تُغْمِضُوا فِيهِ: Qatāda read «إلا أن تُغمَضوا فيه» and said: "unless it is overlooked for you in it"; and it is narrated from him «إلا أن تُغمِضوا فيه», i.e. that you would take it [only] at a reduction, so how would you give it in charity? [Translator's note: the source prints both of Qatāda's readings with the standard vowelling.] «أن» is in the position of accusative (manṣūb), and the implied form is «إلّا بأن».

nahhas-irab:268-268.t:
الشَّيْطانُ يَعِدُكُمُ الْفَقْرَ: two objects; one also says الفُقر. وَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْفَحْشاءِ: outside the Qur'an «ويأمركم الفحشاء» is permitted, dropping the bāʾ. Sībawayh recited: [al-Basīṭ] 61-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded; I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)

nahhas-irab:269-269.t: وَمَنْ يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ: a condition, which is why the alif was lightened [i.e. dropped]; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْراً كَثِيراً.

nahhas-irab:270-270.t:
وَما أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ نَفَقَةٍ أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِنْ نَذْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُهُ: the implied form may be «وما أنفقتم من نفقة فإنّ الله يعلمها وما نذرتم من نذر فإنّ الله يعلمه» (whatever expenditure you spend, Allah knows it, and whatever vow you make, Allah knows it), then [the first] was omitted. The implied form may also be «وما أنفقتم من نفقة فإنّ الله يعلمه», with the hāʾ referring to «ما», as the poet recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 62-
فتوضح فالمقراة لم يعف رسمها ... لما نسجته من جنوب وشمأل
(Then Tūḍiḥ and al-Miqrāt: their traces have not been effaced, because of what south and north winds have woven over them.)
And أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِنْ نَذْرٍ is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:271-271.t:
إِنْ تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ: this is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Nāfiʿ. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «فنَعِمّا هي» with fatḥa on the nūn. It is narrated from Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ with sukūn on the ʿayn; Qālūn narrated it from Nāfiʿ. Outside the Qur'an «فنعم ما هي» is permitted, but in the written text it is joined, so assimilation is obligatory. The grammarians report four dialect forms of نعم: one says «نَعِمَ الرجلُ زيد», and this is the original; one says «نِعِمَ الرجل», giving the nūn kasra because of the kasra of the ʿayn; one says «نَعْمَ الرجل», the original being نَعِمَ with the kasra dropped because it is heavy; and one says «نِعْمَ الرجل», and this is the most eloquent of the forms. [Translator's note: the source writes the four forms unvowelled; the vowelling follows the explanations.] Its original is نَعِمَ; it occurs in every [expression of] praise, so it was lightened: the kasra of the ʿayn was shifted onto the nūn and the ʿayn made quiescent. So whoever reads «فنِعِمّا هي» has two possible analyses: one is that he brought it in the dialect of whoever says نِعِمَ; the other is that it is in the good dialect, so that the original is نِعْمَ, then the ʿayn was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. As for what is reported from Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ of sukūn on the ʿayn, it is impossible. It is reported that Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: as for sukūn on the ʿayn with the mīm doubled, no one is able to pronounce it; one only attempts to combine two quiescent letters, and [actually] gives a vowel without noticing. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever reads «فنَعِمّا هي» has two possible analyses: one is that it is in the dialect of whoever says «نَعِمَ الرجل», and the other is that it is in the dialect of whoever says «نَعْمَ الرجل», then the ʿayn was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Whoever reads «فنَعِمّا» must [consistently] say «بَئِس».
وَإِنْ تُخْفُوها: a condition, which is why the nūn was dropped from it. وَتُؤْتُوهَا: conjoined to it, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ. Qatāda, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū ʿAmr read «ونكفّرُ عنكم من سيّئاتكم» [in the nominative], and Nāfiʿ, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «ونكفّرْ عنكم» [in the jussive], except that al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Juʿfī narrated from al-Aʿmash «ونكفّرَ عنكم» in the accusative. [Translator's note: the source writes these readings unvowelled; the case of each follows from the discussion below.] Abū Ḥātim said: al-Aʿmash read «فهو خير لكم نكفّرْ عنكم» without the wāw, in the jussive. What is sound from ʿĀṣim is that he read it in the nominative with the nūn; Ḥafṣ narrated from him that he read وَيُكَفِّرُ with the yāʾ and the nominative, and this is likewise narrated from al-Ḥasan; and it is narrated from him with the yāʾ and the jussive. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās read «وتُكفِّرْ عنكم من سيّئاتكم» with the tāʾ, kasra on the fāʾ and the jussive, and ʿIkrima read «وتُكفَّرْ عنكم» with the tāʾ, fatḥa on the fāʾ and the jussive.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best of the readings is «ونكفّرُ عنكم» in the nominative; this is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. Sībawayh said: the nominative here is the [proper] aspect and it is the good one, because the speech after the fāʾ runs as it would outside a conditional. He permitted the jussive, construing it on the meaning, because the meaning is: "and if you conceal it and give it to the poor, it will be better for you, and We will expiate for you". What Abū Ḥātim reported from al-Aʿmash, without the wāw and in the jussive, is as a badal (substitute), as if it were in the position of the fāʾ [clause]. What is narrated from ʿĀṣim, «وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنْكُمْ» with the yāʾ and the nominative, means "Allah will expiate"; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd. Abū Ḥātim said: its meaning is "the giving will expiate". Ibn ʿAbbās's reading «وتُكفِّر» means "and the charities will expiate", and ʿIkrima's reading «وتُكفَّر عنكم» [means]: i.e. some things of your misdeeds [will be expiated]. As for the accusative «ونكفّرَ», it is weak; it is with «أن» implied, and it is permitted, though far-fetched, because in a conditional one thing becomes due only through another's becoming due, so it resembles the interrogative.

nahhas-irab:272-272.t: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُداهُمْ وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ: a number of people have spoken about the meaning of "He guides" and "He leads astray". Among the most eminent of what has been narrated on this is what Sufyān narrated from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Qurashī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿUmar, that he said in his sermon: «من يهده الله فلا مضلّ له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له» ("Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leads astray, none can guide"). The Catholicos was present and gestured in disapproval. ʿUmar said: what is he saying? They said: he says that Allah neither guides nor leads astray. ʿUmar said to him: you lie, O enemy of Allah! Rather, the One who created you is the one who leads you astray and will enter you into the Fire, if Allah wills. Allah created the people of Paradise and what they will do, and created the people of the Fire and what they will do, and said: these are for this and those are for that. And people have not ceased to disagree about predestination (qadar). Abū ʿUbayd said: Allah the Exalted said: وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَما تَعْمَلُونَ [al-Ṣāffāt: 96]. وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَما تُنْفِقُونَ إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ اللَّهِ وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ: the first «ما» is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) by تنفقوا; the second has no position because it is a particle; and the third is like the first.

nahhas-irab:273-273.t: تَعْرِفُهُمْ بِسِيماهُمْ: with this meaning one also says سيمياء. لا يَسْئَلُونَ النَّاسَ إِلْحافاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "importuning".

nahhas-irab:274-274.t: الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ. The fāʾ entered, although «زيد فمنطلق» is not permitted, because the speech has the sense of a conditional, i.e. "because of their spending, they have their reward". Thus is the speech of the Arabs: when you say «السارق فاقطعه» (the thief: cut [his hand]), its meaning is "because of his theft, cut [his hand]". The meaning of «بالليل والنهار» is "in the night and the day".

nahhas-irab:275-275.t:
الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبا: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is لا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَما يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطانُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ. فَمَنْ جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ: [the verb is masculine] because it is a non-real feminine, i.e. "whoever an admonition (وعظ) comes to", as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 63-
إنّ السّماحة والمروءة ضمّنا
(Generosity and manliness were enclosed [in a grave].)
Al-Ḥasan read «فمن جاءته موعظة».

nahhas-irab:276-276.t: يَمْحَقُ اللَّهُ الرِّبا: the original [final letter] in الربا is wāw. Sībawayh said: its dual is ربوان. The Kufans said: you write it with yāʾ and its dual is with yāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: I have never seen an error uglier or more outrageous than this; the error in spelling does not suffice them, so that they also err in the dual, while they recite وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ رِباً لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ [al-Rūm: 39]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: الربا was written in the Muṣḥaf with wāw to distinguish it from الزنا, and الربا was more entitled to the wāw because it is from ربا يربو.

nahhas-irab:279-279.t: فَأْذَنُوا بِحَرْبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿUbayd reported from al-Aṣmaʿī: «فأذنوا» means "be informed (على أذن) of that", i.e. having knowledge. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a concise and good view. The lexicographers report that one says أذنت به أذنا when you came to know of it. The meaning of «فآذنوا» (then announce), in the reading of al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim, is with the object omitted.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t:
«يَوْماً» is accusative by اتّقوا. Outside the Qur'an «يومَ لا تجزي» in construct would be permissible.
In the sentence there is an omission about which the grammarians differ. The Basrans said: the implied sense is "a day in which (فيه) no soul will avail another soul in anything"; then «فيه» was omitted. Al-Kisāʾī said: this is a mistake; [omitting] «فيه» is not permissible — if it were, الذي تكلّمتُ زيدٌ would be permissible in the sense of "about whom I spoke". He said: rather, the implied sense is "and fear a day which (يجزيه) no soul will avail"; then the hāʾ was omitted. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is permissible to omit «فيه» and to omit the hāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: what al-Kisāʾī said does not follow, because [the preposition] may be omitted from adverbials of time but not from other words. You say تكلّمت في اليوم, and كلّمت, and تكلّمت اليوم. This is the argument of the Basrans.
As for al-Farrāʾ, he replied to al-Kisāʾī by saying: if you say كلّمت زيدا ("I spoke to Zayd") and تكلّمت في زيد ("I spoke about Zayd"), the two meanings are different, so omission is not permissible there, since the meaning would be reversed; but with adverbials the information conveyed is the same. This clause is in the position of the accusative according to the Basrans as a naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, which is why a pronoun must refer back to it; according to the Kufans it is a ṣila.
«وَلا يُقْبَلُ مِنْها شَفاعَةٌ»: «تقبل» with tāʾ is permissible because الشفاعة is feminine; treating it as masculine is good only because it means التشفّع ("intercession"), as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil metre] 20-
إنّ السّماحة والمروءة ضمّنا ... قبرا بمرو على الطريق الواضح
(Generosity and manliness have been placed in a grave at Marw, on the open road.)
Al-Akhfash said: the masculine is good because you have separated [the verb from its subject]. Sībawayh said: the longer the [separating] speech, the better; and it is more common with inanimate things — they distinguished between living beings and inanimate things just as they distinguished between humans and others in the plural. «شَفاعَةٌ» is the noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], and likewise «عَدْلٌ». «وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:49-49.t:
«وَإِذْ نَجَّيْناكُمْ»: «إذ» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «اذكروا نعمتي». «مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ»: al-Kisāʾī said: one only says "the āl of so-and-so (man)" and "the āl of so-and-so (woman)"; it is not said of towns — one does not say "he is of the āl of Ḥimṣ" nor "of the āl of Medina". He said: it is said only of the greatest leader, such as Muḥammad, upon him be peace — the people of his religion and his followers — and "the āl of Pharaoh" because he is their leader in misguidance. He said: but we have heard it of towns; they said "the people (ahl) of Medina" and "the āl of Medina". Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: if you make the plural of آل you say آلون; if you make the plural of آل that is in the sense of "mirage" you say أَوْآل, like مال and أموال. Abū Jaʿfar said: the original of آل is أهل; then an alif was substituted for the hāʾ. If you make the diminutive you return it to its origin and say أُهَيْل. «فِرْعَوْنَ» is in the position of the genitive, except that it is a diptote because it is foreign. Al-Akhfash said:
«يَسُومُونَكُمْ» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is presumably that it is a new start, i.e. resumptive]; or, if you wish, it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "inflicting upon you". Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يَذْبَحُونَ أَبْناءَكُمْ» [without doubling]; [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «يُذَبِّحُونَ»; Ibn Muḥayṣin's reading is known to be the light form, which the following comparison implies;] the doubled form is more expressive because it carries the meaning of multiplicity. «وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ» is conjoined. «وَفِي ذلِكُمْ بَلاءٌ»: [بلاء] is nominative as mubtadaʾ; «عَظِيمٌ» is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: «وَإِذْ فَرَقْنا» is in the position of the accusative. Al-Akhfash reported «فَرَّقْنا» [with doubling]. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «فَرَقْنا» for the reported variant.] «الْبَحْرَ» is the object.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t:
«وَإِذْ واعَدْنا مُوسى»: Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «وإذ وعدنا» without alif [Translator's note: the source has «وإذا», evidently for «وإذ»], and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He rejected «واعدنا», saying: because mutual appointment (muwāʿada) takes place only between humans; as for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, He alone makes promises and threats. This is how we have found the Qur'an, as in His saying «وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ الْحَقِّ» [Ibrāhīm: 22], His saying «وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ» [al-Fatḥ: 29], and His saying «وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّها لَكُمْ» [al-Anfāl: 7].
Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the view of Abū Isḥāq in the book before this one. This statement of Abū ʿUbayd is a clear mistake, because he has merged one category into another and rejected what is better and finer. «واعدنا» is better; it is the reading of Mujāhid, al-Aʿraj, Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. His saying, glory be to Him, «وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا» [al-Māʾida: 9] has nothing to do with this, because «واعدنا موسى» belongs to the category of meeting at an appointed time (muwāfāt), and has nothing to do with promise and threat; it is rather from the saying:
"your appointment is on Friday", "your appointment is at such-and-such a place"; and the eloquent usage for this is to say واعدته.
«مُوسى أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً» are two objects. Al-Akhfash said: the implied sense is "and when We appointed with Moses the completion of forty nights"; then [the muḍāf] was omitted, as He said «وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ» [Yūsuf: 82].
«ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ» is with assimilation [اتّخذتّم]; or, if you wish, you may pronounce [the dhāl] distinctly, because the dhāl is voiced and the tāʾ voiceless, so distinct pronunciation is good. Assimilation is permissible only because the second is as if separate. «العجل» is the first object, and the second object is omitted.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: «ثُمَّ عَفَوْنا»: «ثم» indicates that the second comes after the first, and with an interval besides. The position of the nūn and alif is nominative by the verb.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
«وَإِذْ آتَيْنا» is in the sense of "We gave". «مُوسَى الْكِتابَ» are two objects. «وَالْفُرْقانَ» is conjoined to الكتاب. Al-Farrāʾ and Quṭrub said: it may be «وَإِذْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ», i.e. the Torah, and [gave] Muḥammad ﷺ the Furqān. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake both in i'rab and in meaning. As for i'rab: what is conjoined to a thing is like it, whereas on this view what is conjoined to a thing would be different from it. As for meaning: He, Majestic and Mighty, has said about it «وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى وَهارُونَ الْفُرْقانَ» [al-Anbiyāʾ: 48]. Abū Isḥāq said: the Furqān may be this same Book, mentioned again; but this too is far-fetched — it occurs only in poetry, as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir metre] 21-
وألفى قولها كذبا ومينا
(And he found her words to be lies and falsehood.)
The best that has been said on this is the view of Mujāhid: a criterion between truth and falsehood which He taught him.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t:
«وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ يا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ بِاتِّخاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلى بارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ عِنْدَ بارِئِكُمْ فَتابَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ» (54)
«وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ يا قَوْمِ»: the yāʾ was dropped because the vocative is a place of omission and the kasra indicates it; it is in the status of the tanwīn, so you dropped it as you drop the tanwīn from a single noun. Outside the Qur'an it is permissible to keep it quiescent and say «يا قومي», because it is a noun in the position of the genitive; or, if you wish, you may give it fatḥa; or, if you wish, you may attach a hāʾ to it and say يا قوميه; or, if you wish, you may substitute an alif for it, because it is lighter, and say يا قوما; or, if you wish, you may say يا قومُ in the sense of "O you people"; and if you treat them as indefinite you use the accusative with tanwīn.
«إِنَّكُمْ»: إنّ has kasra because it comes after القول ("saying"), so it begins a new sentence. «ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ»: the plural of paucity is used in place of the plural of abundance, which is نفوس. «بِاتِّخاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ»: [العجل] is the object, i.e. "by your having taken the calf"; the kāf and mīm are in the position of the genitive by the construct, and in interpretation they are in the position of the nominative. «فَتُوبُوا» is an imperative. «إِلى بارِئِكُمْ» is genitive through إلى. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr that he made the hamza of «بارِئْكُمْ» quiescent, and Sībawayh reported from him a slurring (ikhtilās) of the vowel. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for making the hamza quiescent, Abū al-ʿAbbās held that it is a solecism (laḥn), permissible neither in prose nor in poetry, because it is the letter carrying the case-ending; but the early leading grammarians permitted it and recited: [al-Rajaz metre] 22-
إذا اعوججن قلت صاحب قوم
(When they swerved, I said: "Companion, set them straight!")
«إِلى بارِيكُمْ» is also permissible, substituting a yāʾ for the hamza. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «بارِئِكُمْ» for these variants.]
«إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ»: the hāʾ is the noun (ism) of «إنّ»; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «التواب» the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of إنّ. Or, if you wish, «هو» is redundant; or, if you wish, it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ, with «التواب» the khabar of «إنّ» and «الرحيم» its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: «وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ» is conjoined. «يا مُوسى» is a single [non-construct] noun in the vocative. «جَهْرَةً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial); one says "I saw the governor جهارًا or جهرةً", i.e. not screened by anything; from this is "so-and-so commits sins openly (يجاهر)", i.e. he does not hide from people. «فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ»: [الصاعقة] is nominative by its verb. «وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ» is in the position of the ḥāl, i.e. "looking on".

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: «ثُمَّ بَعَثْناكُمْ»: the position of the nūn and alif is nominative by the verb, and the kāf and mīm are accusative by the verb.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: the singular of «الْغَمامَ» is غمامة, like سحابة and سحاب. Al-Farrāʾ said: غمائم is permissible. «وَأَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ»: [المنّ] is accusative because the verb falls upon it. «وَالسَّلْوى» is conjoined; the case does not show in it because it is maqṣūr (ending in a short alif). This is necessarily so with every maqṣūr word, because it always has an alif at its end. Al-Khalīl said: the alif is an airy letter with no fixed point, so it resembled a vowel, and its taking a vowel became impossible. Al-Farrāʾ said: if the alif took a vowel it would become a hamza. Al-Akhfash said: «المنّ» is a collective with no singular, like الخير and الشرّ; and no singular has been heard for «السلوى» — if it were said by analogy, one would say in the singular سلوى [too], as one says سُمانى and شُكاعى for singular and plural alike.
«كُلُوا» is an imperative. «مِنْ طَيِّباتِ» is genitive through من. «ما رَزَقْناكُمْ» is genitive by the iḍāfa (genitive construct).

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
«وَإِذْ قُلْنَا ادْخُلُوا»: the alif of «قلنا» was dropped [in pronunciation] because it and the dāl after it are both quiescent; the alif with which one begins before the dāl is a connecting alif, because it is from يدخل. «فَكُلُوا» is conjoined to it. «رَغَداً» is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "an abundant eating"; it may also be in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial). «وَادْخُلُوا» is conjoined. «سُجَّداً» is accusative as a ḥāl. «وَقُولُوا» is conjoined. «حِطَّةٌ» is [nominative] by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject).
Al-Akhfash said: «حِطَّةً» has been read in the accusative, as a substitute for the verb. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «حِطَّةٌ» for the accusative reading.] Abū Jaʿfar said: the ḥadīth from Ibn ʿAbbās that they were told: «Say: There is no god but Allah», and in another ḥadīth from him that they were told: «Say: forgiveness», is an interpretation in favour of the accusative, i.e. "say something that will remove (يحطّ) your sins from you", as you say "say something good" (قل خيرا).
The ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd, «they said: ḥiṭṭatun», is an interpretation in favour of the nominative, which is more proper linguistically, and the leading Qur'an readers read the nominative. It became more proper linguistically only because of what is reported from the Arabs about the meaning of بدّل. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: one says بدّلتُ الشيء, i.e. I changed it but did not remove its substance; and أبدلته, I removed its substance and its person; as Abū al-Najm said: [al-Rajaz metre] 23-
عزل الأمير المبدل
(The removal of the governor who is replaced.)
And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: «قالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنَا ائْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هذا أَوْ بَدِّلْهُ» [Yūnus: 15]. [Translator's note: the entry ends here in the source; the argument appears to continue under the next verse.]

nahhas-irab:177-177.t:
(لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ): the noun of ليس, and the khabar (predicate) is (أَنْ تُوَلُّوا). The Kufans read (لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا) [Translator's note: the printed vocalisation is identical to the standard reading; the reading described is presumably الْبِرَّ in the accusative as khabar, the other readers having الْبِرُّ in the nominative], making «أن» be in the position of the nominative; the first [reading] has no fronting or postponement. In the reading of Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd: "ليس البرّ بأن تولّوا", so here only the nominative is permissible for البرّ. (وَلكِنَّ الْبِرَّ): the Kufans read "ولكن البرّ" [Translator's note: i.e. وَلكِنِ الْبِرُّ with lightened لكن], nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ) is the khabar, and there are three views on it: the implied form may be "but righteousness is the righteousness of whoever believes in Allah", then [the muḍāf] was omitted, as al-Khansāʾ said: [al-Basīṭ] 32-
فإنما هي إقبال وإدبار
(For she is but coming and going.)
i.e. "given to coming [and going]". The implied form may be "but the one possessed of righteousness is whoever believes in Allah"; and البرّ may mean البارّ (the righteous), as one says رجل عدل ("a man [who is] justice"). There is a difficulty in the verse with respect to iʿrāb, because after this comes (وَالْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذا عاهَدُوا وَالصَّابِرِينَ), on which there are five views. «الموفون» may be nominative, conjoined to «من», with «الصابرين» [accusative] by way of praise, i.e. "and I mean the patient." «الموفون» may be nominative in the sense of "and they are those who fulfil", as praise of the [persons referred to by the] pronouns, with «الصابرين» conjoined to ذوي القربى. «الموفون» may be nominative as "and they are those who fulfil", with «الصابرين» meaning "and I mean the patient." These are three answers that cannot be faulted with respect to iʿrāb and that are found in the speech of the Arabs. Sībawayh recited: [al-Kāmil] 33-
لا يبعدن قومي الّذين هم ... سمّ العداة وآفة الجزر
النّازلين بكلّ معترك ... والطّيّبون معاقد الأزر
(May my people not perish, who are poison to their enemies and the bane of the slaughter-camels; who alight in every battlefield, and who are pure where the waist-wrappers are tied.)
If you like, you may say النازلون and الطيبين; if you like, you may put both in the nominative; and both may be in the accusative.
Al-Kisāʾī said: «الموفون» may be conjoined to «من» and «الصابرين» conjoined to «ذوي القربى». Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is a mistake and a clear error, because if you put والصابرين in the accusative and conjoin it to ذوي القربى, it enters into the ṣila (relative clause) of «من», so you would have conjoined to «من» before the ṣila is complete and separated the ṣila from the relative noun by the conjoined element. The fifth answer: «الموفون» is conjoined to the latent pronoun in آمن, and «الصابرين» conjoined to «ذوي القربى». Al-Kisāʾī said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "والموفين والصابرين". Abū Jaʿfar said: they would be conjoined to ذوي القربى, or [accusative] by way of praise. Al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh in «al-Nisāʾ»: "والمقيمون الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة" [al-Nisāʾ: 162].

nahhas-irab:178-178.t:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصاصُ): the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (فِي الْقَتْلى): the case ending does not appear on it because it contains the alif of the feminine, which was brought to mark the femininity of the group. (الْحُرُّ بِالْحُرِّ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
(وَالْعَبْدُ بِالْعَبْدِ وَالْأُنْثى بِالْأُنْثى) is conjoined to it. (فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ) is a condition, and the apodosis is (فَاتِّباعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ); it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "then upon him is following up with what is right." Outside the Qur'an فاتّباعا وأداء is permissible, making both of them maṣdars (verbal nouns). (ذلِكَ تَخْفِيفٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:179-179.t: (وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصاصِ حَياةٌ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The reading of Ubayy and Abū al-Jawzāʾ, "ولكم في القصص", is irregular (shādhdh), and the apparent text points to something else. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصاصُ فِي الْقَتْلى﴾, so one part of the speech points to another, and the exegesis is in terms of retaliation (al-qiṣāṣ). Sufyān al-Thawrī related from al-Suddī from Abū Mālik [regarding] ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصاصِ حَياةٌ﴾: he said: [it means] that you do not kill one another. Then He said (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ): the object has been omitted because the hearer knows it. Al-Layth related from Rabīʿa about His saying (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ): [i.e. that you may guard against] what is forbidden to you and what I [Translator's note: so in the source, "نهيت"] have forbidden some of you to do to others.

nahhas-irab:180-180.t:
(كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ): there is an implied conjunctive wāw in the speech, the meaning being "and it is prescribed for you". Similar to it, according to some views, is ﴿لا يَصْلاها إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى﴾ [al-Layl: 15, 16], i.e. "and none will burn in it". (أَحَدَكُمُ) is the object and (الْمَوْتُ) the fāʿil (agent). (إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْراً) is a condition, and there are two views on its apodosis. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: the implied form is "then the bequest", and then the fāʾ was dropped, as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 34-
من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها ... والشّرّ بالشّرّ عند الله مثلان
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will be grateful for them; and evil for evil are, with Allah, equal.)
The other answer is that with a past [verb in a condition] the apodosis may come before or after it, so the implied form is "the bequest is for the parents and near relatives, if he leaves wealth." If you drop the fāʾ, الوصية is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and if you do not suppose the fāʾ, you may also put it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, or put it in the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. "the bequest is prescribed for you." Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned several views on the verse, among them that it is abrogated by the obligatory shares, and among them that it is a recommendation concerning bequest. Abū Jaʿfar said: the [correct] view is that none of this may be taken as a recommendation except with evidence; and it has been said that it is abrogated by the ḥadīth «There is no bequest for an heir». (حَقًّا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun); outside the Qur'an «حقّ» [nominative] is permissible, in the sense of "that is a duty."

nahhas-irab:181-181.t: (فَمَنْ بَدَّلَهُ) is a condition, and its apodosis is (فَإِنَّما إِثْمُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ). «ما» restrains (kāffa) أنّ from governing. (إِثْمُهُ) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ) is in the position of the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:182-182.t:
(فَمَنْ خافَ) is a condition. The original is خوف; the wāw was changed into an alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it is vowelled.
The people of Kufa incline (imāla) «خاف» to indicate the kasra of فَعِلْتُ [i.e. خِفْتُ]. (مِنْ مُوصٍ), and من موصّ [is also read]; the light form is clearer, because most grammarians say موصّ is for intensity/frequency, though it may be like كرّم and أكرم.
