(جَنَفاً) is from جنف يجنف, "to deviate"; the noun from it is جنف and جانف [Translator's note: so in the source]. (فَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ) is conjoined to خاف; the pronoun refers to the heirs, who have not been mentioned, because the meaning is known. The apodosis of the condition is (فَلا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ).

nahhas-irab:183-183.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيامُ): the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (كَما كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative in three ways. It may be a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar from كتب, i.e. "fasting is prescribed for you with a prescribing like…"; the implied form may be "fasting is prescribed for you, a fasting like…"; and it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "fasting is prescribed for you, resembling what was prescribed for those before you." It may also be in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of الصيام [Translator's note: the source continues "وما للصيام وما بيانه «الذين آمنوا»", which is garbled and cannot be construed with confidence]. «ما» is in the position of the genitive, and its ṣila (relative clause) is كتب على الذين من قبلكم; the pronoun in كتب refers back to «ما».

nahhas-irab:184-184.t:
(أَيَّاماً مَعْدُوداتٍ): al-Akhfash said: (أَيَّاماً) is accusative by الصيام, i.e. "it is prescribed for you that you fast numbered days." Al-Farrāʾ said: it is accusative by كتب, because when a passive verb puts one noun after it in the nominative, it puts the other in the accusative. There is a subtle and obscure point of grammar in the verse. It may be said: the grammarians do not allow هذا صارف ظريف زيدا ("this is a turner-away, a clever one, of Zayd"), so how can «أياما» be accusative by الصيام when the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of الصيام? The answer is that if you make أياما an object, this is not permissible; but if you make it an adverbial (ẓarf), it is permissible, because adverbials are governed by abstract notions. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā held that this is not permissible at all. If you make the kāf be in the position of the accusative by كتب, it is not permissible [to make أياما accusative by الصيام], because you would be separating الصيام from what it governs by something it does not govern. If you make the kāf be in the position of the accusative by الصيام and make أياما accusative by الصيام, there is no disagreement that it is fully good. (مَعْدُوداتٍ) is a naʿt of أيام, except that the tāʾ takes kasra — according to the Basrans because it is a sound plural, and according to the Kufans because it is not a radical. (فَمَنْ كانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضاً) is a condition with من, i.e. "whoever among you is ill during these days". (فَعِدَّةٌ) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate), عليه, has been omitted. Al-Kisāʾī said: فعدّة [Translator's note: i.e. فَعِدَّةً, accusative] is also permissible, i.e. "let him fast a number." (مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ): «أخر» is a diptote according to Sībawayh because it is deflected (maʿdūl) from the article, since the rule for فُعَل of this kind is to come with the article, as in الكبر and الفضل. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is a deflected أخر, as you say
حمراء and حمر, and that is why it is a diptote. It has also been said that it is a diptote because it is on the pattern of a plural.
It may be said: one only says يوم آخر ("another day"), not أخرى; and أخر is the plural of أخرى. There are two answers to this: one is that the adjective of الأيام may be feminine, and that is why it is qualified by أخر; the other is that أخر is the plural of أخرى, as though it were أيام أخرى, then since they are many, أيام أخر was said. (وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ): the original is يطوقونه, and it has been read so; then the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the ṭāʾ and the wāw changed into a yāʾ because what precedes it has kasra. Ibn ʿAbbās read يطوّقونه, so the wāw remained sound, since there is no kasra before it; and يطّوّقونه is read, the original being يتطوّقونه, then the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ. The reading agreed upon is (يُطِيقُونَهُ), and the soundest view about it is that the verse is abrogated, as we have mentioned. As for يطيّقونه and تطّيّقونه, they are not permissible, because the wāw is not changed into a yāʾ except for a cause. "فدية طعام مساكين": this is the reading of the people of Medina and of Ibn ʿĀmir; ʿUbayd Allāh transmitted it from him from Nāfiʿ [Translator's note: so in the source]. Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza read (وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعامُ مِسْكِينٍ) [Translator's note: their reading is فِدْيَةٌ طَعامُ مِسْكِينٍ with فدية nominative with tanwīn and طعام nominative; the printed vocalisation does not show this distinctly], and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He held that he chose it because its meaning is that for each day one of them is to be fed, so the singular expresses the plural, whereas the plural does not express the singular. Abū Jaʿfar said: this statement of Abū ʿUbayd is rejected, because this is known only by indication; it is known that the meaning of "وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مساكين" is that for each day there is a poor person, so the preferred reading is this one, so that a plural corresponds to a plural. Abū ʿUbayd chose to read (فِدْيَةٌ طَعامُ مِسْكِينٍ) [Translator's note: i.e. with طعامُ nominative, not in construct]; he said: because the food is the ransom. Abū Jaʿfar said: الطعام may not be a naʿt, because it is a substance, but it is permissible as a badal (substitute); clearer than that is to read (فِدْيَةٌ طَعامُ) in a genitive construct [Translator's note: i.e. فِدْيَةُ طَعامِ], because فدية is vague and applies to food and other things, so it becomes like your saying هذا ثوب خزّ ("this is a garment of silk"). (فَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ خَيْراً فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ): a condition and its apodosis. (وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. "fasting is better for you."

nahhas-irab:185-185.t:
(شَهْرُ رَمَضانَ): six ways have been related in it. (شَهْرُ رَمَضانَ) is the reading of the majority. Mujāhid and Shahr ibn Ḥawshab read (شَهْرُ رَمَضانَ) in the accusative [Translator's note: i.e. شَهْرَ; the printed vocalisation shows the nominative]. Assimilation of the rāʾ into the rāʾ is related from al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr; this is not permissible, lest two vowelless letters come together. The fourth reading is concealment (ikhfāʾ) [i.e. a reduced vowel]. The fifth way is to transfer the vowel of the rāʾ to the hāʾ, so the hāʾ takes ḍamma; this is the view of the Kufans, as Imruʾ al-Qays said: [al-Ṭawīl] 35-
فمن كان ينسانا وحسن بلائنا ... فليس بناسينا على حالة بكر
(Whoever forgets us and our fine trial [in battle], Bakr will not forget us in any state.)
And (شَهْرُ رَمَضانَ) [Translator's note: the sixth way, presumably شَهَرَ/شَهَرُ with fatḥa on the hāʾ; the printed vocalisation does not show it] is permissible on two grounds: one according to the reading of those who read the accusative and transferred the vowel of the rāʾ to the hāʾ; the other according to the dialect of those who say لحم and لحم, نهر and نهر [Translator's note: i.e. لَحْم/لَحَم, نَهْر/نَهَر]. «شهر رمضان» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ). شهر may also be nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "what is made obligatory upon you to fast is the month of Ramaḍān", or "that is the month of Ramaḍān", or "the fasting [is]", or "the days [are]". رمضان is a diptote because its nūn is an augment. The accusative of شهر رمضان is irregular, and several views have been given on it. Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "fasting is prescribed for you, and that you fast the month of Ramaḍān." Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "fasting is prescribed for you", i.e. that you fast the month of Ramaḍān. Abū Jaʿfar said: you may not make شهر رمضان accusative by تصوموا, because it would enter into the ṣila (relative clause) and then the ṣila would be separated from the relative; likewise if you make it accusative by الصيام. But you may make it accusative by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "hold to the month of Ramaḍān and fast the month of Ramaḍān". This too is far-fetched, because the month has not been mentioned before so as to incite to it.
(هُدىً لِلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّناتٍ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from القرآن, and القرآن is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (فَمَنْ شَهِدَ مِنْكُمُ الشَّهْرَ): it may be asked: what is the benefit of this, when both the resident and the traveller witness the month? The answer is that الشهر is not an object but an adverbial of time, the implied form being "whoever of you is present in the town during the month." Another answer is that the implied form is "whoever of you witnesses the month, not being a traveller or ill". (فَلْيَصُمْهُ): al-Ḥasan read (فَلْيَصُمْهُ) [Translator's note: i.e. فَلِيَصُمْهُ with kasra on the lām; the printed form shows the standard reading], and he used to give kasra to the lām of the imperative whether it was at the beginning or something preceded it; that is the original. Whoever made it vowelless dropped the kasra because it is heavy. (وَمَنْ كانَ مَرِيضاً أَوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ): the noun of «كان» is latent in it, «مريضا» is its khabar, and «أو على سفر» is conjoined, i.e. "or travelling".
(فَعِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ): اليسر and اليسر are two dialectal forms, and likewise العسر and العسر [Translator's note: i.e. اليُسْر/اليُسُر and العُسْر/العُسُر].
(وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ): there are five views on it. Al-Akhfash said: it is conjoined, i.e. "and He wants [it], so that you complete the number", as He said ﴿يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 8]. Someone else said: Allah wants this lightening so that you complete the number. It has been said: the wāw is intrusive (muqḥama). Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "and so that you complete the number He did this." Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a good view; similar to it is ﴿وَكَذلِكَ نُرِي إِبْراهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُوقِنِينَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 75], i.e. "and so that he would be among the certain, We did that." The fifth view was mentioned by Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarī [al-Zajjāj]: he said it is construed according to the meaning, the implied form being "Allah did that to make it easy for you and so that you complete the number." He said: similar to it is what Sībawayh recited: [al-Kāmil] 36-
بادت وغيّر آيهنّ مع البلى ... إلّا رواكد جمرهنّ هباء
ومشجّج أمّا سواء قذاله ... فبدا وغيّر ساره المعزاء
(They have perished, and decay has altered their signs, except the settled hearth-stones whose embers are dust, and a battered tent-peg whose head shows plainly, while the stony ground has altered the rest of it.)
because the meaning of "they have perished except the settled stones" is "there are settled stones in them", so it is as though he said: "and in them there is a battered peg", or "there there is a battered peg." Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, the two ʿĀṣims and al-Aʿraj read (وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ) [Translator's note: their reading is evidently وَلِتُكَمِّلُوا with the doubled form; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading], and al-Kisāʾī chose (وَلِتُكْمِلُوا) because of His saying ﴿الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 3]. Abū Jaʿfar said: they are two dialectal forms with one meaning, as He said ﴿فَمَهِّلِ الْكافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْداً﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 17]. ولتكملوا with a vowelless lām is not permissible; the difference between this and what preceded is that the implied form is "and for that you complete the number", so dropping أن and the kasra is not permissible. (وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا) is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:280-280.t:
وَإِنْ كانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ: «كان» means "occurred" (وقع). Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 64-
فدى لبني ذهل بن شيبان ناقتي ... إذا كان يوم ذو كواكب أشهب
(My she-camel is a ransom for the Banū Dhuhl ibn Shaybān, when there comes a grey day full of stars [i.e. a day of battle dark enough to show the stars].)
This is the best of what has been said about it, because it is then general for all people. It may also be that the khabar (predicate) of كان is omitted, i.e. "and if one in hardship is [party] to the debt". Ḥajjāj al-Warrāq said: in the Muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh it is «وإن كان ذا عسرة». Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied form is "and if the one dealt with is in hardship". فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلى مَيْسَرَةٍ: i.e. what you deal with him by is a deferment. Al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read «فنظْرة إلى ميسرة», dropping the kasra because of its heaviness. Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ read «فناظِرْهُ» as a command, «إلى ميسُرِه» with ḍamma on the sīn and kasra on the rāʾ, keeping the hāʾ in continuous recitation. Abū Isḥāq said: it has been read (فناظرة إلى ميسرة), and the people of Medina read (إلى ميسُرة). «فنظرةً إلى ميسرة» in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) is permitted. [Translator's note: the source writes these readings unvowelled or with the standard vowelling; the vowels given follow the descriptions.] Abū Ḥātim said: «فناظرة» is not permitted; that is only in «al-Naml»: فَناظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ الْمُرْسَلُونَ [al-Naml: 35], because she was a woman who said this of herself, from نظرت تنظر, so she is ناظرة. As for «فنظرة» in al-Baqara, it is from deferring; from that is «أنظرتك بالدّين» (I gave you deferment for the debt), i.e. I deferred you in it, and قالَ رَبِّ فَأَنْظِرْنِي إِلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ [al-Ḥijr: 36]. Abū Isḥāq permitted it and said: it is one of the nouns of the maṣdars, like لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِها كاذِبَةٌ [al-Wāqiʿa: 2] and أَنْ يُفْعَلَ بِها فاقِرَةٌ [al-Qiyāma: 25]. Abū Jaʿfar said: «ميسَرة» is the most eloquent of the forms, and it is the dialect of the people of Najd. «ميسُرة», even though it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, is among the anomalous forms; the pattern مَفْعُلة is not found in the speech of the Arabs except in a few counted anomalous words, none of which lacks a مَفْعَلة variant. Moreover, the hāʾ is an addition, and there is no مَفْعُل at all in the speech of the Arabs. The reading of whoever read «إلى ميسُرِهِ» is a solecism (laḥn) that is not permitted. [Translator's note: the source prints this as «إِلى مَيْسَرَةٍ», evidently a slip for the variant with the pronoun.] Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: had they read «إلى ميسَرِه» it would have been more fitting. What al-Akhfash said is good; one says جلست مجلسا, and مَفْعَل is frequent. Al-Akhfash said: «إلى مُوسَرة» is permitted, like مُدخَلة. وَأَنْ تَصَدَّقُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «وأن تتصدّقوا», and ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read «وأن تَصَدَقوا», lightened. تتصدّقوا is on the original form; in تصّدّقوا the tāʾ is assimilated into the ṣād because of its closeness to it, and this is not permitted in تتفكرون because the tāʾ is far from the fāʾ. Whoever lightens drops the tāʾ because [the other] indicates [it], and so as not to combine two quiescent letters and two tāʾs.

nahhas-irab:281-281.t: وَاتَّقُوا يَوْماً: an object. تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ: its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:282-282.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا تَدايَنْتُمْ بِدَيْنٍ: we have mentioned everything about it in our first book, «al-Maʿānī».
فَاكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُبْ: He kept the lām in the second and dropped it from the first because the second is for an absent person and the first is for those addressed. If you wish, you drop the lām with the one addressed because of how often they use it, and this is better; and if you wish, you keep it on the original form. As for the absent person, Muḥammad ibn Yazīd claimed that the lām is indispensable in the verb when you command him, while Sībawayh and the Kufans permitted dropping it and recited: [al-Wāfir] 65-
محمّد تفد نفسك كلّ نفس ... إذا ما خفت من قوم تبالا
(Muhammad, may every soul ransom your soul, whenever you fear ruin from a people.)
وَلْيُمْلِلِ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ: this is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and the Banū Asad; Tamīm say أمليت, and the Qur'an has come with both dialects together. He, Majestic and Mighty, said: فَهِيَ تُمْلى عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا [al-Furqān: 5]. The original is أمللت; the lām was replaced by a yāʾ because it is lighter. فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُونا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَامْرَأَتانِ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «وامرأتان» is conjoined to it, with the khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e. "then a man and two women take their place". Or, if you wish, you imply the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then the one called to witness is a man and two women". The accusative is permitted outside the Qur'an, i.e. "then call to witness [a man and two women]"; Sībawayh reported «إن خنجرا فخنجرا» (if a dagger, then a dagger), i.e. then take a dagger. «أن تضلّ إحداهما فتذْكِرَ إحداهما الأخرى»: this is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, ʿĪsā, Ibn Kathīr and Ḥumayd, with fatḥa on «أن», the accusative on «تذكر» and without doubling. The people of Medina read أَنْ تَضِلَّ إِحْداهُما فَتُذَكِّرَ with fatḥa on «أن», the accusative on «تذكر» and with doubling. Abān ibn Taghlib, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «إن تضلّ إحداهما فتذكّرُ إحداهما الأخرى», with kasra on «إن», the nominative on تذكّر and with doubling. [Translator's note: the source prints these readings with the same vowelling as the standard text or unvowelled; the forms given follow the descriptions.] Abū Jaʿfar said: «تَضَلّ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the ḍād is permitted, and «تِضَلّ» with kasra on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the ḍād is permitted. The first reading is good, because the eloquent usage is to say أذكرتك, ذاكرتك and وعظتك [Translator's note: so in the source; the point evidently concerns أذكرتك and ذكّرتك as equivalent]; He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرى تَنْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ [al-Dhāriyāt: 55], and in the hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: «رحم الله فلانا كأيّ من آية أذكرنيها» ("May Allah have mercy on so-and-so; how many a verse he reminded me of!"). In this reading, despite its goodness, there is a severe difficulty in grammar. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is on the pattern of a conditional; it is a conditional put first whose original place is later, i.e. "call to witness two women in place of the man, so that the one who remembers may remind the one who forgets, if she forgets". When the conditional was put first, it was joined to what preceded it, so «أن» was given fatḥa, and its apodosis came to refer back to it. He said: its parallel is «إني ليعجبني أن يسأل السائل فيعطى» (it pleases me that the asker asks and is given), the meaning being that the giving pleases him if the asker asks. Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is an error according to the Basrans, because if the «إن» of the conditional were given fatḥa the meaning would be reversed. Sībawayh said: أَنْ تَضِلَّ إِحْداهُما فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْداهُمَا الْأُخْرى is accusative because He commanded the calling of witnesses so that she may remind, and for the sake of her reminding. He said: if someone says: how can you say «أن تضلّ», when this was not prepared for the sake of erring and confusion? [the answer is that] He only mentioned «أن تضلّ» because it is the cause of the reminding, as a man says «أعددته أن يميل الحائط فأدعمه» (I prepared it in case the wall leans, so that I may prop it up), while he does not, by preparing it, seek the leaning of the wall; rather he is stating the reason and the cause of the propping. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān report from Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that the implied form is: "of those witnesses you approve of, for fear that one of them errs and for fear that one of them reminds the other". Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is a mistake, and Abū al-ʿAbbās is too eminent to say the like of it, because the meaning is contrary to it; for the meaning would become "for fear that one of them errs and for fear that one of them reminds the other", and this is absurd. The soundest of the views is that of Sībawayh. Whoever says «تَضَلّ» brought it in the dialect of whoever says ضلِلت تضَلّ, and on this basis you say «تِضَلّ» with kasra on the tāʾ, to indicate that the past is فَعِلت.
وَلا تَسْئَمُوا: al-Akhfash said: one says سئمت أسأم سآمة, سآما, سأما and سأما. أَنْ تَكْتُبُوهُ: in the position of accusative (manṣūb) by the verb, as Zuhayr said: [al-Ṭawīl] 66-
سئمت تكاليف الحياة ومن يعش
(I have grown weary of the burdens of life, and whoever lives …)
صَغِيراً أَوْ كَبِيراً: as ḥāl (circumstantial): "I gave him his debt, whether small or large". ذلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ: mubtadaʾ and khabar. وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهادَةِ: conjoined to it, and likewise وَأَدْنى. أَلَّا: in the position of accusative, i.e. «من أن لا». إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً حاضِرَةً: «أن» is in the position of accusative, an exception not of the same kind as the first.
Al-Akhfash said: i.e. "unless a transaction takes place" [i.e. reading تجارةٌ حاضرةٌ, with تكون complete]; and others said: تُدِيرُونَها is the khabar. ʿĀṣim read إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً حاضِرَةً, i.e. "unless the dealing is a present transaction". وَأَشْهِدُوا إِذا تَبايَعْتُمْ: a command. Some claimed it is by way of recommendation and good conduct, and they said the same about His saying: إِذا تَدايَنْتُمْ بِدَيْنٍ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى فَاكْتُبُوهُ. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and he claimed that its parallel is وَإِذا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطادُوا [al-Māʾida: 2]; he said: and its parallel is فَإِذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ [al-Jumuʿa: 10]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistaken view according to all the lexicographers and people of reasoning; His saying, the Exalted, وَإِذا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطادُوا and فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ do not resemble this, because those two are a permission after a prohibition, and it is not permissible in the language to construe a command as recommendation except by what the Arabs use, such as a preceding prohibition or the like. Some claimed that this is among what has been permitted to be left without a [abrogating] verse, and on this basis they explained أَوْ نُنْسِها [al-Baqara: 106], saying: We permit you to leave it. It has been said: the permission is in leaving the writing of the debt, [by His saying] «فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا». And it has been said: writing is obligatory as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded, when the debt is for a term, and Allah commanded this to safeguard people's rights. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: witnessing is obligatory in everything sold, little or much, as Allah the Exalted said: وَأَشْهِدُوا إِذا تَبايَعْتُمْ. وَلا يُضَارَّ كاتِبٌ وَلا شَهِيدٌ: the implied form may be «ولا يضارِر» or «ولا يضارَر». Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq inclining to this [i.e. the active], he said: because after it comes وَإِنْ تَفْعَلُوا فَإِنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ; so it is more fitting that whoever testifies without truth or distorts in writing be called a transgressor (fāsiq); he is more fitting [to be so called] than whoever asks a witness who is busy to testify. Al-Mufaḍḍal said: al-Aʿmash read «ولا يضارِّ كاتب ولا شهيد».
Abū Jaʿfar said: the rāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and likewise the fatḥa has a [valid] meaning, except that fatḥa is lighter. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «ولا يضارِر» with kasra on the first rāʾ, and Ibn Masʿūd read «ولا يضارَر» with fatḥa on the first rāʾ. These two readings are by way of exegesis, and it is not permissible to depart from the recitation that is in the Muṣḥaf. [Translator's note: the source writes these forms without distinguishing vowels; the vowels given follow the descriptions.] وَإِنْ تَفْعَلُوا فَإِنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ: i.e. "for this act [is transgression]"; the implied form may also be "for harming is transgression on your part", as the poet said: [al-Wāfir] 67-
إذا نهي السّفيه جرى إليه
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs towards it [i.e. towards folly, implied by "the fool"].)

nahhas-irab:283-283.t:
وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ عَلى سَفَرٍ وَلَمْ تَجِدُوا كاتِباً: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū al-ʿĀliya read «ولم تجدوا كِتابا» (a writing), and it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās «ولم تجدوا كُتّابا» (scribes). Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading is anomalous, and the generality [of readers] are against it; rarely does anything depart from the reading of the generality without there being a flaw in it. The sequence of the speech indicates كاتب: He the Exalted said before this وَلْيَكْتُبْ بَيْنَكُمْ كاتِبٌ بِالْعَدْلِ, and كُتّاب requires a group. فَرِهانٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ: this is the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and of the people of Kufa and the people of Medina. Ibn ʿAbbās read «فرُهُن» with two ḍammas, and it is the reading of Abū ʿAmr. ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd read «فرُهْن» with sukūn on the hāʾ, and it is narrated from the people of Mecca. Abū Jaʿfar said: the regular pattern here is رهان, as you say بغل and بغال, كبش and كباش. The proper course for «رُهُن» is to be the plural of رهان, like كتاب and كتب; and it has been said: it is the plural of رهن, like سقف [and سُقُف], but this is not the pattern. The proper course for «رُهْن» with sukūn on the hāʾ is that the ḍamma was dropped from it because of its heaviness; and it has been said: it is a plural of رهن, like سهم حشر (a slender arrow) and سهام حشر; the first is more fitting, because the first is not an adjective while this one is an adjective. فَلْيُؤَدِّ: from الأداء, with a hamza; its hamza may be lightened, so the hamza is changed into a wāw; it is not changed into an alif nor made "between-between", because what precedes an alif can only have fatḥa. الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ: originally with a hamza because it is from الأمانة, so the first radical of the verb is a hamza. The original of اؤتمن is أأتمن; they disliked combining two hamzas, so when one of them was removed, [the other] was given hamza. If the hamza is lightened, two quiescent letters meet, the yāʾ in الذي and the lightened hamza, so it was dropped and you say «الذي تمن» [Translator's note: so in the source; the lightened pronunciation is evidently الذِيتُمِن]. When you pronounce the hamza, two quiescent letters had also met, except that you dropped the yāʾ because what precedes it indicates it. When the hamza is lightened, it is not permitted to bring a wāw after a kasra. When beginning [the word] it is أُؤتمن [i.e. اُوتُمِن]. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «ولا يكتموا الشهادة», making it a prohibition for absent persons.
وَمَنْ يَكْتُمْها فَإِنَّهُ آثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ: there are several aspects in it. If you put آثم in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», «قلبه» is an agent standing in place of the khabar. If you wish, you put آثم in the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and قلبه is the agent, the two being in the position of the khabar of «إنّ». If you wish, you put آثم in the nominative as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ [قلبه], intended to come later. If you wish, قلبه is a badal (substitute) of آثم, as you say "he is the heart of the sinner"; and if you wish, it is a badal of the pronoun latent in آثم. Abū Ḥātim permitted «فإنه آثمٌ قلبَه» [in the accusative] and said: as you say "he is sinful in heart". He said: and its parallel is «أنت عربيّ قلبا» (you are Arab at heart), as a maṣdar. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Ḥātim was faulted for this, because قلبه is definite and what he said is not permitted with a definite noun; one does not say «أنت عربيّ قلبه». [Translator's note: the source writes Abū Ḥātim's reading with the same spelling as the standard text and his gloss as «هو آثم قلب الإثم»; the accusative قلبَه follows from the objection.]

nahhas-irab:284-284.t:
وَإِنْ تُبْدُوا ما فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ: a condition. أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ: conjoined to it. يُحاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition. فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ: conjoined to the apodosis. Sībawayh said: it has reached us that some read «فيغفرَ لمن يشاء ويعذّبَ من يشاء» [in the accusative]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Aʿraj; according to the Basrans it is with «أن» implied, and in reality it is conjunction on the meaning, while conjunction on the wording is better, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 68-
ومتى مايع منك كلاما ... يتكلّم فيجبك بعقل
(And whenever he takes in speech from you, he speaks and answers you with sense.)
Al-Ḥasan, Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يحاسبكم به الله فيغفرُ لمن يشاء ويعذّبُ من يشاء» [in the nominative], cutting it off from what precedes. [Translator's note: the source prints both variant readings with the standard vowelling; the cases given follow the explanations.] It is narrated from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif «يحاسبكم به الله يغفرْ لمن يشاء» without the fāʾ, as a badal (substitute). Had it been without the fāʾ, better than the jussive would be the nominative, so that it would be in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 69-
متى تأته تعشو إلى ضوء ناره ... تجد خير نار عندها خير موقد
(Whenever you come to him, making your way by night towards the light of his fire, you find the best of fires, with the best of kindlers beside it.)

nahhas-irab:285-285.t: كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ: on the wording; outside the Qur'an «آمنوا» is permitted, on the meaning. وَقالُوا سَمِعْنا: with an omission, i.e. "we heard as those who accept hear". It has also been said: سمع means "accepted", as one says «سمع الله لمن حمده» (Allah hears whoever praises Him). غُفْرانَكَ: a maṣdar (verbal noun). رَبَّنا: an annexed vocative (munādā muḍāf).

nahhas-irab:286-286.t: لا تُؤاخِذْنا: jussive (majzūm) because it is a request, and likewise وَلا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنا إِصْراً وَلا تُحَمِّلْنا ما لا طاقَةَ لَنا بِهِ; its form is the form of the prohibition. وَاعْفُ عَنَّا: also a request, and its form is the form of the command; for that reason it is not declined [i.e. it is indeclinable] according to the Basrans, and it is jussive according to the Kufans. Likewise وَاغْفِرْ لَنا وَارْحَمْنا, and likewise فَانْصُرْنا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكافِرِينَ.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t:
«فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا»: [الذين] is in the position of the nominative by the verb. «قَوْلًا» is the object. «غَيْرَ الَّذِي» is its naʿt (adjective). Al-Aʿmash read «يَفْسِقُونَ» with kasra on the sīn. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «يَفْسُقُونَ» for al-Aʿmash's variant.] One says فسق يفسق, so he is فاسق from a thing, when he goes out of it; if you say فاسق without saying "from such-and-such", its meaning is "one who goes out of obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty".
In «نَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطاياكُمْ» [al-Baqara: 58] there is some obscure Arabic which we shall explain, if Allah wills. Among this is the view of al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him: the original of the plural of خطيئة is that you say خطايِئُ; then it was transposed, and one said خطائِي with a hamza followed by a yāʾ; then an alif is substituted for the yāʾ as an obligatory substitution, so you say:
خطاءى. This substitution was permissible elsewhere than in this case, [as in] عذارى, except that here he held it to be a lightening. When two alifs came together with a hamza between them, the hamza being of the same kind as the alif, it was as if you had combined three alifs, so you substituted a yāʾ for the hamza and said خطايا. As for Sībawayh, his view is that the original is خطايِئُ, as in the first [view]; then, according to him, the yāʾ had to be given a hamza, as you gave it one in مدائن, so you say خطائِئُ; but two hamzas do not come together in one word, so you substituted a yāʾ for the second and said خطائِي, then you proceeded as you did in the first [view]. Al-Farrāʾ said: خطايا is the plural of خطيّة without hamza, as you say هديّة and هدايا. He said: if you made the plural of خطيئة with hamza you would say خطاءِئ. Al-Kisāʾī said: if you made its plural with hamza you would assimilate the hamza into the hamza, as you said دوابّ.
Mujāhid read «تُغفَر لكم خطاياكم», making it feminine according to the group, and al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «تُغفَر لكم خطيئتُكم». What is clear is «نَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ», because after it comes «وَسَنَزِيدُ» with nūn, and خطاياكم, following the written text; and it is in keeping with its pattern.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: «وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقى»: the dhāl has kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «إذ» is not declined because it is in the status of «في» [Translator's note: so in the source; the comparison seems to be with الذي, a noun that is completed only by what follows], in that it is a noun that is complete only with what follows it. «فَانْفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتا عَشْرَةَ عَيْناً»: «اثنتا» is in the position of the nominative by «فانفجرت», and the sign of the nominative in it is the alif. It is declined, unlike its counterparts [the compound numbers], because the dual is always declined, its meaning being sound. «عَيْناً» is accusative as specification (bayān). Mujāhid, Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read «اثْنَتا عَشِرَةَ عَيْناً» [with kasra on the shīn]; this is the dialect of Banū Tamīm, and this is rare in their dialect, because their way is lightening; and the dialect of the people of the Hijaz is «عَشْرة», though their way is heaviness. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «عَشْرَةَ» for the variant; the vowelling in brackets follows the known reports for these readers.] «وَلا تَعْثَوْا» is a prohibition, which is why the nūn is dropped from it; it is from عثي يعثى. [Translator's note: the source has «عثى يعثى»; translated with the usual form.]

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
«وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ» is conjoined. «يا مُوسى» is a single [non-construct] noun in the vocative. «لَنْ نَصْبِرَ» is accusative (subjunctive) by لن. «عَلى طَعامٍ» is genitive through على. «واحِدٍ» is its naʿt (adjective). «فَادْعُ» is a request in the status of an imperative, which is why the wāw is dropped from it; the dialect of Banū ʿĀmir is «فادعِ لنا» with kasra on the ʿayn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «يُخْرِجْ لَنا» is jussive because it is the answer to the imperative, and it carries the meaning of requital (mujāzāt).
«مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضُ»: al-Akhfash said: «من» is redundant. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake according to the view of Sībawayh, because according to him «من» is not added in an affirmative statement. What led al-Akhfash to this is that he found no object for يخرج, so he wanted to make ما the object. It is better that the object be omitted, indicated by the rest of the speech, the implied sense being "He will bring forth for us, of what the earth grows, something to eat".
«مِنْ بَقْلِها» is a badal (substitute) with the particle repeated. «وَقِثَّائِها» is conjoined. Ṭalḥa and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read «وَقُثَّائِها» with ḍamma on the qāf. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «وَقِثَّائِها» for the variant.] For its plural you say قثائيّ, like عِلْباء and عَلابيّ, except that قثّاء is of the hamzated roots; one says أقثأتُ القوم.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: in my view «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنى» is sound only if it is of the hamzated roots, from their saying دنيء بيّن الدناءة ("base, of evident baseness"), with the hamza then substituted. Abū Jaʿfar said: what we have mentioned is permissible only in poetry, not in prose — so how [could it be] in the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty? Abū Isḥāq said: it is from الدنوّ ("nearness"), i.e. "that which is nearer", from their saying ثوب مقارب, i.e. of little value. Abū Jaʿfar said:
Better than these two views is that the meaning is — and Allah knows best — "Would you take in exchange what is nearer to you in this world for what is better for you on the Day of Resurrection?", because when they asked for something other than what they were commanded to accept, they exchanged what was nearer to them in this world for what was better for them, because of the reward they would have in it.
«اهْبِطُوا مِصْراً» is indefinite. This is the best of the ways, because it is [written] with an alif in the written text. It may also be fully declined while being made a name for the land; we chose the first only because hardly anything like Miṣr is called بلاد or بلد — it is called بلدة — and بلاد is used only in such cases as بلاد الروم. [Translator's note: the passage is translated as written; the argument appears compressed in the source.] Al-Kisāʾī said: Miṣr may be fully declined while definite because of its lightness — he means that it is like هند. This is a mistake according to the view of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, because if you named a woman Zayd you would not decline it fully. Al-Kisāʾī said: Miṣr may be fully declined while definite, because the Arabs fully decline everything that is a diptote in [the language of poetry] except afʿal min ("more … than"). [Translator's note: the attribution «قال الكسائي» is repeated in the source; the second statement, which concerns poetic licence, is translated as written.]
«فَإِنَّ لَكُمْ ما سَأَلْتُمْ»: «ما» is accusative by أنّ. «وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ»: [الذلّة] is the noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. «وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ» is conjoined. We have mentioned the hamza in النبيئين in the book before this one. «ذلِكَ بِما عَصَوْا»: al-Akhfash said: i.e. by their disobedience. «وَكانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ» is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا»: [الذين] is the noun (ism) of «إنّ», and «(آمنوا)» is its ṣila (relative clause). «وَالَّذِينَ هادُوا وَالنَّصارى وَالصَّابِئِينَ» are all conjoined. «مَنْ آمَنَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); آمن is in the position of the jussive through the condition; the fāʾ [introduces] the apodosis and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ: «فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ». The clause is the khabar of إنّ, and the pronoun referring back to الذين from the clause is omitted, i.e. "whoever of them believes". Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «وَلا خَوْفَ عَلَيْهِمْ» as the tabriʾa [the lā of generic negation]. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «خَوْفٌ».] The nominative, as mubtadaʾ, is better; and «لا» may be made in the sense of ليس. As for «وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ», it can only be by the inception [i.e. nominative as mubtadaʾ], because «لا» does not govern a definite noun.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: «وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَكُمْ»: al-Akhfash said: i.e. "and remember when We took your covenant". «وَرَفَعْنا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا ما آتَيْناكُمْ», i.e. "and We said: Take what We have given you".

nahhas-irab:64-64.t:
«فَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ»: [فضل] is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; according to him it is not permissible to make it overt, because the Arabs have dispensed with making it overt: when they want that, they bring أنّ, and when they bring it they do not omit the khabar. The implied sense is "were it not that the grace of Allah overtook you". «وَرَحْمَتُهُ» is conjoined to فضل.
«لَكُنْتُمْ» is the answer of لولا. «مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ» is the khabar of كنتم.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: «وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ»: [الذين] is in the position of the accusative, and no second object is needed when علمتم is in the sense of "you knew (recognised)". Al-Akhfash reported: لقد علمتُ زيدا ولم أكن أعلمه ("I have come to know Zayd, though I did not know him before"). «اعْتَدَوْا مِنْكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ» is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. «فَقُلْنا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً»: [قردة] is the khabar (predicate) of كان. «خاسِئِينَ» is a naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: «فَجَعَلْناها نَكالًا»: [نكالا] is the second object. «لِما بَيْنَ»: [بين] is an adverbial (ẓarf). «وَما خَلْفَها» is conjoined. «وَمَوْعِظَةً» is conjoined to «نكالا». «لِلْمُتَّقِينَ» is genitive through the lām.

nahhas-irab:186-186.t:
(فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ): the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. (أُجِيبُ) is a second khabar; Sībawayh related «هذا حلو حامض» ("this is sweet and sour"). It may also be a naʿt (adjective), or resumptive. (فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا): a lām of command, and likewise (وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا). The lām of command makes [the verb] jussive because it makes the verb future and nothing else, so it resembles the conditional إن; it has also been said:
because it occurs only with verbs.

nahhas-irab:187-187.t:
(أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيامِ الرَّفَثُ): the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). Abū Isḥāq said:
«الرفث» is a word comprising everything a man desires from a woman. (هُنَّ لِباسٌ لَكُمْ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the nūn of هنّ is doubled because it corresponds to the mīm and wāw in the masculine. (عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ): أن takes fatḥa because of علم. (فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ): we have mentioned it; it is a permission. (وَابْتَغُوا ما كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ) is conjoined to it, and likewise (وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا). (فَلا تَقْرَبُوها): jussive by the prohibition; what is said about «لا» is like what is said about the lām of command.
Al-Kisāʾī said: "do not approach them in any approaching."

nahhas-irab:188-188.t:
(وَلا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْباطِلِ وَتُدْلُوا) is conjoined to تأكلوا; in the reading of Ubayy: "ولا تدلوا". ولا تدلوا [Translator's note: so in the source; the point concerns وَتُدْلُوا] may also be the answer to the prohibition with the wāw [i.e. accusative after the wāw of accompaniment], as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 37-
لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله ... عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم
(Do not forbid a trait while doing the like of it yourself; if you do, it is a great disgrace upon you.)
(بِها): the hāʾ refers to the wealth, i.e. "you bribe with it" or "you dispute on account of it", so it is as if you had let it down [as a bucket into a well]. The hāʾ may also refer to the argument, even though it has not been mentioned, as one says أدلى بحجته ("he put forward his argument"). «أموالكم» is a construct of the genus, i.e. "the wealth that belongs to you."

nahhas-irab:189-189.t:
(يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ): if you lighten the hamza, you cast its vowel onto the sīn and drop it, saying يسلونك. أهلّة is the plural of هلال for both the lower and higher numbers; in the higher numbers one ought to say
هلل, but they found that heavy, just as they found it heavy in the weak words كساء and رداء. (قُلْ هِيَ مَواقِيتُ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The singular is ميقات; the wāw changed into yāʾ because what precedes it has kasra and it is vowelless. مواقيت is a diptote according to the Basrans because it is a plural that cannot itself be pluralised and has no parallel among singulars; al-Farrāʾ said it is a diptote because it is the utmost [form] of plural. (لِلنَّاسِ): genitive by the lām. (وَالْحَجِّ) is conjoined to it. This [الحَجّ] is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; the people of Najd say الحجّ with kasra on the ḥāʾ. The fatḥa is for the maṣdar (verbal noun) and the kasra for the noun. الحجّة with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ is a single occurrence, and الحجّة [Translator's note: i.e. الحِجّة with kasra] is the work of a year; from it comes ذو الحجّة. A year is also called حجّة, as Zuhayr said: [al-Ṭawīl] 38-
وقفت بها من بعد عشرين حجّة ... فلأيا عرفت الدّار بعد توهّم
(I stopped there after twenty years, and only with difficulty did I recognise the abode, after much guessing.)
(وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ): البرّ may not be accusative, because the bāʾ enters only on the khabar. One says بيوت with kasra [Translator's note: i.e. بِيُوت], and it is a poor dialectal form because it contradicts the rule; it is permissible on the basis that ḍamma is replaced by kasra because of its adjacency to the yāʾ. (وَلكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقى): Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned it; the implied form is "whoever guards against what has been forbidden."

nahhas-irab:190-190.t: (وَلا تَعْتَدُوا): do not kill those whom you have not been commanded to kill; included in the command regarding this are women and children, and killing two for one. One says اعتدى when someone exceeds what is due. (وَالْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:191-191.t:
(وَلا تُقاتِلُوهُمْ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ): a prohibition, and it is abrogated. The Kufans read "ولا تقتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام حتّى يقتلوكم فيه",
according to the Arabs' saying قتلنا بني فلان ("we killed the tribe of so-and-so") when they killed some of them; this is not permissible unless the meaning is known. It is related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: this reading should not be read, because whoever reads it must take the meaning to be "do not kill them and do not fight them until they kill some of you."

nahhas-irab:193-193.t: (فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا فَلا عُدْوانَ إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ): al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: the meaning is "if some of them desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers among them." It has also been said: فإن انتهوا refers to the whole group.

nahhas-irab:194-194.t: (الشَّهْرُ الْحَرامُ بِالشَّهْرِ الْحَرامِ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the implied form is "fighting in the sacred month for fighting in the sacred month." (وَالْحُرُماتُ قِصاصٌ): fatḥa on the rāʾ and making it vowelless are also permissible [Translator's note: i.e. الحُرَمات and الحُرْمات].

nahhas-irab:195-195.t: (وَلا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ): the original is بأيديكم [Translator's note: i.e. بأيدِيِكم, with a vowel on the yāʾ]; the vowel on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless. Al-Akhfash said: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); Abū al-ʿAbbās holds that it is attached to the maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:196-196.t:
(وَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ فَإِنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ وَلا تَحْلِقُوا رُؤُسَكُمْ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْهَدْيُ مَحِلَّهُ فَمَنْ كانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضاً أَوْ بِهِ أَذىً مِنْ رَأْسِهِ فَفِدْيَةٌ مِنْ صِيامٍ أَوْ صَدَقَةٍ أَوْ نُسُكٍ فَإِذا أَمِنْتُمْ فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذا رَجَعْتُمْ تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كامِلَةٌ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ) (196). (وَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ): العمرة is conjoined to الحجّ. The reading of al-Shaʿbī, (وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ) [Translator's note: his reading is وَالْعُمْرَةُ in the nominative; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading], is irregular and far-fetched, because the case of العمرة must be like the case of الحج — that is the rule for a conjoined element. If it is said that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), there would be no benefit in that, because the ʿumra has always been for Allah, Mighty and Majestic; moreover it takes the ʿumra out of the [command to] complete. Whoever argued for the nominative said: if you put it in the accusative, the ʿumra must be obligatory. Abū Jaʿfar said: this argument is a mistake, because no obligation is established by this; the obligation is only ﴿وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 97]. If someone said "Complete the obligatory and the voluntary prayer", it would not follow from this that the voluntary prayer is obligatory; the meaning is only "when you have entered upon the obligatory or voluntary prayer, complete it." (فَإِنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ): Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said:
the singular of الهدي is هدية; al-Farrāʾ said: it has no singular. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: one also says هديّ, and others related that it is the dialect of Banū Tamīm. Zuhayr said: [al-Wāfir] 39-
فلم أر معشرا أسروا هديّا ... ولم أر جار بيت يستباء
(I have never seen a group take captive one under protection, nor seen a neighbour of a house taken as plunder.)
Al-Akhfash said: the implied form is "then upon him is whatever is easy of sacrificial animals." (فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ), i.e. "then upon him is a fast of three days." The hāʾ is kept in ثلاثة to distinguish masculine from feminine. It has been said: the masculine was more entitled to the hāʾ because the hāʾ enters masculine words in the lower-number plural, as in قردة; this is the view of the Kufans. Some Basrans said: the masculine was more entitled to the hāʾ because its femininity [as a plural] is not real, so it was made feminine in wording, while the feminine's femininity is real, so it was made feminine by meaning and by form, because that is more emphatic. Some of them said: the feminine marker fell on the masculine because it means "a group". (تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كامِلَةٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate); تيك is a dialectal form. (ذلِكَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ): the original is حاضرين; the nūn was dropped because of the genitive construct, and the yāʾ is dropped from pronunciation in connected speech because it is vowelless and the lām after it is vowelless.

nahhas-irab:197-197.t:
(الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُوماتٌ فَمَنْ فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ الْحَجَّ فَلا رَفَثَ وَلا فُسُوقَ وَلا جِدالَ فِي الْحَجِّ وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَتَزَوَّدُوا فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوى وَاتَّقُونِ يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ) (197). (الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُوماتٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the implied form is "the months of the Ḥajj are known months." «الحجّ أشهرا» is also permissible as an adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. "in months." Al-Farrāʾ held that the accusative is not permissible, his reason being that أشهرا is an indefinite noun not delimited, and that is not the way of adverbials. Likewise, according to him: المسلمون جانب والكفار جانب ("the Muslims are one side and the disbelievers one side"), but if you say "the side of their land" or "the side of their country", the accusative is the right way. (فَمَنْ فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ الْحَجَّ): «من» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and it is conditional; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is construed according to the meaning, i.e. "let there be no obscenity in it". (فَلا رَفَثَ وَلا فُسُوقَ وَلا جِدالَ فِي الْحَجِّ) is by way of total negation (al-tabriya) [i.e. the lā of generic negation]. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read (فَلا رَفَثَ وَلا فُسُوقَ وَلا جِدالَ فِي الْحَجِّ) [Translator's note: his reading is فَلا رَفَثٌ وَلا فُسُوقٌ with tanwīn in the nominative, as the following explanation shows; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading], making «لا» mean «ليس»; or, if you like, you may put them in the nominative as mubtadaʾ. Abū ʿAmr said: the meaning is "let there be no obscenity in it", except that he read [وَلا جِدالَ] in the accusative (وَلا جِدالَ فِي الْحَجِّ) and cut it off from what precedes, because its meaning according to him is that doubt has been removed as to the Ḥajj being in Dhū al-Ḥijja. «فلا رفث ولا فسوق» [Translator's note: i.e. فلا رفثَ ولا فسوقٌ] is also permissible, conjoining it to the position, and the grammarians recited: [al-Sarīʿ] 40-
لا نسب اليوم ولا خلّة ... اتّسع الخرق على الرّاقع
(No kinship today and no friendship; the tear has grown too wide for the mender.)
In ordinary speech one may say فلا رفث ولا فسوقا ولا جدالا في الحج, conjoining according to the wording, according to what would be required with «لا». Al-Farrāʾ said: similar to it is: [al-Ṭawīl] 41-
فلا أب وابنا مثل مروان وابنه ... إذا هو بالمجد ارتدى وتأزّرا
(There is no father and son like Marwān and his son, when he clothes himself in glory as cloak and waist-wrapper.)
(وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ): a condition and its apodosis. (وَتَزَوَّدُوا) is an imperative, and it is a permission.
(وَاتَّقُونِ) is an imperative, and that is why the nūn has been dropped from it. (يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ) is a vocative in a genitive construct. The singular of الألباب is لبّ; the لبّ of everything is its pure essence, and that is why the intellect is called لبّ. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said to me: "Do you know anything in the speech of the Arabs among the doubled verbs that comes on the pattern فَعُلَ?" I said: "Yes; Sībawayh related from Yūnus لببت تلب" [Translator's note: i.e. لَبُبْتَ تَلُبّ]. He found it good and said: "I know no parallel to it."

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: «وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ»: إنّ has kasra because it comes after القول ("saying"). It is reported from Abū ʿAmr [that he read] «يَأْمُرْكُمْ», dropping the ḍamma from the rāʾ because of its heaviness. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «يَأْمُرُكُمْ» for the variant.] Abū al-ʿAbbās said: this is not permissible, because the rāʾ is the letter carrying the case-ending; what is sound from Abū ʿAmr is that he used to slur (yakhtalis) the vowel. «أَنْ تَذْبَحُوا» is in the position of the accusative by يأمركم, i.e. "to slaughter" (بأن تذبحوا). «بَقَرَةً» is accusative by تذبحوا. «قالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنا هُزُواً»: two objects. It is permissible to lighten the hamza, making it between wāw and hamza, and it is permissible to drop the ḍamma from the zāy, as you drop it from عَضُد, and say «هُزْءًا», as the people of Kufa read. [Translator's note: the source prints «هُزُواً» for the quiescent variant.] As for جزء, it is not like هزء, because it is on the pattern fuʿl originally. «قالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ»: the dialect of Tamīm and Asad [uses] «عن» in the place of «أن».

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: «قالُوا ادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ»: the wāw was dropped because it is a request; the dialect of Banū ʿĀmir is «ادعِ لنا» with kasra on the ʿayn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «يُبَيِّنْ لَنا»: the nūn is assimilated into the lām, or, if you wish, you may pronounce it distinctly; when the nūn has a vowel, distinct pronunciation is preferred, as in «وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ» [al-Anʿām: 43]. «(يبيّن)» is jussive because it is the answer to the imperative. «ما هِيَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «قالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّها بَقَرَةٌ»: [بقرة] is the khabar of إنّ. «لا فارِضٌ»: al-Akhfash said: the accusative of فارض is not permissible, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of البقرة, as you say مررت برجل لا قائمٍ ولا جالسٍ ("I passed by a man neither standing nor sitting"). The implied sense may also be "she is neither فارض", and on this basis one says مررت برجل لا قائمٌ ولا جالسٌ. [Translator's note: the source gives both examples unvowelled; the second evidently intends the nominative.] «وَلا بِكْرٌ» is conjoined to فارض. «عَوانٌ» is [nominative] by implying a mubtadaʾ.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: «ما لَوْنُها» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). «ما لونَها» is also permissible, taking ما as redundant and making it accusative by يبيّن. «بَقَرَةٌ صَفْراءُ»: صفراء is a diptote because it has the alif of the feminine, which is inseparable; so it differs from the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa], since what has the hāʾ is fully declined when indefinite. «فاقِعٌ» is a naʿt (adjective). «لَوْنُها» is nominative by فاقع.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t:
«إِنَّ الْبَقَرَ تَشابَهَ عَلَيْنا»: البقر is treated as masculine because it has the meaning of a collective. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: الباقر is the plural of باقرة; he said: and بقر has the plural باقورة. Al-Ḥasan read «إنّ البقر تشّابه علينا», making it an imperfect verb and feminine, the original being تتشابه; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the shīn. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «إن الباقر يشّابه علينا», making it an imperfect verb, using الباقر as masculine, and assimilating. «إنّ البقر تَشابَهُ علينا», with the shīn light and ḍamma on the hāʾ, is permissible; but «يَشابَهُ علينا», with the shīn light and with yāʾ, is not permissible. It is permissible with tāʾ only because the original is تتشابه, and [one tāʾ] was dropped because two tāʾs came together.
«وَإِنَّا إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَمُهْتَدُونَ»: [مهتدون] is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. «شاء» is in the position of the jussive through the condition; its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), according to Sībawayh, is the clause [before it], and according to Abū al-ʿAbbās it is omitted.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t:
Al-Akhfash said: «لا ذلولٌ» is a naʿt (adjective), and its accusative is not permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied sense may be "she is not ذلول". Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read «لا ذَلُولَ تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ», which is permissible by implying the predicate of the negation. [Translator's note: the source prints «لا ذَلُولٌ» for al-Sulamī's reading; his reported reading is with fatḥa (the lā of generic negation), which the following remark about an implied predicate presupposes.] «تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ» is connected with the first [negation] on this meaning, i.e. "she does not plough the earth". «وَلا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ»: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān held that تثير cannot be resumptive, because after it comes «ولا تسقي الحرث»; if it were resumptive, wāw and «لا» would not have been combined. «مُسَلَّمَةٌ», i.e. "she is مسلّمة"; «مسلّمة» may also be a naʿt, i.e. "she is a cow sound from lameness and other defects". One does not say "free from work", because it would not be right [to call her] free from what is good for her. «لا شِيَةَ فِيها»: the original is وِشْيَة; the wāw was dropped as it was dropped from يَشِي, whose original is يَوْشِي.
«قالُوا الْآنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ»: there are four ways in it. With hamza, as the Kufans read «قالُوا الْآنَ»; and lightening the hamza with the wāw dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as the people of Medina read «قالُ لَانَ». Al-Akhfash reported two other ways. One of them is keeping the wāw while lightening the hamza: «قالوا لَانَ جئت بالحقّ» — he kept the wāw because the lām had taken the vowel of the hamza. The counterpart of this is «وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عاداً لُّولى» [al-Najm: 50] in the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr. [Translator's note: the source prints «قالُوا الْآنَ» and «عادا لولا» without the variant vowelling; the bracketed vowelling of the Medinan reading is the translator's. The source spells «الأولى» as «لولا».] Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd say:
I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I do not know that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ committed a solecism (laḥn) in pure Arabic except in two words: one is «عادا لولى» and the other is «يُؤَدِّهْ إِلَيْكَ» [Āl ʿImrān: 75]. It became a solecism only because he assimilated one letter into another, making the first quiescent, while the rule for the second is quiescence and its vowel is only incidental; so it is as if he combined two quiescent letters. Al-Akhfash [also] reported «قالُوا أَلْآنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ», giving a disjunctive hamza to the first alif, which is a connecting alif, as one says يا ألله.
Abū Isḥāq said: الآن is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, though it has alif-lām, because the alif-lām entered it without [reference to something previously] known (ʿahd). You say "I was here until الآن", the meaning being "until this time"; so it was made indeclinable as هذا was made indeclinable, and the nūn was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
«فَذَبَحُوها»: the hāʾ and alif are accusative by the verb; the noun is the hāʾ, and the alif is not dropped because of its lightness and to distinguish between masculine and feminine. «وَما كادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ» is an imperfect verb. Sībawayh permitted كاد أن يفعل, by analogy with عسى.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: «وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْساً»: «إذ» is an adverbial (ẓarf) conjoined to what precedes it. «فَادَّارَأْتُمْ»: the original is تدارأتم; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl, and since one cannot begin with an assimilated letter, because it is quiescent, you added the connecting alif. «وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ ما كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ»: «ما» is in the position of the accusative by مخرج; dropping the tanwīn [مخرجُ ما] by the construct is also permissible.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t:
«كَذلِكَ يُحْيِ اللَّهُ الْمَوْتى»:
the position of the kāf is accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). It is not permissible to assimilate the yāʾ into the yāʾ in «يحيي», so that two quiescent letters do not meet.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t:
«ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ»: you say قسا; when you add the tāʾ you drop the alif because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
«قُلُوبُكُمْ» is nominative by قست. «فَهِيَ كَالْحِجارَةِ»: the kāf is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of هي. «أَوْ أَشَدُّ» is conjoined to the kāf; and it is permissible [to read] «أشدَّ قسوةً», conjoining it to الحجارة. «قَسْوَةً» is as specification (bayān).
«وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحِجارَةِ لَما يَتَفَجَّرُ»: «ما» is in the position of the accusative because it is the noun (ism) of إنّ, and the lām is for emphasis. «منه» is according to the wording of «ما»; in the reading of Ubayy it is «منها», according to the meaning. Abū Ḥātim said: «لما تتفجّر منه الأنهار» is permissible, but «لما تشّقّق» is not, because when he says تتفجّر he makes it feminine by the femininity of الأنهار, and that cannot be in تشّقّق. Abū Jaʿfar said: what he rejected is permissible, construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "and of them there are stones that split". As for يشّقّق with yāʾ, it is construed according to the wording of «ما». Al-Kisāʾī says: it is masculine by the masculinity of البعض ("some"); and similar, in his view, is «نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ» [al-Naḥl: 66], i.e. "of what is in the bellies of some of it".
«وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغافِلٍ»: [غافل] is in the position of the accusative in the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and the bāʾ is for emphasis.
«عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ», i.e. "of your doing"; it needs no resumptive pronoun, unless you make it in the sense of الذي, in which case you omit the resumptive pronoun because of the length of the noun, i.e. "of that which you do (تعملونه)".

nahhas-irab:198-198.t:
(لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُناحٌ): the noun of ليس. (أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا) is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "in that you seek"; according to al-Kisāʾī and al-Khalīl it is in the position of the genitive. (فَإِذا أَفَضْتُمْ مِنْ عَرَفاتٍ) with tanwīn; likewise if you named a woman مسلمات, because the tanwīn [here] is not what distinguishes triptotes from diptotes such that you would drop it; it is only like the nūn in مسلمين. This is the good [usage]. Sībawayh related from the Arabs the dropping of the tanwīn: (من عرفاتِ يا هذا) and رأيت عرفاتِ يا هذا, with kasra on the tāʾ and without tanwīn.
He said: when they made it definite, they dropped the tanwīn. Al-Akhfash and the Kufans related fatḥa on the tāʾ. Al-Akhfash said: it is treated like the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa], so one says من عرفاتَ يا هذا. They recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 42-
تنوّرتها من أذرعات وأهلها ... بيثرب أدنى دارها نظر عالي
(I looked towards her fire from Adhriʿāt, while her people were at Yathrib; the nearest of her abode is a lofty gaze away.)
(فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ عِنْدَ الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرامِ): مشعر is مَفْعَل from شعرت به, i.e. "I came to know of it", i.e. a landmark among the places of worship of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. It ought to have been on the pattern مَفْعُل, built on يشعر, except that there is no noun on the pattern مَفْعُل in the speech of the Arabs. (وَاذْكُرُوهُ كَما هَداكُمْ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "a remembrance like His guiding you", i.e. as a recompense for His guiding you. (وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الضَّالِّينَ): a lām of emphasis, except that it is obligatory so that إن is not taken to mean ما.

nahhas-irab:200-200.t: (فَإِذا قَضَيْتُمْ مَناسِكَكُمْ) with distinct pronunciation (iẓhār), because the second [kāf] is as if separate; (مناسكّم) with assimilation is also permissible. ﴿أَيْنَما تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 78] can only be assimilated [Translator's note: so in the source]. (فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَذِكْرِكُمْ آباءَكُمْ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "a remembrance like your remembrance"; it may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْراً): «أشدّ» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ذكركم, the meaning being "or (like a more intense remembrance)". It is a diptote because it is an adjective on the pattern أفعل. It may also be in the position of the accusative, meaning "or remember Him with a more intense remembrance". (ذِكْراً) is by way of clarification [i.e. tamyīz]. (فَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or, if you like, by the adjectival phrase. (يَقُولُ رَبَّنا آتِنا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. (وَما لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلاقٍ): من is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:201-201.t: The original of (قِنا) is أوقنا [Translator's note: i.e. اِوْقِنا]; the wāw was dropped as it was dropped in يقي, and it was dropped from يقي because it lies between a yāʾ and a kasra, as in يعد. This is the view of the Basrans. The Kufans said: it was dropped to distinguish the intransitive from the transitive. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is a mistake, because the Arabs say ورم يرم, dropping the wāw.

nahhas-irab:203-203.t:
(وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ فِي أَيَّامٍ مَعْدُوداتٍ): the Kufans said: the alif and tāʾ [i.e. the sound feminine plural] are for the lower numbers; the Basrans said: they are for both few and many. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned "the numbered [days]" and "the known [days]" and the scholars' views on them, and we will explain that here. The soundest thing said about the numbered days is that they are three days after the Day of Sacrifice. It has been said that the numbered and the known days are the same; this is a mistake, because of His saying, Majestic and Mighty:
«فمن تعجّل في يومين» ("whoever hastens in two days"); the implied form in Arabic is "whoever hastens in two days of them", and the meaning is "in numbered days, for the remembrance of Allah the Exalted." The soundest thing said about the known days is the view of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him, which is the doctrine of the people of Medina: they are the Day of Sacrifice and the two days after it, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
﴿وَيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ فِي أَيَّامٍ مَعْلُوماتٍ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 28], so these can only be the days on which sacrifice is made. The Day of Sacrifice must be either the first of them, the middle, or the last; if it were the last or the middle, the sacrifice would be before it, which is impossible, so it must be the first. (فَمَنْ تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ): «من» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (فَلا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ). Outside the Qur'an فلا إثم عليهم is permissible, because the meaning of «من» is a group, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ [Yūnus: 42]. Likewise (وَمَنْ تَأَخَّرَ فَلا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ). (لِمَنِ اتَّقى): it may be asked: to what is the lām attached? The answer — and there are several answers: the implied form may be "forgiveness is for whoever is mindful [of Allah]", and this is according to Ibn Masʿūd's interpretation. Al-Akhfash said:
the implied form is "that is for whoever is mindful." It has been said that the implied form is "safety is for whoever is mindful." It has also been said: واذكروا indicates remembrance, so the meaning is "the remembrance is for whoever is mindful."

nahhas-irab:204-204.t: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): it has been said that «من» here is specific. Al-Ḥasan said: the liar; it has also been said: the wrongdoer; and it has been said: the hypocrite. Ibn Muḥayṣin read (وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلى ما فِي قَلْبِهِ) with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. وَيَشْهَدُ اللَّهُ; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading]. (وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ الْخِصامِ): the verb from it is لددت تلدّ [Translator's note: the source has "الفعل مثل منه", evidently a slip]. According to Abū Isḥāq, خصام is the plural of خصم; others said: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of خاصم.

nahhas-irab:205-205.t: (وَإِذا تَوَلَّى سَعى فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيها): accusative by the lām of kay (purpose). (وَيُهْلِكَ الْحَرْثَ وَالنَّسْلَ) is conjoined to it. In the reading of Ubayy: "وليهلك الحرث". Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read ويهلك in the nominative [i.e. وَيُهْلِكُ], and there are several views on its nominative: it may be conjoined to يعجبك. Abū Ḥātim said: it is conjoined to سعى, because its meaning is "he strives and destroys." Abū Isḥāq said: the implied form is "he destroys", i.e. this is decreed [Translator's note: so in the source, "أي يقدر هذا"]. It is related from Ibn Kathīr that he read "ويهلك الحرث والنسل" with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the kāf [Translator's note: i.e. وَيَهْلِكُ], with الحرث and النسل nominative by يهلك.

nahhas-irab:207-207.t: (ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِ اللَّهِ): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

nahhas-irab:208-208.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا فِي السِّلْمِ كَافَّةً): [Translator's note: the source has "في الكسائي", evidently for "قال الكسائي"] al-Kisāʾī [said]: السّلم and السّلم are one [Translator's note: i.e. السِّلْم and السَّلْم], and so it is according to most Basrans, except that Abū ʿAmr distinguished between them. Here he read (ادخلوا في السّلم) [i.e. السِّلْم] and said: it means Islam; and he read the one in «al-Anfāl» and the one in «Sūrat Muḥammad», may Allah bless him and grant him peace, «السّلم» with fatḥa on the sīn, and said: with fatḥa it is peace-making. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī said: «السِّلم» is Islam, «السَّلم» is truce, and السَّلَم is surrender [Translator's note: the vowelling of the three forms is not marked in the source and is supplied according to the usual distinction]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd rejects these distinctions, which are frequent from Abū ʿAmr; language is not taken in this way but only by hearing, not by analogy, and whoever makes a distinction needs evidence. The Basrans related بنو فلان سلم وسلم ("the tribe of so-and-so are at peace") with one meaning. And even if the distinction were sound, the meaning would be the same, because whoever enters Islam has entered into peace. الصلح and السلم are feminine, and may be masculine. (كَافَّةً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is derived from their saying كففت, i.e. "I held back", i.e. none of you is to hold back; from it come مكفوف (blind) and كفّة الميزان (the scale-pan), and it has been said that the palm is called كفّ because one holds things back with it. (وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا) is a prohibition. (خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ) is an object; we have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:209-209.t: (فَإِنْ زَلَلْتُمْ): the maṣdar is زلّ, زلل and مزلّة [Translator's note: the source has "زلا وزللا ومزلّة" in the accusative], and زلّ في الطين زليلا ("he slipped in the mud, a slipping").

nahhas-irab:210-210.t:
Qatāda and Abū Jaʿfar Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read "في ظلال من الغمام" [Translator's note: the context indicates their reading is فِي ظُلَلٍ … and the variant concerns ظلال; the source is not explicit], and Abū Jaʿfar read (وَالْمَلائِكَةُ) in the genitive [Translator's note: i.e. وَالْمَلائِكَةِ; the printed vocalisation shows the nominative]. ظلل is the broken plural of ظلّة, and in the sound plural ظللات. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 43-
إذا الوحش ضمّ الوحش في ظللاتها ... سواقط من حرّ وقد كان أظهرا
(When the wild beasts gathered the wild beasts in their shades, fallen from the heat, it having already reached noon.)
ظللات and ظلّات are also permissible. ظلال is the plural of ظلّ for the higher numbers, and for the lower numbers أظلال; ظلال may also be the plural of ظلّة. It has been said: rather the lower number is أظلال and the higher ظلال. It has also been said: ظلال is the plural of ظلّة, like قلّة and قلال, as [the poet] said: [al-Khafīf] 44-
ممزوجة بماءه القلال
(mixed with the water of the jars)
Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: (وَالْمَلائِكَةُ) in the genitive means "and among the angels"; he said: the nominative is better, as He said ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 158] and ﴿وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا﴾ [al-Fajr: 22]. Al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "هل ينظرون إلّا أن يأتيهم الله والملائكة في ظلل من الغمام". Abū Isḥāq said: the implied form is "in canopies of cloud and of angels."

nahhas-irab:211-211.t:
(سَلْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) with lightening of the hamza; since the sīn took a vowel, there was no need for the connecting alif.
(كَمْ) is in the position of the accusative because it is the second object of آتيناهم; it may also be in the position of the nominative with an implied resumptive pronoun. It does not take case endings although it is a noun, because it is like the particles, since the meaning of interrogation is in it. Sībawayh said: so it is as far removed from resemblance [to the verb] as «كم» and «إذ» are from the fully declinable nouns. (مِنْ آيَةٍ): when you separate كم from the noun, the preferred choice is to bring من; if you drop it, you use the accusative in both interrogative and declarative [كم], and the genitive is permissible in the declarative, as [the poet] said: [al-Ramal] 45-
كم بجود مقرف نال العلى ... وكريم بخله قد وضعه
(How many a man of base descent has attained eminence through generosity, and how many a noble man has his stinginess brought low!)

nahhas-irab:212-212.t: (زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا): the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). Mujāhid and Ḥumayd ibn Qays read (زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا) [Translator's note: their reading is زَيَّنَ … الْحَياةَ, active voice, as the following explanation shows; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading], and it is an irregular reading, because no agent has been mentioned before. (وَالَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (فَوْقَهُمْ): an adverbial (ẓarf) in the position of the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:213-213.t: (كانَ النَّاسُ): the noun of كان. (أُمَّةً): its khabar (predicate). (واحِدَةً): a naʿt (adjective). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the view of the exegetes on the meaning. The implied form in Arabic is "mankind was one community, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets"; this omission is indicated by (وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ), i.e. mankind was upon the religion of truth, then they differed. (فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ), i.e. "giving good tidings" to whoever obeys and "warning" whoever disobeys; both are accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الْكِتابَ): الكتاب in the sense of "the books". (لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ): accusative by an implied أن; it is figurative, like ﴿هذا كِتابُنا يَنْطِقُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 29]. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read (لِيَحْكُمَ) [Translator's note: his reading is لِيُحْكَمَ, passive; the printed vocalisation is the standard reading], which is irregular, because the Book has already been mentioned. (وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ): the position of الذين is nominative by their verb, and those who differed about it are the ones addressed. (فَهَدَى اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الْحَقِّ): Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the view of the exegetes on it; sometimes we repeat something already given in order to explain it further or to choose a view from it. One of the best things said about it is that the meaning is: Allah guided those who believed by making clear to them the truth regarding what those before them differed about. As for the ḥadīth «concerning Friday, they are followers of us», its meaning is that they must follow us, because this Law abrogates their laws. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of بإذنه is "by His knowledge". Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake; that [sense] belongs to الأذن [Translator's note: i.e. الأَذَن, "knowledge"]; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is "by His command", for when you give permission for something, it is as though you have commanded it, i.e. Allah guided those who believed by commanding them what they must put into practice.

nahhas-irab:214-214.t:
(أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ): (أَنْ) stands in place of the two objects. (وَلَمَّا يَأْتِكُمْ): the yāʾ has been dropped because of the jussive. (وَزُلْزِلُوا حَتَّى يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ): this [i.e. يَقُولُ in the nominative] is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries [Translator's note: the printed vocalisation shows the accusative, which is the other reading]. The people of Kufa, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū ʿAmr read (حَتَّى يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ) in the accusative, and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He has two arguments for that. One is from Abū ʿAmr, who said: «زلزلوا» is a past verb and «يقول» an imperfect [lit. future] verb, so since they differ, the accusative is the right way. The other argument he related from al-Kisāʾī, who said: when the past verb is prolonged, it becomes like the future. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the first argument, that «زلزلوا» is past and «يقول» future, it contains no reason for either the nominative or the accusative, because حتّى is not one of the particles that conjoin verbs, nor is it in any way one of the governors of verbs. So al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said, concerning their putting what follows it in the accusative by an implied «أن»: they dropped أن only because they knew that حتى is one of the governors of nouns — this is the sense of what the two said. So this argument is as it were a mistake; it is used only in the chapter on the fāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī's argument, that a verb when prolonged becomes like the future, is no argument at all, because he did not mention the reason for the accusative; and if the first verb were future, the question would remain as it is. Sībawayh's doctrine regarding «حتّى» is that the accusative after it is on two grounds and the nominative on two grounds. You say:
سرت حتّى أدخلها ("I travelled until I entered it"), meaning that the travelling and the entering have both passed, i.e. "I travelled up to my entering it."
This is [حتى of] limit, and the reading of those who read the accusative is according to it. The other ground for the accusative, outside the verse, is سرت حتى أدخلها, i.e. "so that I might enter it." The two grounds for the nominative: سرت حتّى أدخلها [Translator's note: the source has أدخلهما, evidently a slip], i.e. "I travelled and so I enter it", both having passed, i.e. "I had travelled, and so I entered." Here حتّى does not govern by an implied أن, because a [complete] clause follows it, as al-Farazdaq said: [al-Ṭawīl] 46-
فيا عجبا حتّى كليب تسبّني ... كأنّ أباها نهشل أو مجاشع
(How amazing! Even Kulayb insults me, as though its father were Nahshal or Mujāshiʿ!)
On this basis is the reading with the nominative, which is clearer and sounder in meaning, i.e. "and they were shaken until the Messenger says", i.e. until this was his state, because the saying arose from the shaking and was not cut off from it, whereas the accusative of limit does not have this meaning. The other ground for the nominative, outside the verse, is سرت حتى أدخلها with the travelling having passed and the entering happening now. Sībawayh related مرض حتّى ما يرجونه ("he fell ill until they now have no hope for him"), and similar to it is
سرت حتّى أدخلها لا أمنع ("I travelled until I enter it, not being prevented"). (مَتى نَصْرُ اللَّهِ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh, and according to Abū al-ʿAbbās nominative by its verb, i.e. "when will Allah's help occur?" (أَلا إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ): the noun of إنّ and its khabar (predicate). Outside the Qur'an إن نصر الله قريبا is permissible, i.e. "in a near place." In this sense the Arabs do not make قريب dual, plural or feminine; He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 56], and the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 47-
له الويل إن أمسى ولا أمّ هاشم ... قريب ولا بسباسة ابنة يشكرا
(Woe to him if he comes to evening with neither Umm Hāshim near nor Basbāsa, daughter of Yashkur!)
But if you say فلان قريب ("so-and-so is a relative"), you make it dual and plural, saying قريبون and أقرباء or قرباء.
